flowers, which was surrounded by humming bumblebees searching for honey.
Then, expecting to get a place on the bosom of the Lord, she remained
standing by His side, her face smiling in shyness.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is the father of the
sanskrit:
three worlds, and His bosom is the residence of mother Lakñmé, the
goddess of fortune, the proprietor of all opulences. The goddess of
fortune, by her favorable and merciful glance, can increase the opulence
of the three worlds, along with their inhabitants and their directors,
the demigods.

text: The inhabitants of Gandharvaloka and Cäraëaloka then took
sanskrit:
the opportunity to play their musical instruments, such as conchshells,
bugles and drums. They began dancing and singing along with their wives.

text: Lord Brahmä, Lord Çiva, the great sage Aìgirä, and
sanskrit:
similar directors of universal management showered flowers and chanted
mantras indicating the transcendental glories of the Supreme Personality
of Godhead.

text: All the demigods, along with the prajäpatis and their
sanskrit:
descendants, being blessed by Lakñméjé's glance upon them, were
immediately enriched with good behavior and transcendental qualities.
Thus they were very much satisfied.

text: O King, because of being neglected by the goddess of
sanskrit:
fortune, the demons and Räkñasas were depressed, bewildered and
frustrated, and thus they became shameless.

text: Next appeared Väruëé, the lotus-eyed goddess who controls
sanskrit:
drunkards. With the permission of the Supreme Personality of Godhead,
Kåñëa, the demons, headed by Bali Mahäräja, took possession of this
young girl.

text: O King, thereafter, while the sons of Kaçyapa, both demons
sanskrit:
and demigods, were engaged in churning the ocean of milk, a very
wonderful male person appeared.

text: He was strongly built; his arms were long, stout and strong;
sanskrit:
his neck, which was marked with three lines, resembled a conchshell; his
eyes were reddish; and his complexion was blackish. He was very young,
he was garlanded with flowers, and his entire body was fully decorated
with various ornaments.

text: He was dressed in yellow garments and wore brightly polished
sanskrit:
earrings made of pearls. The tips of his hair were anointed with oil,
and his chest was very broad. His body had all good features, he was
stout and strong like a lion, and he was decorated with bangles. In his
hand he carried a jug filled to the top with nectar.

text: This person was Dhanvantari, a plenary portion of a plenary
sanskrit:
portion of Lord Viñëu. He was very conversant with the science of
medicine, and as one of the demigods he was permitted to take a share in
sacrifices.

text: Upon seeing Dhanvantari carrying the jug of nectar, the
sanskrit:
demons, desiring the jug and its contents, immediately snatched it away
by force.

text: When the jug of nectar was carried off by the demons, the
sanskrit:
demigods were morose. Thus they sought shelter at the lotus feet of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari.

text: When the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who always desires
sanskrit:
to fulfill the ambitions of His devotees, saw that the demigods were
morose, He said to them, "Do not be aggrieved. By My own energy I shall
bewilder the demons by creating a quarrel among them. In this way I
shall fulfill your desire to have the nectar."

text: O King, a quarrel then arose among the demons over who would
sanskrit:
get the nectar first. Each of them said, "You cannot drink it first. I
must drink it first. Me first, not you!"

text: Some of the demons said, "All the demigods have taken
sanskrit:
part in churning the ocean of milk. Now, as everyone has an equal right
to partake in any public sacrifice, according to the eternal religious
system it is befitting that the demigods now have a share of the
nectar." O King, in this way the weaker demons forbade the stronger
demons to take the nectar.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viñëu, who can
sanskrit:
counteract any unfavorable situation, then assumed the form of an
extremely beautiful woman. This incarnation as a woman, Mohiné-mürti,
was most pleasing to the mind. Her complexion resembled in color a newly
grown blackish lotus, and every part of Her body was beautifully
situated. Her ears were equally decorated with earrings, Her cheeks were
very beautiful, Her nose was raised and Her face full of youthful
luster. Her large breasts made Her waist seem very thin. Attracted by
the aroma of Her face and body, bumblebees hummed around Her, and thus
Her eyes were restless. Her hair, which was extremely beautiful, was
garlanded with mallikä flowers. Her attractively constructed neck was
decorated with a necklace and other ornaments, Her arms were decorated
with bangles, Her body was covered with a clean sari, and Her breasts
seemed like islands in an ocean of beauty. Her legs were decorated with
ankle bells. Because of the movements of Her eyebrows as She smiled with
shyness and glanced o

text: O King Parékñit, great sages who were completely aware of
sanskrit:
the Vedic ritualistic ceremonies took charge of that surabhi cow, which
produced all the yogurt, milk and ghee absolutely necessary for offering
oblations into the fire. They did this just for the sake of pure ghee,
which they wanted for the performance of sacrifices to elevate
themselves to the higher planetary systems, up to Brahmaloka.

text: Thereafter, a horse named Uccaiùçravä, which was as white
sanskrit:
as the moon, was generated. Bali Mahäräja desired to possess this
horse, and Indra, the King of heaven, did not protest, for he had
previously been so advised by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: As the next result of the churning, the king of elephants,
sanskrit:
named Airävata, was generated. This elephant was white, and with its
four tusks it defied the glories of Kailäsa Mountain, the glorious
abode of Lord Çiva.

text: Thereafter, O King, eight great elephants, which could go in
sanskrit:
any direction, were generated. They were headed by Airävaëa. Eight
she-elephants, headed by Abhramu, were also generated.

text: Generated thereafter from the great ocean were the celebrated
sanskrit:
gems Kaustubha-maëi and Padmaräga-maëi. Lord Viñëu, to decorate His
chest, desired to possess them. Generated next was the pärijäta
flower, which decorates the celestial planets. O King, as you fulfill
the desires of everyone on this planet by fulfilling all ambitions, the
pärijäta fulfills the desires of everyone.

text: Next there appeared the Apsaräs [who are used as prostitutes
sanskrit:
on the heavenly planets]. They were fully decorated with golden
ornaments and lockets and were dressed in fine and attractive clothing.
The Apsaräs move very slowly in an attractive style that bewilders the
inhabitants of the heavenly planets.

text: Then there appeared the goddess of fortune, Ramä, who is
sanskrit:
absolutely dedicated to being enjoyed by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead. She appeared like electricity, surpassing the lightning that
might illuminate a marble mountain.

text: Because of her exquisite beauty, her bodily features, her
sanskrit:
youth, her complexion and her glories, everyone, including the demigods,
the demons and the human beings, desired her. They were attracted
because she is the source of all opulences.

text: The King of heaven, Indra, brought a suitable sitting place
sanskrit:
for the goddess of fortune. All the rivers of sacred water, such as the
Ganges and Yamunä, personified themselves, and each of them brought
pure water in golden waterpots for mother Lakñmé, the goddess of
fortune.

text: The land became a person and collected all the drugs and
sanskrit:
herbs needed for installing the Deity. The cows delivered five products,
namely milk, yogurt, ghee, urine and cow dung, and spring personified
collected everything produced in spring, during the months of Caitra and
Vaiçäkha [April and May].

text: The great sages performed the bathing ceremony of the
sanskrit:
goddess of fortune as directed in the authorized scriptures, the
Gandharvas chanted all-auspicious Vedic mantras, and the professional
women dancers very nicely danced and sang authorized songs prescribed in
the Vedas.

text: The clouds in personified form beat various types of drums,
sanskrit:
known as mådaìgas, paëavas, murajas and änakas. They also blew
conchshells and bugles known as gomukhas and played flutes and stringed
instruments. The combined sound of these instruments was tumultuous.

text: Thereafter, the great elephants from all the directions
sanskrit:
carried big water jugs full of Ganges water and bathed the goddess of
fortune, to the accompaniment of Vedic mantras chanted by learned
brähmaëas. While thus being bathed, the goddess of fortune maintained
her original style, with a lotus flower in her hand, and she appeared
very beautiful. The goddess of fortune is the most chaste, for she does
not know anyone but the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: The ocean, which is the source of all valuable jewels,
sanskrit:
supplied the upper and lower portions of a yellow silken garment. The
predominating deity of the water, Varuëa, presented flower garlands
surrounded by six-legged bumblebees, drunken with honey.

text: Viçvakarmä, one of the prajäpatis, supplied varieties of
sanskrit:
decorated ornaments. The goddess of learning, Sarasvaté, supplied a
necklace, Lord Brahmä supplied a lotus flower, and the inhabitants of
Nägaloka supplied earrings.

text: Thereafter, mother Lakñmé, the goddess of fortune, having
sanskrit:
been properly celebrated with an auspicious ritualistic ceremony, began
moving about, holding in her hand a garland of lotus flowers, which were
surrounded by humming bumblebees. Smiling with shyness, her cheeks
decorated by her earrings, she looked extremely beautiful.

text: Her two breasts, which were symmetrical and nicely situated,
sanskrit:
were covered with sandalwood pulp and kuìkuma powder, and her waist was
very thin. As she walked here and there, her ankle bells jingling
softly, she appeared like a creeper of gold.

text: While walking among the Gandharvas, Yakñas, asuras,
sanskrit:
Siddhas, Cäraëas and denizens of heaven, Lakñmédevé, the goddess of
fortune, was scrutinizingly examining them, but she could not find
anyone naturally endowed with all good qualities. None of them was
devoid of faults, and therefore she could not take shelter of any of
them.

text: The goddess of fortune, examining the assembly, thought in
sanskrit:
this way: Someone who has undergone great austerity has not yet
conquered anger. Someone possesses knowledge, but he has not conquered
material desires. Someone is a very great personality, but he cannot
conquer lusty desires. Even a great personality depends on something
else. How, then, can he be the supreme controller?

text: Someone may possess full knowledge of religion but still not
sanskrit:
be kind to all living entities. In someone, whether human or demigod,
there may be renunciation, but that is not the cause of liberation.
Someone may possess great power and yet be unable to check the power of
eternal time. Someone else may have renounced attachment to the material
world, yet he cannot compare to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
Therefore, no one is completely freed from the influence of the material
modes of nature.

text: Someone may have longevity but not have auspiciousness or
sanskrit:
good behavior. Someone may have both auspiciousness and good behavior,
but the duration of his life is not fixed. Although such demigods as
Lord Çiva have eternal life, they have inauspicious habits like living
in crematoriums. And even if others are well qualified in all respects,
they are not devotees of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: In this way, after full
sanskrit:
deliberation, the goddess of fortune accepted Mukunda as her husband
because although He is independent and not in want of her, He possesses
all transcendental qualities and mystic powers and is therefore the most
desirable.

text: Approaching the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the goddess
sanskrit:
of fortune placed upon His shoulders the garland of newly grown lotus
flowers, which was surrounded by humming bumblebees searching for honey.
Then, expecting to get a place on the bosom of the Lord, she remained
standing by His side, her face smiling in shyness.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: Thereafter, the demons became
sanskrit:
inimical toward one another. Throwing and snatching the container of
nectar, they gave up their friendly relationship. Meanwhile, they saw a
very beautiful young woman coming forward toward them.

text: Upon seeing the beautiful woman, the demons said, "Alas, how
sanskrit:
wonderful is Her beauty, how wonderful the luster of Her body, and how
wonderful the beauty of Her youthful age!" Speaking in this way, they
quickly approached Her, full of lusty desires to enjoy Her, and began to
inquire from Her in many ways.

text: O wonderfully beautiful girl, You have such nice eyes,
sanskrit:
resembling the petals of a lotus flower. Who are You? Where do You come
from? What is Your purpose in coming here, and to whom do You belong? O
You whose thighs are extraordinarily beautiful, our minds are becoming
agitated simply because of seeing You.

text: What to speak of human beings, even the demigods, demons,
sanskrit:
Siddhas, Gandharvas, Cäraëas and the various directors of the
universe, the Prajäpatis, have never touched You before. It is not that
we are unable to understand Your identity.

text: O beautiful girl with beautiful eyebrows, certainly
sanskrit:
Providence, by His causeless mercy, has sent You to please the senses
and minds of all of us. Is this not a fact?

text: We are now all engaged in enmity among ourselves because of
sanskrit:
this one subject matter-the container of nectar. Although we have been
born in the same family, we are becoming increasingly inimical. O
thin-waisted woman, who are so beautiful in Your prestigious position,
we therefore request You to favor us by settling our dispute.

text: All of us, both demons and demigods, have been born of the
sanskrit:
same father, Kaçyapa, and thus we are related as brothers. But now we
are exhibiting our personal prowess in dissension. Therefore we request
You to settle our dispute and divide the nectar equally among us.

text: Having thus been requested by the demons, the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, who had assumed the form of a beautiful woman,
began to smile. Looking at them with attractive feminine gestures, She
spoke as follows.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the form of Mohiné,
sanskrit:
told the demons: O sons of Kaçyapa Muni, I am only a prostitute. Mow is
it that you have so much faith in Me? A learned person never puts his
faith in a woman.

text: O demons, as monkeys, jackals and dogs are unsteady in their
sanskrit:
sexual relationships and want newer and newer friends every day, women
who live independently seek new friends daily. Friendship with such a
woman is never permanent. This is the opinion of learned scholars.

text: Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: After the demons heard
sanskrit:
the words of Mohiné-mürti, who had spoken as if jokingly, they were
all very confident. They laughed with gravity, and ultimately they
delivered the container of nectar into Her hands.

text: Thereafter, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, having taken
sanskrit:
possession of the container of nectar, smiled slightly and spoke in
attractive words. She said: My dear demons, if you accept whatever I may
do, whether honest or dishonest, then I can take responsibility for
dividing the nectar among you.

text: The chiefs of the demons were not very expert in deciding
sanskrit:
things. Upon hearing the sweet words of Mohiné-mürti, they immediately
assented. "Yes," they answered. "What You have said is all right." Thus
the demons agreed to accept Her decision.

text: The demigods and demons then observed a fast. After
sanskrit:
bathing, they offered clarified butter and oblations into the fire and
gave charity to the cows and to the brähmaëas and members of the other
orders of society, namely the kñatriyas, vaiçyas and çüdras, who
were all rewarded as they deserved. Thereafter, the demigods and demons
performed ritualistic ceremonies under the directions of the
brähmaëas. Then they dressed themselves with new garments according to
their own choice, decorated their bodies with ornaments, and sat facing
east on seats made of kuça grass.

text: O King, as the demigods and demons sat facing east in an
sanskrit:
arena fully decorated with flower garlands and lamps and fragrant with
the smoke of incense, that woman, dressed in a most beautiful sari, Her
ankle bells tinkling, entered the arena, walking very slowly because of
Her big, low hips. Her eyes were restless due to youthful pride, Her
breasts were like water jugs, Her thighs resembled the trunks of
elephants, and She carried a waterpot in Her hand.

text: Her attractive nose and cheeks and Her ears, adorned with
sanskrit:
golden earrings, made Her face very beautiful. As She moved, Her sari's
border on Her breasts moved slightly aside. When the demigods and demons
saw these beautiful features of Mohiné-mürti, who was glancing at them
and slightly smiling, they were all completely enchanted.

text: Demons are by nature crooked like snakes. Therefore, to
sanskrit:
distribute a share of the nectar to them was not at all feasible, since
this would be as dangerous as supplying milk to a snake. Considering
this, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who never falls down, did not
deliver a share of nectar to the demons.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead as Mohiné-mürti, the
sanskrit:
master of the universe, arranged separate lines of sitting places and
seated the demigods and demons according to their positions.

text: Taking the container of nectar in Her hands, She first
sanskrit:
approached the demons, satisfied them with sweet words and thus cheated
them of their share of the nectar. Then She administered the nectar to
the demigods, who were sitting at a distant place, to make them free
from invalidity, old age and death.

text: O King, since the demons had promised to accept whatever the
sanskrit:
woman did, whether just or unjust, now, to keep this promise, to show
their equilibrium and to save themselves from fighting with a woman,
they remained silent.

text: The demons had developed affection for Mohiné-mürti and a
sanskrit:
kind of faith in Her, and they were afraid of disturbing their
relationship. Therefore they showed respect and honor to Her words and
did not say anything that might disturb their friendship with Her.

text: Rähu, the demon who causes eclipses of the sun and moon,
sanskrit:
covered himself with the dress of a demigod and thus entered the
assembly of the demigods and drank nectar without being detected by
anyone, even by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The moon and the
sun, however, because of permanent animosity toward Rähu, understood
the situation. Thus Rähu was detected.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, using His disc,
sanskrit:
which was sharp like a razor, at once cut off Rähu's head. When Rähu's
head was severed from his body, the body, being untouched by the nectar,
could not survive.

text: Rähu's head, however, having been touched by the nectar,
sanskrit:
became immortal. Thus Lord Brahmä accepted Rähu's head as one of the
planets. Since Rähu is an eternal enemy of the moon and the sun, he
always tries to attack them on the nights of the full moon and the dark
moon.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is the best friend and
sanskrit:
well-wisher of the three worlds. Thus when the demigods had almost
finished drinking the nectar, the Lord, in the presence of all the
demons, disclosed His original form.

text: The place, the time, the cause, the purpose, the activity
sanskrit:
and the ambition were all the same for both the demigods and the demons,
but the demigods achieved one result and the demons another. Because the
demigods are always under the shelter of the dust of the Lord's lotus
feet, they could very easily drink the nectar and get its result. The
demons, however, not having sought shelter at the lotus feet of the
Lord, were unable to achieve the result they desired.

text: In human society there are various activities performed for
sanskrit:
the protection of one's wealth and life by one's words, one's mind and
one's actions, but they are all performed for one's personal or extended
sense gratification with reference to the body. All these activities are
baffled because of being separate from devotional service. But when the
same activities are performed for the satisfaction of the Lord, the
beneficial results are distributed to everyone, just as water poured on
the root of a tree is distributed throughout the entire tree.

text: The demigods and demons then observed a fast. After
sanskrit:
bathing, they offered clarified butter and oblations into the fire and
gave charity to the cows and to the brähmaëas and members of the other
orders of society, namely the kñatriyas, vaiçyas and çüdras, who
were all rewarded as they deserved. Thereafter, the demigods and demons
performed ritualistic ceremonies under the directions of the
brähmaëas. Then they dressed themselves with new garments according to
their own choice, decorated their bodies with ornaments, and sat facing
east on seats made of kuça grass.

text: O King, as the demigods and demons sat facing east in an
sanskrit:
arena fully decorated with flower garlands and lamps and fragrant with
the smoke of incense, that woman, dressed in a most beautiful sari, Her
ankle bells tinkling, entered the arena, walking very slowly because of
Her big, low hips. Her eyes were restless due to youthful pride, Her
breasts were like water jugs, Her thighs resembled the trunks of
elephants, and She carried a waterpot in Her hand.

text: Her attractive nose and cheeks and Her ears, adorned with
sanskrit:
golden earrings, made Her face very beautiful. As She moved, Her sari's
border on Her breasts moved slightly aside. When the demigods and demons
saw these beautiful features of Mohiné-mürti, who was glancing at them
and slightly smiling, they were all completely enchanted.

text: Demons are by nature crooked like snakes. Therefore, to
sanskrit:
distribute a share of the nectar to them was not at all feasible, since
this would be as dangerous as supplying milk to a snake. Considering
this, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who never falls down, did not
deliver a share of nectar to the demons.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead as Mohiné-mürti, the
sanskrit:
master of the universe, arranged separate lines of sitting places and
seated the demigods and demons according to their positions.

text: Taking the container of nectar in Her hands, She first
sanskrit:
approached the demons, satisfied them with sweet words and thus cheated
them of their share of the nectar. Then She administered the nectar to
the demigods, who were sitting at a distant place, to make them free
from invalidity, old age and death.

text: O King, since the demons had promised to accept whatever the
sanskrit:
woman did, whether just or unjust, now, to keep this promise, to show
their equilibrium and to save themselves from fighting with a woman,
they remained silent.

text: The demons had developed affection for Mohiné-mürti and a
sanskrit:
kind of faith in Her, and they were afraid of disturbing their
relationship. Therefore they showed respect and honor to Her words and
did not say anything that might disturb their friendship with Her.

text: Rähu, the demon who causes eclipses of the sun and moon,
sanskrit:
covered himself with the dress of a demigod and thus entered the
assembly of the demigods and drank nectar without being detected by
anyone, even by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The moon and the
sun, however, because of permanent animosity toward Rähu, understood
the situation. Thus Rähu was detected.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, using His disc,
sanskrit:
which was sharp like a razor, at once cut off Rähu's head. When Rähu's
head was severed from his body, the body, being untouched by the nectar,
could not survive.

text: Rähu's head, however, having been touched by the nectar,
sanskrit:
became immortal. Thus Lord Brahmä accepted Rähu's head as one of the
planets. Since Rähu is an eternal enemy of the moon and the sun, he
always tries to attack them on the nights of the full moon and the dark
moon.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is the best friend and
sanskrit:
well-wisher of the three worlds. Thus when the demigods had almost
finished drinking the nectar, the Lord, in the presence of all the
demons, disclosed His original form.

text: The place, the time, the cause, the purpose, the activity
sanskrit:
and the ambition were all the same for both the demigods and the demons,
but the demigods achieved one result and the demons another. Because the
demigods are always under the shelter of the dust of the Lord's lotus
feet, they could very easily drink the nectar and get its result. The
demons, however, not having sought shelter at the lotus feet of the
Lord, were unable to achieve the result they desired.

text: In human society there are various activities performed for
sanskrit:
the protection of one's wealth and life by one's words, one's mind and
one's actions, but they are all performed for one's personal or extended
sense gratification with reference to the body. All these activities are
baffled because of being separate from devotional service. But when the
same activities are performed for the satisfaction of the Lord, the
beneficial results are distributed to everyone, just as water poured on
the root of a tree is distributed throughout the entire tree.
The Lord Incarnates as Mohiné-Mürti
•  SB 8.9.1 - Çukadeva Gosvämé said: Thereafter, the demons
became inimical toward one another. Throwing and snatching the container
of nectar, they gave up their friendly relationship. Meanwhile, they saw
a very beautiful young woman coming forward toward them.

text: Upon seeing the beautiful woman, the demons said, "Alas, how
sanskrit:
wonderful is Her beauty, how wonderful the luster of Her body, and how
wonderful the beauty of Her youthful age!" Speaking in this way, they
quickly approached Her, full of lusty desires to enjoy Her, and began to
inquire from Her in many ways.

text: O wonderfully beautiful girl, You have such nice eyes,
sanskrit:
resembling the petals of a lotus flower. Who are You? Where do You come
from? What is Your purpose in coming here, and to whom do You belong? O
You whose thighs are extraordinarily beautiful, our minds are becoming
agitated simply because of seeing You.

text: What to speak of human beings, even the demigods, demons,
sanskrit:
Siddhas, Gandharvas, Cäraëas and the various directors of the
universe, the Prajäpatis, have never touched You before. It is not that
we are unable to understand Your identity.

text: O beautiful girl with beautiful eyebrows, certainly
sanskrit:
Providence, by His causeless mercy, has sent You to please the senses
and minds of all of us. Is this not a fact?

text: We are now all engaged in enmity among ourselves because of
sanskrit:
this one subject matter-the container of nectar. Although we have been
born in the same family, we are becoming increasingly inimical. O
thin-waisted woman, who are so beautiful in Your prestigious position,
we therefore request You to favor us by settling our dispute.

text: All of us, both demons and demigods, have been born of the
sanskrit:
same father, Kaçyapa, and thus we are related as brothers. But now we
are exhibiting our personal prowess in dissension. Therefore we request
You to settle our dispute and divide the nectar equally among us.

text: Having thus been requested by the demons, the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, who had assumed the form of a beautiful woman,
began to smile. Looking at them with attractive feminine gestures, She
spoke as follows.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the form of Mohiné,
sanskrit:
told the demons: O sons of Kaçyapa Muni, I am only a prostitute. Mow is
it that you have so much faith in Me? A learned person never puts his
faith in a woman.

text: O demons, as monkeys, jackals and dogs are unsteady in their
sanskrit:
sexual relationships and want newer and newer friends every day, women
who live independently seek new friends daily. Friendship with such a
woman is never permanent. This is the opinion of learned scholars.

text: Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: After the demons heard
sanskrit:
the words of Mohiné-mürti, who had spoken as if jokingly, they were
all very confident. They laughed with gravity, and ultimately they
delivered the container of nectar into Her hands.

Translations 1-29

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, the demons and Daityas all
sanskrit:
engaged with full attention and effort in churning the ocean, but
because they were not devotees of Väsudeva, the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, Kåñëa, they were not able to drink the nectar.

text: O King, after the Supreme Personality of Godhead had brought
sanskrit:
to completion the affairs of churning the ocean and feeding the nectar
to the demigods, who are His dear devotees, He left the presence of them
all and was carried by Garuòa to His own abode.

text: Seeing the victory of the demigods, the demons became
sanskrit:
intolerant of their superior opulence. Thus they began to march toward
the demigods with raised weapons.

text: Thereafter, being enlivened because of drinking the nectar,
sanskrit:
the demigods, who are always at the shelter of the lotus feet of
Näräyaëa, used their various weapons to counterattack the demons in a
fighting spirit.

text: O King, a fierce battle on the beach of the ocean of milk
sanskrit:
ensued between the demigods and the demons. The fighting was so terrible
that simply hearing about it would make the hair on one's body stand on
end.

text: Both parties in that fight were extremely angry at heart,
sanskrit:
and in enmity they beat one another with swords, arrows and varieties of
other weapons.

text: The sounds of the conchshells, bugles, drums, bherés and
sanskrit:
òamarés [kettledrums], as well as the sounds made by the elephants,
horses and soldiers, who were both on chariots and on foot, were
tumultuous.

text: On that battlefield, the charioteers fought with the
sanskrit:
opposing charioteers, the infantry soldiers with the opposing infantry,
the soldiers on horseback with the opposing soldiers on horseback, and
the soldiers on the backs of elephants with the enemy soldiers on
elephants. In this way, the fighting took place between equals.

text: Some soldiers fought on the backs of camels, some on the
sanskrit:
backs of elephants, some on asses, some on white-faced and red-faced
monkeys, some on tigers and some on lions. In this way, they all engaged
in fighting.

text: O King, some soldiers fought on the backs of vultures,
sanskrit:
eagles, ducks, hawks and bhäsa birds. Some fought on the backs of
timiìgilas, which can devour huge whales, some on the backs of
çarabhas, and some on buffalo, rhinoceroses, cows, bulls, jungle cows
and aruëas. Others fought on the backs of jackals, rats, lizards,
rabbits, human beings, goats, black deer, swans and boars. In this way,
mounted on animals of the water, land and sky, including animals with
deformed bodies, both armies faced each other and went forward.

text: O King, O descendant of Mahäräja Päëòu, the
sanskrit:
soldiers of both the demigods and demons were decorated by canopies,
colorful flags, and umbrellas with handles made of valuable jewels and
pearls. They were further decorated by fans made of peacock feathers and
by other fans also. The soldiers, their upper and lower garments waving
in the breeze, naturally looked very beautiful, and in the light of the
glittering sunshine their shields, ornaments and sharp, clean weapons
appeared dazzling. Thus the ranks of soldiers seemed like two oceans
with bands of aquatics.

text: For that battle the most celebrated commander in chief,
sanskrit:
Mahäräja Bali, son of Virocana, was seated on a wonderful airplane
named Vaihäyasa. O King, this beautifully decorated airplane had been
manufactured by the demon Maya and was equipped with weapons for all
types of combat. It was inconceivable and indescribable. Indeed, it was
sometimes visible and sometimes not. Seated in this airplane under a
beautiful protective umbrella and being fanned by the best of cämaras,
Mahäräja Bali, surrounded by his captains and commanders, appeared
just like the moon rising in the evening, illuminating all directions.

text: Surrounding Mahäräja Bali on all sides were the
sanskrit:
commanders and captains of the demons, sitting on their respective
chariots. Among them were the following demons: Namuci, Çambara,
Bäëa, Vipracitti, Ayomukha, Dvimürdhä, Kälanäbha, Praheti, Heti,
Ilvala, Çakuni, Bhütasantäpa, Vajradaàñöra, Virocana, Hayagréva,
Çaìkuçirä, Kapila, Meghadundubhi, Täraka, Cakradåk, Çumbha,
Niçumbha, Jambha, Utkala, Ariñöa, Ariñöanemi, Tripurädhipa, Maya,
the sons of Puloma, the Käleyas and Nivätakavaca. All of these demons
had been deprived of their share of the nectar and had shared merely in
the labor of churning the ocean. Now, they fought against the demigods,
and to encourage their armies, they made a tumultuous sound like the
roaring of lions and blew loudly on conchshells. Balabhit, Lord Indra,
upon seeing this situation of his ferocious rivals, became extremely
angry.

text: Sitting on Airävata, an elephant who can go anywhere and
sanskrit:
who holds water and wine in reserve for showering, Lord Indra looked
just like the sun rising from Udayagiri, where there are reservoirs of
water.

text: Surrounding Lord Indra, King of heaven, were the demigods,
sanskrit:
seated on various types of vehicles and decorated with flags and
weapons. Present among them were Väyu, Agni, Varuëa and other rulers
of various planets, along with their associates.

text: The demigods and demons came before each other and
sanskrit:
reproached one another with words piercing to the heart. Then they drew
near and began fighting face to face in pairs.

text: O King, Mahäräja Bali fought with Indra, Kärttikeya with
sanskrit: Täraka, Varuëa with Heti, and Mitra with Praheti.

text: Yamaräja fought with Kälanäbha, Viçvakarmä with Maya
sanskrit: Dänava, Tvañöä with Çambara, and the sun-god with Virocana.

text: The demigod Aparäjita fought with Namuci, and the two
sanskrit:
Açviné-kumära brothers fought with Våñaparvä. The sun-god fought
with the one hundred sons of Mahäräja Bali, headed by Bäëa, and the
moon-god fought with Rähu. The demigod controlling air fought with
Puloma, and Çumbha and Niçumbha fought the supremely powerful material
energy, Durgädevé, who is called Bhadra Kälé.

text: O Mahäräja Parékñit, suppressor of enemies
sanskrit:
[Arindama], Lord Çiva fought with Jambha, and Vibhävasu fought with
Mahiñäsura. Ilvala, along with his brother Vätäpi, fought the sons
of Lord Brahmä. Durmarña fought with Cupid, the demon Utkala with the
Mätåkä demigoddesses, Båhaspati with Çukräcärya, and Çanaiçcara
[Saturn] with Narakäsura. The Maruts fought Nivätakavaca, the Vasus
fought the Kälakeya demons, the Viçvedeva demigods fought the Pauloma
demons, and the Rudras fought the Krodhavaça demons, who were victims
of anger.

text: All of these demigods and demons assembled on the
sanskrit:
battlefield with a fighting spirit and attacked one another with great
strength. All of them desiring victory, they fought in pairs, hitting
one another severely with sharpened arrows, swords and lances.

text: They severed one another's heads, using weapons like
sanskrit:
bhuçuëòis, cakras, clubs, åñöis, paööiças, çaktis, ulmukas,
präsas, paraçvadhas, nistriàças, lances, parighas, mudgaras and
bhindipälas.

text: The elephants, horses, chariots, charioteers, infantry
sanskrit:
soldiers and various kinds of carriers, along with their riders, were
slashed to pieces. The arms, thighs, necks and legs of the soldiers were
severed, and their flags, bows, armor and ornaments were torn apart.

text: Because of the impact on the ground of the legs of the
sanskrit:
demons and demigods and the wheels of the chariots, particles of dust
flew violently into the sky and made a dust cloud that covered all
directions of outer space, as far as the sun. But when the particles of
dust were followed by drops of blood being sprinkled all over space, the
dust cloud could no longer float in the sky.

text: In the course of the battle, the warfield became strewn
sanskrit:
with the severed heads of heroes, their eyes still staring and their
teeth still pressed against their lips in anger. Helmets and earrings
were scattered from these severed heads. Similarly, many arms, decorated
with ornaments and clutching various weapons, were strewn here and
there, as were many legs and thighs, which resembled the trunks of
elephants.

text: Many headless trunks were generated on that battlefield.
sanskrit:
With weapons in their arms, those ghostly trunks, which could see with
the eyes in the fallen heads, attacked the enemy soldiers.

text: Mahäräja Bali then attacked Indra with ten arrows and
sanskrit:
attacked Airävata, Indra's carrier elephant, with three arrows. With
four arrows he attacked the four horsemen guarding Airävata's legs, and
with one arrow he attacked the driver of the elephant.

text: Before Bali Mahäräja's arrows could reach him, Indra,
sanskrit:
King of heaven, who is expert in dealing with arrows, smiled and
counteracted the arrows with arrows of another type, known as bhalla,
which were extremely sharp.

text: When Bali Mahäräja saw the expert military activities of
sanskrit:
Indra, he could not restrain his anger. Thus he took up another weapon,
known as çakti, which blazed like a great firebrand. But Indra cut that
weapon to pieces while it was still in Bali's hand.

text: Thereafter, one by one, Bali Mahäräja used a lance,
sanskrit:
präsa, tomara, åñöis and other weapons, but whatever weapons he took
up, Indra immediately cut them to pieces.

text: My dear King, Bali Mahäräja then disappeared and resorted
sanskrit:
to demoniac illusions. A giant mountain, generated from illusion, then
appeared above the heads of the demigod soldiers.

text: From that mountain fell trees blazing in a forest fire.
sanskrit:
Chips of stone, with sharp edges like picks, also fell and smashed the
heads of the demigod soldiers.

text: Scorpions, large snakes and many other poisonous animals,
sanskrit:
as well as lions, tigers, boars and great elephants, all began falling
upon the demigod soldiers, crushing everything.

text: O my King, many hundreds of male and female carnivorous
sanskrit:
demons, completely naked and carrying tridents in their hands, then
appeared, crying the slogans "Cut them to pieces! Pierce them!"

text: Fierce clouds, harassed by strong winds, then appeared in
sanskrit:
the sky. Rumbling very gravely with the sound of thunder, they began to
shower live coals.

text: A great devastating fire created by Bali Mahäräja began
sanskrit:
burning all the soldiers of the demigods. This fire, accompanied by
blasting winds, seemed as terrible as the Säàvartaka fire, which
appears at the time of dissolution.

text: Thereafter, whirlpools and sea waves, agitated by fierce
sanskrit:
blasts of wind, appeared everywhere, before everyone's vision, in a
furious flood.

text: While this magical atmosphere in the fight was being
sanskrit:
created by the invisible demons, who were expert in such illusions, the
soldiers of the demigods became morose.

text: O King, when the demigods could find no way to counteract
sanskrit:
the activities of the demons, they wholeheartedly meditated upon the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, the creator of the universe, who then
immediately appeared.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose eyes resemble the
sanskrit:
petals of a newly blossomed lotus, sat on the back of Garuòa, spreading
His lotus feet over Garuòa's shoulders. Dressed in yellow, decorated by
the Kaustubha gem and the goddess of fortune, and wearing an invaluable
helmet and earrings, the Supreme Lord, holding various weapons in His
eight hands, became visible to the demigods.

text: As the dangers of a dream cease when the dreamer awakens,
sanskrit:
the illusions created by the jugglery of the demons were vanquished by
the transcendental prowess of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as soon
as He entered the battlefield. Indeed, simply by remembrance of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, one becomes free from all dangers.

text: O King, when the demon Kälanemi, who was carried by a
sanskrit:
lion, saw that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, carried by Garuòa,
was on the battlefield, the demon immediately took his trident, whirled
it and discharged it at Garuòa's head. The Supreme Personality of
Godhead, Hari, the master of the three worlds, immediately caught the
trident, and with the very same weapon he killed the enemy Kälanemi,
along with his carrier, the lion.

text: Thereafter, two very powerful demons named Mälé and
sanskrit:
Sumälé were killed by the Supreme Lord, who severed their heads with
His disc. Then Mälyavän, another demon, attacked the Lord. With his
sharp club, the demon, who was roaring like a lion, attacked Garuòa,
the lord of the birds, who are born from eggs. But the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, the original person, used His disc to cut off
the head of that enemy also.

monkeys, some on tigers and some on lions. In this way, they all engaged
in fighting.

text: O King, some soldiers fought on the backs of vultures,
sanskrit:
eagles, ducks, hawks and bhäsa birds. Some fought on the backs of
timiìgilas, which can devour huge whales, some on the backs of
çarabhas, and some on buffalo, rhinoceroses, cows, bulls, jungle cows
and aruëas. Others fought on the backs of jackals, rats, lizards,
rabbits, human beings, goats, black deer, swans and boars. In this way,
mounted on animals of the water, land and sky, including animals with
deformed bodies, both armies faced each other and went forward.

text: O King, O descendant of Mahäräja Päëòu, the
sanskrit:
soldiers of both the demigods and demons were decorated by canopies,
colorful flags, and umbrellas with handles made of valuable jewels and
pearls. They were further decorated by fans made of peacock feathers and
by other fans also. The soldiers, their upper and lower garments waving
in the breeze, naturally looked very beautiful, and in the light of the
glittering sunshine their shields, ornaments and sharp, clean weapons
appeared dazzling. Thus the ranks of soldiers seemed like two oceans
with bands of aquatics.

text: For that battle the most celebrated commander in chief,
sanskrit:
Mahäräja Bali, son of Virocana, was seated on a wonderful airplane
named Vaihäyasa. O King, this beautifully decorated airplane had been
manufactured by the demon Maya and was equipped with weapons for all
types of combat. It was inconceivable and indescribable. Indeed, it was
sometimes visible and sometimes not. Seated in this airplane under a
beautiful protective umbrella and being fanned by the best of cämaras,
Mahäräja Bali, surrounded by his captains and commanders, appeared
just like the moon rising in the evening, illuminating all directions.

text: Surrounding Mahäräja Bali on all sides were the
sanskrit:
commanders and captains of the demons, sitting on their respective
chariots. Among them were the following demons: Namuci, Çambara,
Bäëa, Vipracitti, Ayomukha, Dvimürdhä, Kälanäbha, Praheti, Heti,
Ilvala, Çakuni, Bhütasantäpa, Vajradaàñöra, Virocana, Hayagréva,
Çaìkuçirä, Kapila, Meghadundubhi, Täraka, Cakradåk, Çumbha,
Niçumbha, Jambha, Utkala, Ariñöa, Ariñöanemi, Tripurädhipa, Maya,
the sons of Puloma, the Käleyas and Nivätakavaca. All of these demons
had been deprived of their share of the nectar and had shared merely in
the labor of churning the ocean. Now, they fought against the demigods,
and to encourage their armies, they made a tumultuous sound like the
roaring of lions and blew loudly on conchshells. Balabhit, Lord Indra,
upon seeing this situation of his ferocious rivals, became extremely
angry.

text: Sitting on Airävata, an elephant who can go anywhere and
sanskrit:
who holds water and wine in reserve for showering, Lord Indra looked
just like the sun rising from Udayagiri, where there are reservoirs of
water.

text: Surrounding Lord Indra, King of heaven, were the demigods,
sanskrit:
seated on various types of vehicles and decorated with flags and
weapons. Present among them were Väyu, Agni, Varuëa and other rulers
of various planets, along with their associates.

text: The demigods and demons came before each other and
sanskrit:
reproached one another with words piercing to the heart. Then they drew
near and began fighting face to face in pairs.

text: O King, Mahäräja Bali fought with Indra, Kärttikeya with
sanskrit: Täraka, Varuëa with Heti, and Mitra with Praheti.

text: Yamaräja fought with Kälanäbha, Viçvakarmä with Maya
sanskrit: Dänava, Tvañöä with Çambara, and the sun-god with Virocana.

text: The demigod Aparäjita fought with Namuci, and the two
sanskrit:
Açviné-kumära brothers fought with Våñaparvä. The sun-god fought
with the one hundred sons of Mahäräja Bali, headed by Bäëa, and the
moon-god fought with Rähu. The demigod controlling air fought with
Puloma, and Çumbha and Niçumbha fought the supremely powerful material
energy, Durgädevé, who is called Bhadra Kälé.

text: O Mahäräja Parékñit, suppressor of enemies
sanskrit:
[Arindama], Lord Çiva fought with Jambha, and Vibhävasu fought with
Mahiñäsura. Ilvala, along with his brother Vätäpi, fought the sons
of Lord Brahmä. Durmarña fought with Cupid, the demon Utkala with the
Mätåkä demigoddesses, Båhaspati with Çukräcärya, and Çanaiçcara
[Saturn] with Narakäsura. The Maruts fought Nivätakavaca, the Vasus
fought the Kälakeya demons, the Viçvedeva demigods fought the Pauloma
demons, and the Rudras fought the Krodhavaça demons, who were victims
of anger.

text: All of these demigods and demons assembled on the
sanskrit:
battlefield with a fighting spirit and attacked one another with great
strength. All of them desiring victory, they fought in pairs, hitting
one another severely with sharpened arrows, swords and lances.

text: They severed one another's heads, using weapons like
sanskrit:
bhuçuëòis, cakras, clubs, åñöis, paööiças, çaktis, ulmukas,
präsas, paraçvadhas, nistriàças, lances, parighas, mudgaras and
bhindipälas.

text: The elephants, horses, chariots, charioteers, infantry
sanskrit:
soldiers and various kinds of carriers, along with their riders, were
slashed to pieces. The arms, thighs, necks and legs of the soldiers were
severed, and their flags, bows, armor and ornaments were torn apart.

text: Because of the impact on the ground of the legs of the
sanskrit:
demons and demigods and the wheels of the chariots, particles of dust
flew violently into the sky and made a dust cloud that covered all
directions of outer space, as far as the sun. But when the particles of
dust were followed by drops of blood being sprinkled all over space, the
dust cloud could no longer float in the sky.

text: In the course of the battle, the warfield became strewn
sanskrit:
with the severed heads of heroes, their eyes still staring and their
teeth still pressed against their lips in anger. Helmets and earrings
were scattered from these severed heads. Similarly, many arms, decorated
with ornaments and clutching various weapons, were strewn here and
there, as were many legs and thighs, which resembled the trunks of
elephants.

text: Many headless trunks were generated on that battlefield.
sanskrit:
With weapons in their arms, those ghostly trunks, which could see with
the eyes in the fallen heads, attacked the enemy soldiers.

text: Mahäräja Bali then attacked Indra with ten arrows and
sanskrit:
attacked Airävata, Indra's carrier elephant, with three arrows. With
four arrows he attacked the four horsemen guarding Airävata's legs, and
with one arrow he attacked the driver of the elephant.

text: Before Bali Mahäräja's arrows could reach him, Indra,
sanskrit:
King of heaven, who is expert in dealing with arrows, smiled and
counteracted the arrows with arrows of another type, known as bhalla,
which were extremely sharp.

text: When Bali Mahäräja saw the expert military activities of
sanskrit:
Indra, he could not restrain his anger. Thus he took up another weapon,
known as çakti, which blazed like a great firebrand. But Indra cut that
weapon to pieces while it was still in Bali's hand.

text: Thereafter, one by one, Bali Mahäräja used a lance,
sanskrit:
präsa, tomara, åñöis and other weapons, but whatever weapons he took
up, Indra immediately cut them to pieces.

text: My dear King, Bali Mahäräja then disappeared and resorted
sanskrit:
to demoniac illusions. A giant mountain, generated from illusion, then
appeared above the heads of the demigod soldiers.

text: From that mountain fell trees blazing in a forest fire.
sanskrit:
Chips of stone, with sharp edges like picks, also fell and smashed the
heads of the demigod soldiers.

text: Scorpions, large snakes and many other poisonous animals,
sanskrit:
as well as lions, tigers, boars and great elephants, all began falling
upon the demigod soldiers, crushing everything.

text: O my King, many hundreds of male and female carnivorous
sanskrit:
demons, completely naked and carrying tridents in their hands, then
appeared, crying the slogans "Cut them to pieces! Pierce them!"

text: Fierce clouds, harassed by strong winds, then appeared in
sanskrit:
the sky. Rumbling very gravely with the sound of thunder, they began to
shower live coals.

text: A great devastating fire created by Bali Mahäräja began
sanskrit:
burning all the soldiers of the demigods. This fire, accompanied by
blasting winds, seemed as terrible as the Säàvartaka fire, which
appears at the time of dissolution.

text: Thereafter, whirlpools and sea waves, agitated by fierce
sanskrit:
blasts of wind, appeared everywhere, before everyone's vision, in a
furious flood.

text: While this magical atmosphere in the fight was being
sanskrit:
created by the invisible demons, who were expert in such illusions, the
soldiers of the demigods became morose.

text: O King, when the demigods could find no way to counteract
sanskrit:
the activities of the demons, they wholeheartedly meditated upon the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, the creator of the universe, who then
immediately appeared.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose eyes resemble the
sanskrit:
petals of a newly blossomed lotus, sat on the back of Garuòa, spreading
His lotus feet over Garuòa's shoulders. Dressed in yellow, decorated by
the Kaustubha gem and the goddess of fortune, and wearing an invaluable
helmet and earrings, the Supreme Lord, holding various weapons in His
eight hands, became visible to the demigods.

text: As the dangers of a dream cease when the dreamer awakens,
sanskrit:
the illusions created by the jugglery of the demons were vanquished by
the transcendental prowess of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as soon
as He entered the battlefield. Indeed, simply by remembrance of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, one becomes free from all dangers.

text: O King, when the demon Kälanemi, who was carried by a
sanskrit:
lion, saw that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, carried by Garuòa,
was on the battlefield, the demon immediately took his trident, whirled
it and discharged it at Garuòa's head. The Supreme Personality of
Godhead, Hari, the master of the three worlds, immediately caught the
trident, and with the very same weapon he killed the enemy Kälanemi,
along with his carrier, the lion.

text: Thereafter, two very powerful demons named Mälé and
sanskrit:
Sumälé were killed by the Supreme Lord, who severed their heads with
His disc. Then Mälyavän, another demon, attacked the Lord. With his
sharp club, the demon, who was roaring like a lion, attacked Garuòa,
the lord of the birds, who are born from eggs. But the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, the original person, used His disc to cut off
the head of that enemy also.
The Battle Between the Demigods and the Demons
•  SB 8.10.1 - Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, the demons and
Daityas all engaged with full attention and effort in churning the
ocean, but because they were not devotees of Väsudeva, the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, they were not able to drink the
nectar.

text: O King, after the Supreme Personality of Godhead had brought
sanskrit:
to completion the affairs of churning the ocean and feeding the nectar
to the demigods, who are His dear devotees, He left the presence of them
all and was carried by Garuòa to His own abode.

text: Seeing the victory of the demigods, the demons became
sanskrit:
intolerant of their superior opulence. Thus they began to march toward
the demigods with raised weapons.

text: Thereafter, being enlivened because of drinking the nectar,
sanskrit:
the demigods, who are always at the shelter of the lotus feet of
Näräyaëa, used their various weapons to counterattack the demons in a
fighting spirit.

text: O King, a fierce battle on the beach of the ocean of milk
sanskrit:
ensued between the demigods and the demons. The fighting was so terrible
that simply hearing about it would make the hair on one's body stand on
end.

text: Both parties in that fight were extremely angry at heart,
sanskrit:
and in enmity they beat one another with swords, arrows and varieties of
other weapons.

text: The sounds of the conchshells, bugles, drums, bherés and
sanskrit:
òamarés [kettledrums], as well as the sounds made by the elephants,
horses and soldiers, who were both on chariots and on foot, were
tumultuous.

text: On that battlefield, the charioteers fought with the
sanskrit:
opposing charioteers, the infantry soldiers with the opposing infantry,
the soldiers on horseback with the opposing soldiers on horseback, and
the soldiers on the backs of elephants with the enemy soldiers on
elephants. In this way, the fighting took place between equals.

Translations 1-57

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: Thereafter, by the supreme grace
sanskrit:
of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Çré Hari, all the demigods,
headed by Indra and Väyu, were brought back to life. Being enlivened,
the demigods began severely beating the very same demons who had
defeated them before.

text: When the most powerful Indra became angry and took his
sanskrit:
thunderbolt in hand to kill Mahäräja Bali, the demons began lamenting,
"Alas, alas!"

text: Sober and tolerant and well equipped with paraphernalia for
sanskrit:
fighting, Bali Mahäräja moved before Indra on the great battlefield.
King Indra, who always carries the thunderbolt in his hand, rebuked Bali
Mahäräja as follows.

text: Indra said: O rascal, as a cheater sometimes binds the eyes
sanskrit:
of a child and takes away his possessions, you are trying to defeat us
by displaying some mystic power, although you know that we are the
masters of all such mystic powers.

text: Those fools and rascals who want to ascend to the upper
sanskrit:
planetary system by mystic power or mechanical means, or who endeavor to
cross even the upper planets and achieve the spiritual world or
liberation, I cause to be sent to the lowest region of the universe.

text: Today, with my thunderbolt, which has hundreds of sharp
sanskrit:
edges, I, the same powerful person, shall sever your head from your
body. Although you can produce so much jugglery through illusion, you
are endowed with a poor fund of knowledge. Now, try to exist on this
battlefield with your relatives and friends.

text: Bali Mahäräja replied: All those present on this
sanskrit:
battlefield are certainly under the influence of eternal time, and
according to their prescribed activities, they are destined to receive
fame, victory, defeat and death, one after another.

text: Seeing the movements of time, those who are cognizant of the
sanskrit:
real truth neither rejoice nor lament for different circumstances.
Therefore, because you are jubilant due to your victory, you should be
considered not very learned.

text: You demigods think that your own selves are the cause of
sanskrit:
your attaining fame and victory. Because of your ignorance, saintly
persons feel sorry for you. Therefore, although your words afflict the
heart, we do not accept them.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: After thus rebuking Indra, King
sanskrit:
of heaven, with sharp words, Bali Mahäräja, who could subdue any other
hero, drew back to his ear the arrows known as näräcas and attacked
Indra with these arrows. Then he again chastised Indra with strong
words.

text: Since Mahäräja Bali's rebukes were truthful, King Indra
sanskrit:
did not at all become sorry, just as an elephant beaten by its driver's
rod does not become agitated.

text: When Indra, the defeater of enemies, released his
sanskrit:
infallible thunderbolt scepter at Bali Mahäräja with a desire to kill
him, Bali Mahäräja indeed fell to the ground with his airplane, like a
mountain with its wings cut off.

text: When the demon Jambhäsura saw that his friend Bali had
sanskrit:
fallen, he appeared before Indra, the enemy, just to serve Bali
Mahäräja with friendly behavior.

text: The greatly powerful Jambhäsura, carried by a lion,
sanskrit:
approached Indra and forcefully struck him on the shoulder with his
club. He also struck Indra's elephant.

text: Being beaten by Jambhäsura's club, Indra's elephant was
sanskrit:
confused and aggrieved. Thus it touched its knees to the ground and fell
unconscious.

text: Thereafter, Mätali, Indra's chariot driver, brought
sanskrit:
Indra's chariot, which was drawn by one thousand horses. Indra then left
his elephant and got onto the chariot.

sanskrit:
the demons, smiled. Nonetheless, he struck Mätali in the battle with a
trident of blazing fire.

text: Although the pain was extremely severe, Mätali tolerated
sanskrit:
it with great patience. Indra, however, became extremely angry at
Jambhäsura. He struck Jambhäsura with his thunderbolt and thus severed
his head from his body.

text: When Närada Åñi informed Jambhäsura's friends and
sanskrit:
relatives that Jambhäsura had been killed, the three demons named
Namuci, Bala and Päka arrived on the battlefield in great haste.

text: Rebuking Indra with harsh, cruel words that were piercing
sanskrit:
to the heart, these demons showered him with arrows, just as torrents of
rain wash a great mountain.

text: Quickly handling the situation on the battlefield, the
sanskrit:
demon Bala put all of Indra's one thousand horses into tribulation by
simultaneously piercing them all with an equal number of arrows.

text: Päka, another demon, attacked both the chariot, with all
sanskrit:
its paraphernalia, and the chariot driver, Mätali, by fitting two
hundred arrows to his bow and releasing them all simultaneously. This
was indeed a wonderful act on the battlefield.

text: Then Namuci, another demon, attacked Indra and injured him
sanskrit:
with fifteen very powerful golden-feathered arrows, which roared like a
cloud full of water.

text: Other demons covered Indra, along with his chariot and
sanskrit:
chariot driver, with incessant showers of arrows, just as clouds cover
the sun in the rainy season.

text: The demigods, being severely oppressed by their enemies and
sanskrit:
being unable to see Indra on the battlefield, were very anxious. Having
no captain or leader, they began lamenting like traders in a wrecked
vessel in the midst of the ocean.

text: Thereafter, Indra released himself from the cage of the
sanskrit:
network of arrows. Appearing with his chariot, flag, horses and chariot
driver and thus pleasing the sky, the earth and all directions, he shone
effulgently like the sun at the end of night. Indra was bright and
beautiful in the vision of everyone.

text: When Indra, who is known as Vajra-dhara, the carrier of the
sanskrit:
thunderbolt, saw his own soldiers so oppressed by the enemies on the
battlefield, he became very angry. Thus he took up his thunderbolt to
kill the enemies.

text: O King Parékñit, King Indra used his thunderbolt to cut
sanskrit:
off the heads of both Bala and Päka in the presence of all their
relatives and followers. In this way he created a very fearful
atmosphere on the battlefield.

text: O King, when Namuci, another demon, saw the killing of both
sanskrit:
Bala and Päka, he was full of grief and lamentation. Thus he angrily
made a great attempt to kill Indra.

text: Being angry and roaring like a lion, the demon Namuci took
sanskrit:
up a steel spear, which was bound with bells and decorated with
ornaments of gold. He loudly cried, "Now you are killed!" Thus coming
before Indra to kill him, Namuci released his weapon.

text: O King, when Indra, King of heaven, saw this very powerful
sanskrit:
spear falling toward the ground like a blazing meteor, he immediately
cut it to pieces with his arrows. Then, being very angry, he struck
Namuci's shoulder with his thunderbolt to cut off Namuci's head.

text: Although King Indra hurled his thunderbolt at Namuci with
sanskrit:
great force, it could not even pierce his skin. It is very wonderful
that the famed thunderbolt that had pierced the body of Våträsura
could not even slightly injure the skin of Namuci's neck.

text: When Indra saw the thunderbolt return from the enemy, he
sanskrit:
was very much afraid. He began to wonder whether this had happened
because of some miraculous superior power.

text: Indra thought: Formerly, when many mountains flying in the
sanskrit:
sky with wings would fall to the ground and kill people, I cut their
wings with this same thunderbolt.

text: Våträsura was the essence of the austerities undergone by
sanskrit:
Tvañöä, yet the thunderbolt killed him. Indeed, not only he but also
many other stalwart heroes, whose very skin could not be injured even by
all kinds of weapons, were killed by the same thunderbolt.

text: But now, although the same thunderbolt has been released
sanskrit:
against a less important demon, it has been ineffectual. Therefore,
although it was as good as a brahmästra, it has now become useless like
an ordinary rod. I shall therefore hold it no longer.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: While the morose Indra was
sanskrit:
lamenting in this way, an ominous, unembodied voice said from the sky,
"This demon Namuci is not to be annihilated by anything dry or moist."

text: The voice also said, "O Indra, because I have given this
sanskrit:
demon the benediction that he will never be killed by any weapon that is
dry or moist, you have to think of another way to kill him."

text: After hearing the ominous voice, Indra, with great
sanskrit:
attention, began to meditate on how to kill the demon. He then saw that
foam would be the means, for it is neither moist nor dry.

text: Thus Indra, King of heaven, severed Namuci's head with a
sanskrit:
weapon of foam, which was neither dry nor moist. Then all the sages
satisfied Indra, the exalted personality, by showering flowers and
garlands upon him, almost covering him.

text: Viçvävasu and Parävasu, the two chiefs of the
sanskrit:
Gandharvas, sang in great happiness. The kettledrums of the demigods
sounded, and the Apsaräs danced in jubilation.

text: Väyu, Agni, Varuëa and other demigods began killing the
sanskrit: demons who opposed them, just as lions kill deer in a forest.

text: O King, when Lord Brahmä saw the imminent total
sanskrit:
annihilation of the demons, he sent a message with Närada, who went
before the demigods to make them stop fighting.

text: The great sage Närada said: All of you demigods are
sanskrit:
protected by the arms of Näräyaëa, the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, and by His grace you have gotten the nectar. By the grace of
the goddess of fortune, you are glorious in every way. Therefore, please
stop this fighting.

text: Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé said: Accepting the words of
sanskrit:
Närada, the demigods gave up their anger and stopped fighting. Being
praised by their followers, they returned to their heavenly planets.

text: Following the order of Närada Muni, whatever demons
sanskrit:
remained on the battlefield took Bali Mahäräja, who was in a
precarious condition, to the hill known as Astagiri.

text: There, on that hill, Çukräcärya brought to life all the
sanskrit:
dead demoniac soldiers who had not lost their heads, trunks and limbs.
He achieved this by his own mantra, known as Saàjévané.

text: Bali Mahäräja was very experienced in universal affairs.
sanskrit:
When he regained his senses and memory by the grace of Çukräcärya, he
could understand everything that had happened. Therefore, although he
had been defeated, he did not lament.

grace of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Çré Hari, all the
demigods, headed by Indra and Väyu, were brought back to life. Being
enlivened, the demigods began severely beating the very same demons who
had defeated them before.

sanskrit:
thunderbolt in hand to kill Mahäräja Bali, the demons began lamenting,

sanskrit:

sanskrit:
of a child and takes away his possessions, you are trying to defeat us
by displaying some mystic power, although you know that we are the
masters of all such mystic powers.

text: Those fools and rascals who want to ascend to the upper
sanskrit:
planetary system by mystic power or mechanical means, or who endeavor to
cross even the upper planets and achieve the spiritual world or
liberation, I cause to be sent to the lowest region of the universe.

text: Today, with my thunderbolt, which has hundreds of sharp
sanskrit:
edges, I, the same powerful person, shall sever your head from your

sanskrit:
battlefield are certainly under the influence of eternal time, and

sanskrit:
real truth neither rejoice nor lament for different circumstances.

sanskrit:
your attaining fame and victory. Because of your ignorance, saintly

text: Following the order of Närada Muni, whatever demons
sanskrit:
remained on the battlefield took Bali Mahäräja, who was in a
precarious condition, to the hill known as Astagiri.

text: There, on that hill, Çukräcärya brought to life all the
sanskrit:
dead demoniac soldiers who had not lost their heads, trunks and limbs.
He achieved this by his own mantra, known as Saàjévané.

text: Bali Mahäräja was very experienced in universal affairs.
sanskrit:
When he regained his senses and memory by the grace of Çukräcärya, he
could understand everything that had happened. Therefore, although he
had been defeated, he did not lament.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: The Supreme Personality of
sanskrit:
Godhead, Hari, in the form of a woman, captivated the demons and enabled
the demigods to drink the nectar. After hearing of these pastimes, Lord
Çiva, who is carried by a bull, went to the place where Madhusüdana,
the Lord, resides. Accompanied by his wife, Umä, and surrounded by his
companions, the ghosts, Lord Çiva went there to see the Lord's form as
a woman.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead welcomed Lord Çiva and
sanskrit:
Umä with great respect, and after being seated comfortably, Lord Çiva
duly worshiped the Lord and smilingly spoke as follows.

sanskrit:
all-pervading Lord, master of the universe, by Your energy You are
transformed into the creation. You are the root and efficient cause of
everything. You are not material. Indeed, You are the Supersoul or
supreme living force of everything. Therefore, You are Parameçvara, the
supreme controller of all controllers.

text: The manifest, the unmanifest, false ego and the beginning,
sanskrit:
maintenance and annihilation of this cosmic manifestation all come from
You, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. But because You are the
Absolute Truth, the supreme absolute spirit soul, the Supreme Brahman,
such changes as birth, death and sustenance do not exist in You.

text: Pure devotees or great saintly persons who desire to achieve
sanskrit:
the highest goal in life and who are completely free from all material
desires for sense gratification engage constantly in the transcendental
service of Your lotus feet.

text: My Lord, You are the Supreme Brahman, complete in
sanskrit:
everything. Being completely spiritual, You are eternal, free from the
material modes of nature, and full of transcendental bliss. Indeed, for
You there is no question of lamentation. Since You are the supreme
cause, the cause of all causes, nothing can exist without You. Yet we
are different from You in a relationship of cause and effect, for in one
sense the cause and effect are different. You are the original cause of
creation, manifestation and annihilation, and You bestow benedictions
upon all living entities. Everyone depends upon You for the results of
his activities, but You are always independent.

text: My dear Lord, Your Lordship alone is the cause and the
sanskrit:
effect. Therefore, although You appear to be two, You are the absolute
one. As there is no difference between the gold of a golden ornament and
the gold in a mine, there is no difference between cause and effect;
both of them are the same. Only because of ignorance do people concoct
differences and dualities. You are free from material contamination, and
since the entire cosmos is caused by You and cannot exist without You,
it is an effect of Your transcendental qualities. Thus the conception
that Brahman is true and the world false cannot be maintained.

text: Those who are known as the impersonalist Vedäntists regard
sanskrit:
You as the impersonal Brahman. Others, known as the Mémäàsaka
philosophers, regard You as religion. The Säìkhya philosophers regard
You as the transcendental person who is beyond prakåti and puruña and
who is the controller of even the demigods. The followers of the codes
of devotional service known as the Païcarätras regard You as being
endowed with nine different potencies. And the Pataïjala philosophers,
the followers of Pataïjali Muni, regard You as the supreme independent
Personality of Godhead, who has no equal or superior.

text: O my Lord, I, who am considered to be the best of the
sanskrit:
demigods, and Lord Brahmä and the great åñis, headed by Maréci, are
born of the mode of goodness. Nonetheless, we are bewildered by Your
illusory energy and cannot understand what this creation is. Aside from
us, what is to be said of others, like the demons and human beings, who
are in the base modes of material nature [rajo-guëa and tamo-guëa]?
How will they know You?

text: My Lord, You are the supreme knowledge personified. You
sanskrit:
know everything about this creation and its beginning, maintenance and
annihilation, and You know all the endeavors made by the living
entities, by which they are either implicated in this material world or
liberated from it. As the air enters the vast sky and also enters the
bodies of all moving and nonmoving entities, You are present everywhere,
and therefore You are the knower of all.

text: My Lord, I have seen all kinds of incarnations You have
sanskrit:
exhibited by Your transcendental qualities, and now that You have
appeared as a beautiful young woman, I wish to see that form of Your
Lordship.

text: My Lord, we have come here desiring to see that form of
sanskrit:
Your Lordship which You showed to the demons to captivate them
completely and in this way enable the demigods to drink nectar. I am
very eager to see that form.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: When Lord Viñëu was thus
sanskrit:
requested by Lord Çiva, who carries a trident in his hand, He smiled
with gravity and replied to Lord Çiva as follows.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: When the demons
sanskrit:
took away the jug of nectar, I assumed the form of a beautiful woman to
bewilder them by directly cheating them and thus to act in the interest
of the demigods.

text: O best of the demigods, I shall now show you My form that
sanskrit:
is very much appreciated by those who are lusty. Since you want to see
that form, I shall reveal it in your presence.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: After speaking in this way,
sanskrit:
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viñëu, immediately disappeared,
and Lord Çiva remained there with Umä, looking for Him all around with
moving eyes.

text: Thereafter, in a nice forest nearby, full of trees with
sanskrit:
reddish-pink leaves and varieties of flowers, Lord Çiva saw a beautiful
woman playing with a ball. Her hips were covered with a shining sari and
ornamented with a belt.

text: Because the ball was falling down and bouncing up, as She
sanskrit:
played with it Her breasts trembled, and because of the weight of those
breasts and Her heavy flower garlands, Her waist appeared to be all but
breaking at every step, as Her two soft feet, which were reddish like
coral, moved here and there.

text: The woman's face was decorated by broad, beautiful,
sanskrit:
restless eyes, which moved as the ball bounced here and there from Her
hand. The two brilliant earrings on Her ears decorated Her shining
cheeks like bluish reflections, and the hair scattered on Her face made
Her even more beautiful to see.

text: As She played with the ball, the sari covering Her body
sanskrit:
became loose, and Her hair scattered. She tried to bind Her hair with
Her beautiful left hand, and at the same time She played with the ball
by striking it with Her right hand. This was so attractive that the
Supreme Lord, by His internal potency, in this way captivated everyone.

text: While Lord Çiva observed the beautiful woman playing with
sanskrit:
the ball, She sometimes glanced at him and slightly smiled in
bashfulness. As he looked at the beautiful woman and She watched him, he
forgot both himself and Umä, his most beautiful wife, as well as his
associates nearby.

text: When the ball leaped from Her hand and fell at a distance,
sanskrit:
the woman began to follow it, but as Lord Çiva observed these
activities, a breeze suddenly blew away the fine dress and belt that
covered her.

text: Thus Lord Çiva saw the woman, every part of whose body was
sanskrit:
beautifully formed, and the beautiful woman also looked at him.
Therefore, thinking that She was attracted to him, Lord Çiva became
very much attracted to Her.

text: Lord Çiva, his good sense taken away by the woman because
sanskrit:
of lusty desires to enjoy with Her, became so mad for Her that even in
the presence of Bhaväné he did not hesitate to approach Her.

text: The beautiful woman was already naked, and when She saw
sanskrit:
Lord Çiva coming toward Her, She became extremely bashful. Thus She
kept smiling, but She hid Herself among the trees and did not stand in
one place.

text: His senses being agitated, Lord Çiva, victimized by lusty
sanskrit:
desires, began to follow Her, just as a lusty elephant follows a
she-elephant.

text: After following Her with great speed, Lord Çiva caught Her
sanskrit:
by the braid of Her hair and dragged Her near him. Although She was
unwilling, he embraced Her with his arms.

text: Being embraced by Lord Çiva like a female elephant
sanskrit:
embraced by a male, the woman, whose hair was scattered, swirled like a
snake. O King, this woman, who had large, high hips, was a woman of
yogamäyä presented by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. She released
Herself somehow or other from the fond embrace of Lord Çiva's arms and
ran away.

text: As if harassed by an enemy in the form of lusty desires,
sanskrit:
Lord Çiva followed the path of Lord Viñëu, who acts very wonderfully
and who had taken the form of Mohiné.

text: Just as a maddened bull elephant follows a female elephant
sanskrit:
who is able to conceive pregnancy, Lord Çiva followed the beautiful
woman and discharged semen, even though his discharge of semen never
goes in vain.

text: O King, wheresoever on the surface of the globe fell the
sanskrit:
semen of the great personality of Lord Çiva, mines of gold and silver
later appeared.

text: Following Mohiné, Lord Çiva went everywhere-near the
sanskrit:
shores of the rivers and lakes, near the mountains, near the forests,
near the gardens, and wherever there lived great sages.

text: O Mahäräja Parékñit, best of kings, when Lord Çiva had
sanskrit:
fully discharged semen, he could see how he himself had been victimized
by the illusion created by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus he
restrained himself from any further mäyä.

text: Thus Lord Çiva could understand his position and that of
sanskrit:
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has unlimited potencies. Having
reached this understanding, he was not at all surprised by the wonderful
way Lord Viñëu had acted upon him.

text: Seeing Lord Çiva unagitated and unashamed, Lord Viñëu
sanskrit:
[Madhusüdana] was very pleased. Thus He resumed His original form and
spoke as follows.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O best of the
sanskrit:
demigods, although you have been amply harassed because of My potency in
assuming the form of a woman, you are established in your position.
Therefore, may all good fortune be upon you.

text: My dear Lord Çambhu, who within this material world but
sanskrit:
you can surpass My illusory energy? People are generally attached to
sense enjoyment and conquered by its influence. Indeed, the influence of
material nature is very difficult for them to surmount.

text: The material, external energy [mäyä], who cooperates with
sanskrit:
Me in creation and who is manifested in the three modes of nature, will
not be able to bewilder you any longer.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, having thus been praised
sanskrit:
by the Supreme Personality, who bears the mark of Çrévatsa on His
chest, Lord Çiva circumambulated Him. Then, after taking permission
from Him, Lord Çiva returned to his abode, Kailäsa, along with his
associates.

text: O descendant of Bharata Mahäräja, Lord Çiva, in
sanskrit:
jubilation, then addressed his wife, Bhaväné, who is accepted by all
authorities as the potency of Lord Viñëu.

text: Lord Çiva said: O Goddess, you have now seen the illusory
sanskrit:
energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the unborn master
of everyone. Although I am one of the principal expansions of His
Lordship, even I was illusioned by His energy. What then is to be said
of others, who are fully dependent on mäyä?

text: When I finished performing mystic yoga for one thousand
sanskrit:
years, you asked me upon whom I was meditating. Now, here is that
Supreme Person to whom time has no entrance and who the Vedas cannot
understand.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: My dear King, the person who bore
sanskrit:
the great mountain on His back for the churning of the ocean of milk is
the same Supreme Personality of Godhead, known as Çärìga-dhanvä. I
have now described to you His prowess.

text: The endeavor of one who constantly hears or describes this
sanskrit:
narration of the churning of the ocean of milk will never be fruitless.
Indeed, chanting the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is
the only means to annihilate all sufferings in this material world.

text: Assuming the form of a young woman and thus bewildering the
sanskrit:
demons, the Supreme Personality of Godhead distributed to His devotees,

milk. Unto that Supreme Personality of Godhead, who always fulfills the
desires of His devotees, I offer my respectful obeisances.
