one. As there is no difference between the gold of a golden ornament and
the gold in a mine, there is no difference between cause and effect;
both of them are the same. Only because of ignorance do people concoct
differences and dualities. You are free from material contamination, and
since the entire cosmos is caused by You and cannot exist without You,
it is an effect of Your transcendental qualities. Thus the conception
that Brahman is true and the world false cannot be maintained.

text: Those who are known as the impersonalist Vedäntists regard
sanskrit:
You as the impersonal Brahman. Others, known as the Mémäàsaka
philosophers, regard You as religion. The Säìkhya philosophers regard
You as the transcendental person who is beyond prakåti and puruña and
who is the controller of even the demigods. The followers of the codes
of devotional service known as the Païcarätras regard You as being
endowed with nine different potencies. And the Pataïjala philosophers,
the followers of Pataïjali Muni, regard You as the supreme independent
Personality of Godhead, who has no equal or superior.

text: O my Lord, I, who am considered to be the best of the
sanskrit:
demigods, and Lord Brahmä and the great åñis, headed by Maréci, are
born of the mode of goodness. Nonetheless, we are bewildered by Your
illusory energy and cannot understand what this creation is. Aside from
us, what is to be said of others, like the demons and human beings, who
are in the base modes of material nature [rajo-guëa and tamo-guëa]?
How will they know You?

text: My Lord, You are the supreme knowledge personified. You
sanskrit:
know everything about this creation and its beginning, maintenance and
annihilation, and You know all the endeavors made by the living
entities, by which they are either implicated in this material world or
liberated from it. As the air enters the vast sky and also enters the
bodies of all moving and nonmoving entities, You are present everywhere,
and therefore You are the knower of all.

text: My Lord, I have seen all kinds of incarnations You have
sanskrit:
exhibited by Your transcendental qualities, and now that You have
appeared as a beautiful young woman, I wish to see that form of Your
Lordship.

text: My Lord, we have come here desiring to see that form of
sanskrit:
Your Lordship which You showed to the demons to captivate them
completely and in this way enable the demigods to drink nectar. I am
very eager to see that form.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: When Lord Viñëu was thus
sanskrit:
requested by Lord Çiva, who carries a trident in his hand, He smiled
with gravity and replied to Lord Çiva as follows.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: When the demons
sanskrit:
took away the jug of nectar, I assumed the form of a beautiful woman to
bewilder them by directly cheating them and thus to act in the interest
of the demigods.

text: O best of the demigods, I shall now show you My form that
sanskrit:
is very much appreciated by those who are lusty. Since you want to see
that form, I shall reveal it in your presence.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: After speaking in this way,
sanskrit:
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viñëu, immediately disappeared,
and Lord Çiva remained there with Umä, looking for Him all around with
moving eyes.

text: Thereafter, in a nice forest nearby, full of trees with
sanskrit:
reddish-pink leaves and varieties of flowers, Lord Çiva saw a beautiful
woman playing with a ball. Her hips were covered with a shining sari and
ornamented with a belt.

text: Because the ball was falling down and bouncing up, as She
sanskrit:
played with it Her breasts trembled, and because of the weight of those
breasts and Her heavy flower garlands, Her waist appeared to be all but
breaking at every step, as Her two soft feet, which were reddish like
coral, moved here and there.

text: The woman's face was decorated by broad, beautiful,
sanskrit:
restless eyes, which moved as the ball bounced here and there from Her
hand. The two brilliant earrings on Her ears decorated Her shining
cheeks like bluish reflections, and the hair scattered on Her face made
Her even more beautiful to see.

text: As She played with the ball, the sari covering Her body
sanskrit:
became loose, and Her hair scattered. She tried to bind Her hair with
Her beautiful left hand, and at the same time She played with the ball
by striking it with Her right hand. This was so attractive that the
Supreme Lord, by His internal potency, in this way captivated everyone.

text: While Lord Çiva observed the beautiful woman playing with
sanskrit:
the ball, She sometimes glanced at him and slightly smiled in
bashfulness. As he looked at the beautiful woman and She watched him, he
forgot both himself and Umä, his most beautiful wife, as well as his
associates nearby.

text: When the ball leaped from Her hand and fell at a distance,
sanskrit:
the woman began to follow it, but as Lord Çiva observed these
activities, a breeze suddenly blew away the fine dress and belt that
covered her.

text: Thus Lord Çiva saw the woman, every part of whose body was
sanskrit:
beautifully formed, and the beautiful woman also looked at him.
Therefore, thinking that She was attracted to him, Lord Çiva became
very much attracted to Her.

text: Lord Çiva, his good sense taken away by the woman because
sanskrit:
of lusty desires to enjoy with Her, became so mad for Her that even in
the presence of Bhaväné he did not hesitate to approach Her.

text: The beautiful woman was already naked, and when She saw
sanskrit:
Lord Çiva coming toward Her, She became extremely bashful. Thus She
kept smiling, but She hid Herself among the trees and did not stand in
one place.

text: His senses being agitated, Lord Çiva, victimized by lusty
sanskrit:
desires, began to follow Her, just as a lusty elephant follows a
she-elephant.

text: After following Her with great speed, Lord Çiva caught Her
sanskrit:
by the braid of Her hair and dragged Her near him. Although She was
unwilling, he embraced Her with his arms.

text: Being embraced by Lord Çiva like a female elephant
sanskrit:
embraced by a male, the woman, whose hair was scattered, swirled like a
snake. O King, this woman, who had large, high hips, was a woman of
yogamäyä presented by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. She released
Herself somehow or other from the fond embrace of Lord Çiva's arms and
ran away.

text: As if harassed by an enemy in the form of lusty desires,
sanskrit:
Lord Çiva followed the path of Lord Viñëu, who acts very wonderfully
and who had taken the form of Mohiné.

text: Just as a maddened bull elephant follows a female elephant
sanskrit:
who is able to conceive pregnancy, Lord Çiva followed the beautiful
woman and discharged semen, even though his discharge of semen never
goes in vain.

text: O King, wheresoever on the surface of the globe fell the
sanskrit:
semen of the great personality of Lord Çiva, mines of gold and silver
later appeared.

text: Following Mohiné, Lord Çiva went everywhere-near the
sanskrit:
shores of the rivers and lakes, near the mountains, near the forests,
near the gardens, and wherever there lived great sages.

text: O Mahäräja Parékñit, best of kings, when Lord Çiva had
sanskrit:
fully discharged semen, he could see how he himself had been victimized
by the illusion created by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Thus he
restrained himself from any further mäyä.

text: Thus Lord Çiva could understand his position and that of
sanskrit:
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has unlimited potencies. Having
reached this understanding, he was not at all surprised by the wonderful
way Lord Viñëu had acted upon him.

text: Seeing Lord Çiva unagitated and unashamed, Lord Viñëu
sanskrit:
[Madhusüdana] was very pleased. Thus He resumed His original form and
spoke as follows.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O best of the
sanskrit:
demigods, although you have been amply harassed because of My potency in
assuming the form of a woman, you are established in your position.
Therefore, may all good fortune be upon you.

text: My dear Lord Çambhu, who within this material world but
sanskrit:
you can surpass My illusory energy? People are generally attached to
sense enjoyment and conquered by its influence. Indeed, the influence of
material nature is very difficult for them to surmount.

text: The material, external energy [mäyä], who cooperates with
sanskrit:
Me in creation and who is manifested in the three modes of nature, will
not be able to bewilder you any longer.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, having thus been praised
sanskrit:
by the Supreme Personality, who bears the mark of Çrévatsa on His
chest, Lord Çiva circumambulated Him. Then, after taking permission
from Him, Lord Çiva returned to his abode, Kailäsa, along with his
associates.

text: O descendant of Bharata Mahäräja, Lord Çiva, in
sanskrit:
jubilation, then addressed his wife, Bhaväné, who is accepted by all
authorities as the potency of Lord Viñëu.

text: Lord Çiva said: O Goddess, you have now seen the illusory
sanskrit:
energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the unborn master
of everyone. Although I am one of the principal expansions of His
Lordship, even I was illusioned by His energy. What then is to be said
of others, who are fully dependent on mäyä?

text: When I finished performing mystic yoga for one thousand
sanskrit:
years, you asked me upon whom I was meditating. Now, here is that
Supreme Person to whom time has no entrance and who the Vedas cannot
understand.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: My dear King, the person who bore
sanskrit:
the great mountain on His back for the churning of the ocean of milk is
the same Supreme Personality of Godhead, known as Çärìga-dhanvä. I
have now described to you His prowess.

text: The endeavor of one who constantly hears or describes this
sanskrit:
narration of the churning of the ocean of milk will never be fruitless.
Indeed, chanting the glories of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is
the only means to annihilate all sufferings in this material world.

text: Assuming the form of a young woman and thus bewildering the
sanskrit:
demons, the Supreme Personality of Godhead distributed to His devotees,
the demigods, the nectar produced from the churning of the ocean of
milk. Unto that Supreme Personality of Godhead, who always fulfills the
desires of His devotees, I offer my respectful obeisances.
Translations 1-47

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: The present Manu, who is named
sanskrit:
Çräddhadeva, is the son of Vivasvän, the predominating deity on the
sun planet. Çräddhadeva is the seventh Manu. Now please hear from me
as I describe his sons.

text: O King Parékñit, among the ten sons of Manu are
sanskrit:
Ikñväku, Nabhaga, Dhåñöa, Çaryäti, Nariñyanta and Näbhäga. The
seventh son is known as Diñöa. Then come Tarüña and Påñadhra, and
the tenth son is known as Vasumän.

text: In this manvantara, O King, the Ädityas, the Vasus, the
sanskrit:
Rudras, the Viçvedevas, the Maruts, the two Açviné-kumära brothers
and the Åbhus are the demigods. Their head king [Indra] is Purandara.

text: Kaçyapa, Atri, Vasiñöha, Viçvämitra, Gautama, Jamadagni
sanskrit: and Bharadväja are known as the seven sages.

text: In this manvantara, the Supreme Personality of Godhead
sanskrit:
appeared as the youngest of all the Ädityas, known as Vämana, the
dwarf. His father was Kaçyapa and His mother Aditi.

text: I have briefly explained to you the position of the seven
sanskrit:
Manus. Now I shall describe the future Manus, along with the
incarnations of Lord Viñëu.

text: O King, I have previously described [in the Sixth Canto] the
sanskrit:
two daughters of Viçvakarmä, named Saàjïä and Chäyä, who were the
first two wives of Vivasvän.

text: It is said that the sun-god had a third wife, named
sanskrit:
Vaòavä. Of the three wives, the wife named Saàjïä had three
children-Yama, Yamé and Çräddhadeva. Now let me describe the children
of Chäyä.

text: Chäyä had a son named Sävarëi and a daughter named
sanskrit:
Tapaté, who later became the wife of King Saàvaraëa. Chäyä's third
child is known as Çanaiçcara [Saturn]. Vaòavä gave birth to two
sons, namely the Açviné brothers.

text: O King, when the period of the eighth Manu arrives,
sanskrit:
Sävarëi will become the Manu. Nirmoka and Virajaska will be among his
sons.

text: In the period of the eighth Manu, among the demigods will
sanskrit:
be the Sutapäs, the Virajas and the Amåtaprabhas. The king of the
demigods, Indra, will be Bali Mahäräja, the son of Virocana.

text: Bali Mahäräja gave a gift of three paces of land to Lord
sanskrit:
Viñëu, and because of this charity he lost all the three worlds.
Later, however, when Lord Viñëu is pleased because of Bali's giving
everything to Him, Bali Mahäräja will achieve the perfection of life.

text: With great affection, the Personality of Godhead bound Bali
sanskrit:
and then installed him in the kingdom of Sutala, which is more opulent
than the heavenly planets. Mahäräja Bali now resides on that planet
and is more comfortably situated than Indra.

text: O King, during the eighth manvantara, the great
sanskrit:
personalities Gälava, Déptimän, Paraçuräma, Açvatthämä,
Kåpäcärya, Åñyaçåìga and our father, Vyäsadeva, the incarnation
of Näräyaëa, will be the seven sages. For the present, they are all
residing in their respective äçramas.

text: In the eighth manvantara, the greatly powerful Personality
sanskrit:
of Godhead Särvabhauma will take birth. His father will be Devaguhya,
and His mother will be Sarasvaté. He will take the kingdom away from
Purandara [Lord Indra] and give it to Bali Mahäräja.

text: O King, the ninth Manu will be Dakña-sävarëi, who is
sanskrit: born of Varuëa. Among his sons will be Bhütaketu, and Déptaketu.

text: In this ninth manvantara, the Päras and Marécigarbhas
sanskrit:
will be among the demigods. The king of heaven, Indra, will be named
Adbhuta, and Dyutimän will be among the seven sages.

text: Åñabhadeva, a partial incarnation of the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, will take birth from his father, Äyuñmän, and
his mother, Ambudhärä. He will enable the Indra named Adbhuta to enjoy
the opulence of the three worlds.

text: The son of Upaçloka known as Brahma-sävarëi will be the
sanskrit:
tenth Manu. Bhüriñeëa will be among his sons, and the brähmaëas
headed by Haviñmän will be the seven sages.

text: Haviñmän, Sukåta, Satya, Jaya, Mürti and others will be
sanskrit:
the seven sages, the Suväsanas and Viruddhas will be among the
demigods, and Çambhu will be their king, Indra.

text: In the home of Viçvasrañöä, a plenary portion of the
sanskrit:
Supreme Personality of Godhead will appear from the womb of Viñücé as
the incarnation known as Viñvaksena. He will make friends with Çambhu.

text: In the eleventh manvantara, the Manu will be
sanskrit:
Dharma-sävarëi, who will be extremely learned in spiritual knowledge.
From him there will come ten sons, headed by Satyadharma.

text: The Vihaìgamas, Kämagamas, Nirväëarucis and others will
sanskrit:
be the demigods. The king of the demigods, Indra, will be Vaidhåta, and
the seven sages will be headed by Aruëa.

text: The son of Äryaka known as Dharmasetu, a partial
sanskrit:
incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, will appear from the
womb of Vaidhåtä, the wife of Äryaka, and will rule the three worlds.

text: O King, the twelfth Manu will be named Rudra-sävarëi.
sanskrit: Devavän, Upadeva and Devaçreñöha will be among his sons.

text: In this manvantara, the name of Indra will be Åtadhämä,
sanskrit:
and the demigods will be headed by the Haritas. Among the sages will be
Tapomürti, Tapasvé and Ägnédhraka.

text: From the mother named Sunåtä and the father named
sanskrit:
Satyasahä will come Svadhämä, a partial incarnation of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead. He will rule that manvantara.

text: The thirteenth Manu will be named Deva-sävarëi, and he
sanskrit:
will be very advanced in spiritual knowledge. Among his sons will be
Citrasena and Vicitra.

text: In the thirteenth manvantara, the Sukarmäs and Suträmas
sanskrit:
will be among the demigods, Divaspati will be the king of heaven, and
Nirmoka and Tattvadarça will be among the seven sages.

text: The son of Devahotra known as Yogeçvara will appear as a
sanskrit:
partial incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. His mother's
name will be Båhaté. He will perform activities for the welfare of
Divaspati.

text: The name of the fourteenth Manu will be Indra-sävarëi. He
sanskrit: will have sons like Uru, Gambhéra and Budha.

text: The Pavitras and Cäkñuñas will be among the demigods,
sanskrit:
and Çuci will be Indra, the king of heaven. Agni, Bähu, Çuci,
Çuddha, Mägadha and others of great austerity will be the seven sages.

text: O King Parékñit, in the fourteenth manvantara the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead will appear from the womb of Vitänä, and His
father's name will be Saträyaëa. This incarnation will be celebrated
as Båhadbhänu, and He will administer spiritual activities.

text: O King, I have now described to you the fourteen Manus
sanskrit:
appearing in the past, present and future. The total duration of time
ruled by these Manus is one thousand yuga cycles. This is called a
kalpa, or one day of Lord Brahmä.

text: Kaçyapa, Atri, Vasiñöha, Viçvämitra, Gautama, Jamadagni
sanskrit: and Bharadväja are known as the seven sages.

text: In this manvantara, the Supreme Personality of Godhead
sanskrit:
appeared as the youngest of all the Ädityas, known as Vämana, the
dwarf. His father was Kaçyapa and His mother Aditi.

text: I have briefly explained to you the position of the seven
sanskrit:
Manus. Now I shall describe the future Manus, along with the
incarnations of Lord Viñëu.

text: O King, I have previously described [in the Sixth Canto] the
sanskrit:
two daughters of Viçvakarmä, named Saàjïä and Chäyä, who were the
first two wives of Vivasvän.

text: It is said that the sun-god had a third wife, named
sanskrit:
Vaòavä. Of the three wives, the wife named Saàjïä had three
children-Yama, Yamé and Çräddhadeva. Now let me describe the children
of Chäyä.

text: Chäyä had a son named Sävarëi and a daughter named
sanskrit:
Tapaté, who later became the wife of King Saàvaraëa. Chäyä's third
child is known as Çanaiçcara [Saturn]. Vaòavä gave birth to two
sons, namely the Açviné brothers.

text: O King, when the period of the eighth Manu arrives,
sanskrit:
Sävarëi will become the Manu. Nirmoka and Virajaska will be among his
sons.

text: In the period of the eighth Manu, among the demigods will
sanskrit:
be the Sutapäs, the Virajas and the Amåtaprabhas. The king of the
demigods, Indra, will be Bali Mahäräja, the son of Virocana.

text: Bali Mahäräja gave a gift of three paces of land to Lord
sanskrit:
Viñëu, and because of this charity he lost all the three worlds.
Later, however, when Lord Viñëu is pleased because of Bali's giving
everything to Him, Bali Mahäräja will achieve the perfection of life.

text: With great affection, the Personality of Godhead bound Bali
sanskrit:
and then installed him in the kingdom of Sutala, which is more opulent
than the heavenly planets. Mahäräja Bali now resides on that planet
and is more comfortably situated than Indra.

text: O King, during the eighth manvantara, the great
sanskrit:
personalities Gälava, Déptimän, Paraçuräma, Açvatthämä,
Kåpäcärya, Åñyaçåìga and our father, Vyäsadeva, the incarnation
of Näräyaëa, will be the seven sages. For the present, they are all
residing in their respective äçramas.

text: In the eighth manvantara, the greatly powerful Personality
sanskrit:
of Godhead Särvabhauma will take birth. His father will be Devaguhya,
and His mother will be Sarasvaté. He will take the kingdom away from
Purandara [Lord Indra] and give it to Bali Mahäräja.

text: O King, the ninth Manu will be Dakña-sävarëi, who is
sanskrit: born of Varuëa. Among his sons will be Bhütaketu, and Déptaketu.

text: In this ninth manvantara, the Päras and Marécigarbhas
sanskrit:
will be among the demigods. The king of heaven, Indra, will be named
Adbhuta, and Dyutimän will be among the seven sages.

text: Åñabhadeva, a partial incarnation of the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, will take birth from his father, Äyuñmän, and
his mother, Ambudhärä. He will enable the Indra named Adbhuta to enjoy
the opulence of the three worlds.

text: The son of Upaçloka known as Brahma-sävarëi will be the
sanskrit:
tenth Manu. Bhüriñeëa will be among his sons, and the brähmaëas
headed by Haviñmän will be the seven sages.

text: Haviñmän, Sukåta, Satya, Jaya, Mürti and others will be
sanskrit:
the seven sages, the Suväsanas and Viruddhas will be among the
demigods, and Çambhu will be their king, Indra.

text: In the home of Viçvasrañöä, a plenary portion of the
sanskrit:
Supreme Personality of Godhead will appear from the womb of Viñücé as
the incarnation known as Viñvaksena. He will make friends with Çambhu.

text: In the eleventh manvantara, the Manu will be
sanskrit:
Dharma-sävarëi, who will be extremely learned in spiritual knowledge.
From him there will come ten sons, headed by Satyadharma.

text: The Vihaìgamas, Kämagamas, Nirväëarucis and others will
sanskrit:
be the demigods. The king of the demigods, Indra, will be Vaidhåta, and
the seven sages will be headed by Aruëa.

text: The son of Äryaka known as Dharmasetu, a partial
sanskrit:
incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, will appear from the
womb of Vaidhåtä, the wife of Äryaka, and will rule the three worlds.

text: O King, the twelfth Manu will be named Rudra-sävarëi.
sanskrit: Devavän, Upadeva and Devaçreñöha will be among his sons.

text: In this manvantara, the name of Indra will be Åtadhämä,
sanskrit:
and the demigods will be headed by the Haritas. Among the sages will be
Tapomürti, Tapasvé and Ägnédhraka.

text: From the mother named Sunåtä and the father named
sanskrit:
Satyasahä will come Svadhämä, a partial incarnation of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead. He will rule that manvantara.

text: The thirteenth Manu will be named Deva-sävarëi, and he
sanskrit:
will be very advanced in spiritual knowledge. Among his sons will be
Citrasena and Vicitra.

text: In the thirteenth manvantara, the Sukarmäs and Suträmas
sanskrit:
will be among the demigods, Divaspati will be the king of heaven, and
Nirmoka and Tattvadarça will be among the seven sages.

text: The son of Devahotra known as Yogeçvara will appear as a
sanskrit:
partial incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. His mother's
name will be Båhaté. He will perform activities for the welfare of
Divaspati.

text: The name of the fourteenth Manu will be Indra-sävarëi. He
sanskrit: will have sons like Uru, Gambhéra and Budha.

text: The Pavitras and Cäkñuñas will be among the demigods,
sanskrit:
and Çuci will be Indra, the king of heaven. Agni, Bähu, Çuci,
Çuddha, Mägadha and others of great austerity will be the seven sages.

text: O King Parékñit, in the fourteenth manvantara the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead will appear from the womb of Vitänä, and His
father's name will be Saträyaëa. This incarnation will be celebrated
as Båhadbhänu, and He will administer spiritual activities.

text: O King, I have now described to you the fourteen Manus
sanskrit:
appearing in the past, present and future. The total duration of time
ruled by these Manus is one thousand yuga cycles. This is called a
kalpa, or one day of Lord Brahmä.
Translations 1-36

text: Mahäräja Parékñit inquired: O most opulent Çukadeva
sanskrit:
Gosvämé, please explain to me how Manu and the others in each
manvantara are engaged in their respective duties, and by whose order
they are so engaged.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: The Manus, the sons of Manu, the
sanskrit:
great sages, the Indras and all the demigods, O King, are appointed by
the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His various incarnations such as
Yajïa.

text: O King, I have already described to you various incarnations
sanskrit:
of the Lord, such as Yajïa. The Manus and others are chosen by these
incarnations, under whose direction they conduct the universal affairs.

text: At the end of every four yugas, the great saintly persons,
sanskrit:
upon seeing that the eternal occupational duties of mankind have been
misused, reestablish the principles of religion.

text: Thereafter, O King, the Manus, being fully engaged according
sanskrit:
to the instructions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, directly
reestablish the principles of occupational duty in its full four parts.

text: To enjoy the results of sacrifices [yajïas], the rulers of
sanskrit:
the world, namely the sons and grandsons of Manu, discharge the orders
of the Supreme Personality of Godhead until the end of Manu's reign. The
demigods also share the results of these sacrifices.

text: Indra, King of heaven, receiving benedictions from the
sanskrit:
Supreme Personality of Godhead and thus enjoying highly developed
opulences, maintains the living entities all over the three worlds by
pouring sufficient rain on all the planets.

text: In every yuga, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari,
sanskrit:
assumes the form of Siddhas such as Sanaka to preach transcendental
knowledge, He assumes the form of great saintly persons such as
Yäjïavalkya to teach the way of karma, and He assumes the form of
great yogés such as Dattätreya to teach the system of mystic yoga.

text: In the form of Prajäpati Maréci, the Supreme Personality
sanskrit:
of Godhead creates progeny; becoming the king, He kills the thieves and
rogues; and in the form of time, He annihilates everything. All the
different qualities of material existence should be understood to be
qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: People in general are bewildered by the illusory energy,
sanskrit:
and therefore they try to find the Absolute Truth, the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, through various types of research and
philosophical speculation. Nonetheless, they are unable to see the
Supreme Lord.

text: In one kalpa, or one day of Brahmä, there take place the
sanskrit:
many changes called vikalpas. O King, all of these have been previously
described to you by me. Learned scholars who know the past, present and
future have ascertained that in one day of Brahmä there are fourteen
Manus.

text: Mahäräja Parékñit inquired: The Supreme Personality of
sanskrit:
Godhead is the proprietor of everything. Why did He beg three paces of
land from Bali Mahäräja like a poor man, and when He got the gift for
which He had begged, why did He nonetheless arrest Bali Mahäräja? I am
very much anxious to know the mystery of these contradictions.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, when Bali Mahäräja lost
sanskrit:
all his opulence and died in the fight, Çukräcärya, a descendant of
Bhågu Muni, brought him back to life. Because of this, the great soul
Bali Mahäräja became a disciple of Çukräcärya and began to serve
him with great faith, offering everything he had.

text: The brähmaëa descendants of Bhågu Muni were very pleased
sanskrit:
with Bali Mahäräja, who desired to conquer the kingdom of Indra.
Therefore, after purifying him and properly bathing him according to
regulative principles, they engaged him in performing the yajïa known
as Viçvajit.

text: When ghee [clarified butter] was offered in the fire of
sanskrit:
sacrifice, there appeared from the fire a celestial chariot covered with
gold and silk. There also appeared yellow horses like those of Indra,
and a flag marked with a lion.

text: A gilded bow, two quivers of infallible arrows, and
sanskrit:
celestial armor also appeared. Bali Mahäräja's grandfather Prahläda
Mahäräja offered Bali a garland of flowers that would never fade, and
Çukräcärya gave him a conchshell.

text: When Mahäräja Bali had thus performed the special
sanskrit:
ritualistic ceremony advised by the brähmaëas and had received, by
their grace, the equipment for fighting, he circumambulated the
brähmaëas and offered them obeisances. He also saluted Prahläda
Mahäräja and offered obeisances to him.

text: Then, after getting on the chariot given by Çukräcärya,
sanskrit:
Bali Mahäräja, decorated with a nice garland, put protective armor on
his body, equipped himself with a bow, and took up a sword and a quiver
of arrows. When he sat down on the seat of the chariot, his arms
decorated with golden bangles and his ears with sapphire earrings, he
shone like a worshipable fire.

text: When he assembled with his own soldiers and the demon
sanskrit:
chiefs, who were equal to him in strength, opulence and beauty, they
appeared as if they would swallow the sky and burn all directions with
their vision. After thus gathering the demoniac soldiers, Bali
Mahäräja departed for the opulent capital of Indra. Indeed, he seemed
to make the entire surface of the world tremble.

text: King Indra's city was full of pleasing orchards and
sanskrit:
gardens, such as the Nandana garden. Because of the weight of the
flowers, leaves and fruit, the branches of the eternally existing trees
were bending down. The gardens were visited by pairs of chirping birds
and singing bees. The entire atmosphere was celestial.

text: Beautiful women protected by the demigods sported in the
sanskrit:
gardens, which had lotus ponds full of swans, cranes, cakraväkas and
ducks.

text: The city was surrounded by trenches full of Ganges water,
sanskrit:
known as Äkäça-gaìgä, and by a high wall, which was the color of
fire. Upon this wall were parapets for fighting.

text: The doors were made of solid gold plates, and the gates
sanskrit:
were of excellent marble. These were linked by various public roads. The
entire city had been constructed by Viçvakarmä.

text: The city was full of courtyards, wide roads, assembly
sanskrit:
houses, and not less than one hundred million airplanes. The crossroads
were made of pearl, and there were sitting places made of diamond and
coral.

text: Everlastingly beautiful and youthful women, who were
sanskrit:
dressed with clean garments, glittered in the city like fires with
flames. They all possessed the quality of çyämä.

text: The breezes blowing in the streets of the city bore the
sanskrit:
fragrance of the flowers falling from the hair of the women of the
demigods.

text: Apsaräs passed on the streets, which were covered with the
sanskrit:
white, fragrant smoke of aguru incense emanating from windows with
golden filigree.

text: The city was shaded by canopies decorated with pearls, and
sanskrit:
the domes of the palaces had flags of pearl and gold. The city always
resounded with the vibrations of peacocks, pigeons and bees, and above
the city flew airplanes full of beautiful women who constantly chanted
auspicious songs that were very pleasing to the ear.

text: The city was filled with the sounds of mådaìgas,
sanskrit:
conchshells, kettledrums, flutes and well-tuned stringed instruments all
playing in concert. There was constant dancing and the Gandharvas sang.
The combined beauty of Indrapuré defeated beauty personified.

text: No one who was sinful, envious, violent toward other living
sanskrit:
entities, cunning, falsely proud, lusty or greedy could enter that city.
The people who lived there were all devoid of these faults.

text: Bali Mahäräja, who was the commander of numberless
sanskrit:
soldiers, gathered his soldiers outside this abode of Indra and attacked
it from all directions. He sounded the conchshell given him by his
spiritual master, Çukräcärya, thus creating a fearful situation for
the women protected by Indra.

text: Seeing Bali Mahäräja's indefatigable endeavor and
sanskrit:
understanding his motive, King Indra, along with the other demigods,
approached his spiritual master, Båhaspati, and spoke as follows.

text: My lord, our old enemy Bali Mahäräja now has new
sanskrit:
enthusiasm, and he has obtained such astonishing power that we think
that perhaps we cannot resist his prowess.

text: No one anywhere can counteract this military arrangement of
sanskrit:
Bali's. It now appears that Bali is trying to drink up the entire
universe with his mouth, lick up the ten directions with his tongue, and
raise fire in every direction with his eyes. Indeed, he has arisen like
the annihilating fire known as saàvartaka.

text: Kindly inform me. What is the cause for Bali Mahäräja's
sanskrit:
strength, endeavor, influence and victory? How has he become so
enthusiastic?

text: Båhaspati, the spiritual master of the demigods, said: O
sanskrit:
Indra, I know the cause for your enemy's becoming so powerful. The
brähmaëa descendants of Bhågu Muni, being pleased by Bali Mahäräja,
their disciple, endowed him with such extraordinary power.

text: Neither you nor your men can conquer the most powerful
sanskrit:
Bali. Indeed, no one but the Supreme Personality of Godhead can conquer
him, for he is now equipped with the supreme spiritual power
[brahma-tejas]. As no one can stand before Yamaräja, no one can now
stand before Bali Mahäräja.

text: Therefore, waiting until the situation of your enemies is
sanskrit:
reversed, you should all leave this heavenly planet and go elsewhere,
where you will not be seen.

text: Bali Mahäräja has now become extremely powerful because
sanskrit:
of the benedictions given him by the brähmaëas, but when he later
insults the brähmaëas, he will be vanquished, along with his friends
and assistants.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: The demigods, being thus
sanskrit:
advised by Båhaspati for their benefit, immediately accepted his words.
Assuming forms according to their desire, they left the heavenly kingdom
and scattered, without being observed by the demons.

text: When the demigods had disappeared, Bali Mahäräja, the son
sanskrit:
of Virocana, entered the heavenly kingdom, and from there he brought the
three worlds under his control.

text: The brähmaëa descendants of Bhågu, being very pleased
sanskrit:
with their disciple, who had conquered the entire universe, now engaged
him in performing one hundred açvamedha sacrifices.

text: When Bali Mahäräja performed these sacrifices, he gained
sanskrit:
a great reputation in all directions, throughout the three worlds. Thus
he shone in his position, like the brilliant moon in the sky.

text: Because of the favor of the brähmaëas, the great soul
sanskrit:
Bali Mahäräja, thinking himself very satisfied, became very opulent
and prosperous and began to enjoy the kingdom.

fragrance of the flowers falling from the hair of the women of the
demigods.

text: Apsaräs passed on the streets, which were covered with the
sanskrit:
white, fragrant smoke of aguru incense emanating from windows with
golden filigree.

text: The city was shaded by canopies decorated with pearls, and
sanskrit:
the domes of the palaces had flags of pearl and gold. The city always
resounded with the vibrations of peacocks, pigeons and bees, and above
the city flew airplanes full of beautiful women who constantly chanted
auspicious songs that were very pleasing to the ear.

text: The city was filled with the sounds of mådaìgas,
sanskrit:
conchshells, kettledrums, flutes and well-tuned stringed instruments all
playing in concert. There was constant dancing and the Gandharvas sang.
The combined beauty of Indrapuré defeated beauty personified.

text: No one who was sinful, envious, violent toward other living
sanskrit:
entities, cunning, falsely proud, lusty or greedy could enter that city.
The people who lived there were all devoid of these faults.

text: Bali Mahäräja, who was the commander of numberless
sanskrit:
soldiers, gathered his soldiers outside this abode of Indra and attacked
it from all directions. He sounded the conchshell given him by his
spiritual master, Çukräcärya, thus creating a fearful situation for
the women protected by Indra.

text: Seeing Bali Mahäräja's indefatigable endeavor and
sanskrit:
understanding his motive, King Indra, along with the other demigods,
approached his spiritual master, Båhaspati, and spoke as follows.

text: My lord, our old enemy Bali Mahäräja now has new
sanskrit:
enthusiasm, and he has obtained such astonishing power that we think
that perhaps we cannot resist his prowess.

text: No one anywhere can counteract this military arrangement of
sanskrit:
Bali's. It now appears that Bali is trying to drink up the entire
universe with his mouth, lick up the ten directions with his tongue, and
raise fire in every direction with his eyes. Indeed, he has arisen like
the annihilating fire known as saàvartaka.

text: Kindly inform me. What is the cause for Bali Mahäräja's
sanskrit:
strength, endeavor, influence and victory? How has he become so
enthusiastic?

text: Båhaspati, the spiritual master of the demigods, said: O
sanskrit:
Indra, I know the cause for your enemy's becoming so powerful. The
brähmaëa descendants of Bhågu Muni, being pleased by Bali Mahäräja,
their disciple, endowed him with such extraordinary power.

text: Neither you nor your men can conquer the most powerful
sanskrit:
Bali. Indeed, no one but the Supreme Personality of Godhead can conquer
him, for he is now equipped with the supreme spiritual power
[brahma-tejas]. As no one can stand before Yamaräja, no one can now
stand before Bali Mahäräja.

text: Therefore, waiting until the situation of your enemies is
sanskrit:
reversed, you should all leave this heavenly planet and go elsewhere,
where you will not be seen.

text: Bali Mahäräja has now become extremely powerful because
sanskrit:
of the benedictions given him by the brähmaëas, but when he later
insults the brähmaëas, he will be vanquished, along with his friends
and assistants.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: The demigods, being thus
sanskrit:
advised by Båhaspati for their benefit, immediately accepted his words.
Assuming forms according to their desire, they left the heavenly kingdom
and scattered, without being observed by the demons.

text: When the demigods had disappeared, Bali Mahäräja, the son
sanskrit:
of Virocana, entered the heavenly kingdom, and from there he brought the
three worlds under his control.

text: The brähmaëa descendants of Bhågu, being very pleased
sanskrit:
with their disciple, who had conquered the entire universe, now engaged
him in performing one hundred açvamedha sacrifices.

text: When Bali Mahäräja performed these sacrifices, he gained
sanskrit:
a great reputation in all directions, throughout the three worlds. Thus
he shone in his position, like the brilliant moon in the sky.

text: Because of the favor of the brähmaëas, the great soul
sanskrit:
Bali Mahäräja, thinking himself very satisfied, became very opulent
and prosperous and began to enjoy the kingdom.
Bali Mahäräja Conquers the Heavenly Planets
•  SB 8.15.1-2 - Mahäräja Parékñit inquired: The Supreme
Personality of Godhead is the proprietor of everything. Why did He beg
three paces of land from Bali Mahäräja like a poor man, and when He
got the gift for which He had begged, why did He nonetheless arrest Bali
Mahäräja? I am very much anxious to know the mystery of these
contradictions.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, when Bali Mahäräja lost
sanskrit:
all his opulence and died in the fight, Çukräcärya, a descendant of
Bhågu Muni, brought him back to life. Because of this, the great soul
Bali Mahäräja became a disciple of Çukräcärya and began to serve
him with great faith, offering everything he had.

text: The brähmaëa descendants of Bhågu Muni were very pleased
sanskrit:
with Bali Mahäräja, who desired to conquer the kingdom of Indra.
Therefore, after purifying him and properly bathing him according to
regulative principles, they engaged him in performing the yajïa known
as Viçvajit.

text: When ghee [clarified butter] was offered in the fire of
sanskrit:
sacrifice, there appeared from the fire a celestial chariot covered with
gold and silk. There also appeared yellow horses like those of Indra,
and a flag marked with a lion.

text: A gilded bow, two quivers of infallible arrows, and
sanskrit:
celestial armor also appeared. Bali Mahäräja's grandfather Prahläda
Mahäräja offered Bali a garland of flowers that would never fade, and
Çukräcärya gave him a conchshell.

text: When Mahäräja Bali had thus performed the special
sanskrit:
ritualistic ceremony advised by the brähmaëas and had received, by
their grace, the equipment for fighting, he circumambulated the
brähmaëas and offered them obeisances. He also saluted Prahläda
Mahäräja and offered obeisances to him.

text: Then, after getting on the chariot given by Çukräcärya,
sanskrit:
Bali Mahäräja, decorated with a nice garland, put protective armor on
his body, equipped himself with a bow, and took up a sword and a quiver
of arrows. When he sat down on the seat of the chariot, his arms
decorated with golden bangles and his ears with sapphire earrings, he
shone like a worshipable fire.

text: When he assembled with his own soldiers and the demon
sanskrit:
chiefs, who were equal to him in strength, opulence and beauty, they
appeared as if they would swallow the sky and burn all directions with
their vision. After thus gathering the demoniac soldiers, Bali
Mahäräja departed for the opulent capital of Indra. Indeed, he seemed
to make the entire surface of the world tremble.

text: King Indra's city was full of pleasing orchards and
sanskrit:
gardens, such as the Nandana garden. Because of the weight of the
flowers, leaves and fruit, the branches of the eternally existing trees
were bending down. The gardens were visited by pairs of chirping birds

text: Beautiful women protected by the demigods sported in the
sanskrit:
gardens, which had lotus ponds full of swans, cranes, cakraväkas and
ducks.

text: The city was surrounded by trenches full of Ganges water,
sanskrit:
known as Äkäça-gaìgä, and by a high wall, which was the color of

text: The doors were made of solid gold plates, and the gates
sanskrit:
were of excellent marble. These were linked by various public roads. The
entire city had been constructed by Viçvakarmä.

text: The city was full of courtyards, wide roads, assembly
sanskrit:
houses, and not less than one hundred million airplanes. The crossroads
were made of pearl, and there were sitting places made of diamond and
coral.

text: Everlastingly beautiful and youthful women, who were
sanskrit:
dressed with clean garments, glittered in the city like fires with
flames. They all possessed the quality of çyämä.

text: The breezes blowing in the streets of the city bore the
sanskrit:
fragrance of the flowers falling from the hair of the women of the

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, when Aditi's sons, the
sanskrit:
demigods, had thus disappeared from heaven and the demons had occupied
their places, Aditi began lamenting, as if she had no protector.

text: After many, many days, the great powerful sage Kaçyapa Muni
sanskrit:
arose from a trance of meditation and returned home to see the äçrama
of Aditi neither jubilant nor festive.

text: O best of the Kurus, when Kaçyapa Muni had been properly
sanskrit:
received and welcomed, he took his seat and then spoke as follows to his
wife, Aditi, who was very morose.

text: O most gentle one, I wonder whether anything inauspicious
sanskrit:
has now taken place in regard to religious principles, the brähmaëas
or the people in general, who are subject to the whims of death.

text: O my wife, who are very much attached to household life, if
sanskrit:
the principles of religion, economic development and satisfaction of the
senses are properly followed in household life, one's activities are as
good as those of a transcendentalist. I wonder whether there have been
any discrepancies in following these principles.

text: I wonder whether because of being too attached to the
sanskrit:
members of your family, you failed to properly receive uninvited guests,
who therefore were not welcomed and went away.

text: Homes from which guests go away without having been received
sanskrit:
even with an offering of a little water are like those holes in the
field which are the homes of jackals.

text: O chaste and auspicious woman, when I left home for other
sanskrit:
places, were you in so much anxiety that you did not offer oblations of
ghee into the fire?

text: By worshiping the fire and the brähmaëas, a householder
sanskrit:
can achieve the desired goal of residing in the higher planets, for the
sacrificial fire and the brähmaëas are to be considered the mouth of
Lord Viñëu, who is the Supersoul of all the demigods.

text: O great-minded lady, are all your sons faring well? Seeing
sanskrit:
your withered face, I can perceive that your mind is not tranquil. How
is this so?

text: Aditi said: O my respected brähmaëa husband, all is well
sanskrit:
with the brähmaëas, the cows, religion and the welfare of other
people. O master of the house, the three principles of dharma, artha and
käma flourish in household life, which is consequently full of good
fortune.

text: O beloved husband, the fires, guests, servants and beggars
sanskrit:
are all being properly cared for by me. Because I always think of you,
there is no possibility that any of the religious principles will be
neglected.

text: O my lord, since you are a Prajäpati and are personally my
sanskrit:
instructor in the principles of religion, where is the possibility that
all my desires will not be fulfilled?

text: O son of Maréci, because you are a great personality you
sanskrit:
are equal toward all the demons and demigods, who are born either from
your body or from your mind and who possess one or another of the three
qualities-sattva-guëa, rajo-guëa or tamo-guëa. But although the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, the supreme controller, is equal toward
all living entities, He is especially favorable to the devotees.

text: Therefore, most gentle lord, kindly favor your maidservant.
sanskrit:
We have now been deprived of our opulence and residence by our
competitors, the demons. Kindly give us protection.

text: The demons, our formidably powerful enemies, have taken
sanskrit:
away our opulence, our beauty, our fame and even our residence. Indeed,
we have now been exiled, and we are drowning in an ocean of trouble.

text: O best of sages, best of all those who grant auspicious
sanskrit:
benedictions, please consider our situation and bestow upon my sons the
benedictions by which they can regain what they have lost.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: When Kaçyapa Muni was thus
sanskrit:
requested by Aditi, he slightly smiled. "Alas," he said, "how powerful
is the illusory energy of Lord Viñëu, by which the entire world is
bound by affection for children!"

text: Kaçyapa Muni continued: What is this material body, made
sanskrit:
of five elements? It is different from the spirit soul. Indeed, the
spirit soul is completely different from the material elements from
which the body is made. But because of bodily attachment, one is
regarded as a husband or son. These illusory relationships are caused by
misunderstanding.

text: My dear Aditi, engage in devotional service to the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, who is the master of everything, who can subdue
everyone's enemies, and who sits within everyone's heart. Only that
Supreme Person-Kåñëa, or Väsudeva-can bestow all auspicious
benedictions upon everyone, for He is the spiritual master of the
universe.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is very merciful to
sanskrit:
the poor, will fulfill all of your desires, for devotional service unto
Him is infallible. Any method other than devotional service is useless.
That is my opinion.

text: Çrématé Aditi said: O brähmaëa, tell me the regulative
sanskrit:
principles by which I may worship the supreme master of the world so
that the Lord will be pleased with me and fulfill all my desires.

text: O best of the brähmaëas, kindly instruct me in the
sanskrit:
perfect method of worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead in
devotional service, by which the Lord may very soon be pleased with me
and save me, along with my sons, from this most dangerous condition.

text: Çré Kaçyapa Muni said: When I desired offspring, I
sanskrit:
placed inquiries before Lord Brahmä, who is born from a lotus flower.
Now I shall explain to you the same process Lord Brahmä instructed me,
by which Keçava, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is satisfied.

text: In the bright fortnight of the month of Phälguna [February
sanskrit:
and March], for twelve days ending with Dvädaçé, one should observe
the vow of subsisting only on milk and should worship the lotus-eyed
Supreme Personality of Godhead with all devotion.

text: If dirt dug up by a boar is available, on the day of the
sanskrit:
dark moon one should smear this dirt on his body and then bathe in a
flowing river. While bathing, one should chant the following mantra.

text: O mother earth, you were raised by the Supreme Personality
sanskrit:
of Godhead in the form of a boar because of your desiring to have a
place to stay. I pray that you kindly vanquish all the reactions of my
sinful life. I offer my respectful obeisances unto you.

text: Thereafter, one should perform his daily spiritual duties
sanskrit:
and then, with great attention, offer worship to the Deity of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, and also to the altar, the sun, water,
fire and the spiritual master.

text: O Supreme Personality of Godhead, greatest of all, who
sanskrit:
lives in everyone's heart and in whom everyone lives, O witness of
everything, O Väsudeva, supreme and all-pervading person, I offer my
respectful obeisances unto You.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, the Supreme
sanskrit:
Person. Being very subtle, You are never visible to material eyes. You
are the knower of the twenty-four elements, and You are the inaugurator
of the säìkhya-yoga system.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, who have two heads [präyaëéya and
udäyanéya], three legs [savana-traya], four horns [the four Vedas] and
seven hands [the seven chandas, such as Gäyatré]. I offer my
obeisances unto You, whose heart and soul are the three Vedic rituals
[karma-käëòa, jïäna-käëòa and upäsanä-käëòa] and who expand
these rituals in the form of sacrifice.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, Lord Çiva, or
sanskrit:
Rudra, who are the reservoir of all potencies, the reservoir of all
knowledge, and the master of everyone.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, who are situated
sanskrit:
as Hiraëyagarbha, the source of life, the Supersoul of every living
entity. Your body is the source of the opulence of all mystic power. I
offer my respectful obeisances unto You.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, who are the
sanskrit:
original Personality of Godhead, the witness in everyone's heart, and
the incarnation of Nara-Näräyaëa Åñi in the form of a human being.
O Personality of Godhead, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.

text: My Lord, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, who are
sanskrit:
dressed in yellow garments, whose bodily hue resembles the marakata gem,
and who have full control over the goddess of fortune. O my Lord
Keçava, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.

text: O most exalted and worshipable Lord, best of those who
sanskrit:
bestow benediction, You can fulfill the desires of everyone, and
therefore those who are sober, for their own welfare, worship the dust
of Your lotus feet.

text: All the demigods, as well as the goddess of fortune, engage
sanskrit:
in the service of His lotus feet. Indeed, they respect the fragrance of
those lotus feet. May the Supreme Personality of Godhead be pleased with
me.

text: Kaçyapa Muni continued: By chanting all these mantras,
sanskrit:
welcoming the Supreme Personality of Godhead with faith and devotion,
and offering Him items of worship [such as pädya and arghya], one
should worship Keçava, Håñékeça, Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality
of Godhead.

text: In the beginning, the devotee should chant the
sanskrit:
dvädaçäkñara-mantra and offer flower garlands, incense and so on.
After worshiping the Lord in this way, one should bathe the Lord with
milk and dress Him with proper garments, a sacred thread, and ornaments.
After offering water to wash the Lord's feet, one should again worship
the Lord with fragrant flowers, incense and other paraphernalia.

text: If one can afford to, one should offer the Deity fine rice
sanskrit:
boiled in milk with clarified butter and molasses. While chanting the
same original mantra, one should offer all this to the fire.

text: One should offer all the prasäda to a Vaiñëava or offer
sanskrit:
him some of the prasäda and then take some oneself. After this, one
should offer the Deity äcamana and then betel nut and then again
worship the Lord.

text: Thereafter, one should silently murmur the mantra 108 times
sanskrit:
and offer prayers to the Lord for His glorification. Then one should
circumambulate the Lord and finally, with great delight and
satisfaction, offer obeisances, falling straight like a rod
[daëòavat].

text: After touching to one's head all the flowers and water
sanskrit:
offered to the Deity, one should throw them into a sacred place. Then
one should feed at least two brähmaëas with sweet rice.

text: One should perfectly honor the respectable brähmaëas
sanskrit:
one has fed, and then, after taking their permission, one should take
prasäda with his friends and relatives. For that night, one should
observe strict celibacy, and the next morning, after bathing again, with
purity and attention one should bathe the Deity of Viñëu with milk and
worship Him according to the methods formerly stated in detail.

text: Worshiping Lord Viñëu with great faith and devotion and
sanskrit:
living only by drinking milk, one should follow this vow. One should
also offer oblations to the fire and feed the brähmaëas as mentioned
before.

text: In this way, until twelve days have passed, one should
sanskrit:
observe this payo-vrata, worshiping the Lord every day, executing the
routine duties, performing sacrifices and feeding the brähmaëas.

text: From pratipat until the thirteenth day of the next bright
sanskrit:
moon [çukla-trayodaçé], one should observe complete celibacy, sleep
on the floor, bathe three times a day and thus execute the vow.

text: During this period, one should not unnecessarily talk of
sanskrit:
material subjects or topics of sense gratification, one should be
completely free from envy of all living entities, and one should be a
pure and simple devotee of Lord Väsudeva.

text: Thereafter, following the directions of the çästra with
sanskrit:
help from brähmaëas who know the çästra, on the thirteenth day of
the moon one should bathe Lord Viñëu with five substances [milk,
yogurt, ghee, sugar and honey].

text: Giving up the miserly habit of not spending money, one
sanskrit:
should arrange for the gorgeous worship of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, Viñëu, who is situated in the heart of every living entity.
With great attention, one must prepare an oblation of grains boiled in
ghee and milk and must chant the Puruña-sükta mantra. The offerings of
food should be of varieties of tastes. In this way, one should worship
the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: One should satisfy the spiritual master [äcärya], who is
sanskrit:
very learned in Vedic literature, and should satisfy his assistant
priests [known as hotä, udgätä, adhvaryu and brahma]. One should
please them by offering them clothing, ornaments and cows. This is the
ceremony called viñëu-ärädhana, or worship of Lord Viñëu.

text: O most auspicious lady, one should perform all the
sanskrit:
ceremonies under the direction of learned äcäryas and should satisfy
them and their priests. By distributing prasäda, one should also
satisfy the brähmaëas and others who have assembled.

text: One should satisfy the spiritual master and assistant
sanskrit:
priests by giving them cloth, ornaments, cows and also some monetary
contribution. And by distributing prasäda one should satisfy everyone
assembled, including even the lowest of men, the caëòälas [eaters of
dog flesh].

text: One should distribute viñëu-prasäda to everyone,
sanskrit:
including the poor man, the blind man, the nondevotee and the
non-brähmaëa. Knowing that Lord Viñëu is very pleased when everyone
is sumptuously fed with viñëu-prasäda, the performer of yajïa should
then take prasäda with his friends and relatives.

text: Every day from pratipat to trayodaçé, one should continue
sanskrit:
the ceremony, to the accompaniment of dancing, singing, the beating of a
drum, the chanting of prayers and all-auspicious mantras, and recitation
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam. In this way, one should worship the Supreme
Personality of Godhead.

text: This is the religious ritualistic ceremony known as
sanskrit:
payo-vrata, by which one may worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
I received this information from Brahmä, my grandfather, and now I have
described it to you in all details.

text: O most fortunate lady, establishing your mind in a good
sanskrit:
spirit, execute this process of payo-vrata and thus worship the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, Keçava, who is inexhaustible.

text: This payo-vrata is also known as sarva-yajïa. In other
sanskrit:
words, by performing this sacrifice one can perform all other sacrifices
automatically. This is also acknowledged to be the best of all
ritualistic ceremonies. O gentle lady, it is the essence of all
austerities, and it is the process of giving charity and pleasing the
supreme controller.

text: This is the best process for pleasing the transcendental
sanskrit:
Supreme Personality of Godhead, known as Adhokñaja. It is the best of
all regulative principles, the best austerity, the best process of
giving charity, and the best process of sacrifice.

text: Therefore, my dear gentle lady, follow this ritualistic
sanskrit:
vow, strictly observing the regulative principles. By this process, the
Supreme Person will very soon be pleased with you and will satisfy all
your desires.
16. SB 8.16.1 - Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, when Aditi's sons,
the demigods, had thus disappeared from heaven and the demons had
occupied their places, Aditi began lamenting, as if she had no
protector.

text: After many, many days, the great powerful sage Kaçyapa Muni
sanskrit:
arose from a trance of meditation and returned home to see the äçrama
of Aditi neither jubilant nor festive.

text: O best of the Kurus, when Kaçyapa Muni had been properly
sanskrit:
received and welcomed, he took his seat and then spoke as follows to his
wife, Aditi, who was very morose.

text: O most gentle one, I wonder whether anything inauspicious
sanskrit:
has now taken place in regard to religious principles, the brähmaëas
or the people in general, who are subject to the whims of death.

text: O my wife, who are very much attached to household life, if
sanskrit:
the principles of religion, economic development and satisfaction of the
senses are properly followed in household life, one's activities are as
good as those of a transcendentalist. I wonder whether there have been
any discrepancies in following these principles.

text: I wonder whether because of being too attached to the
sanskrit:
members of your family, you failed to properly receive uninvited guests,
who therefore were not welcomed and went away.

text: Homes from which guests go away without having been received
sanskrit:
even with an offering of a little water are like those holes in the
field which are the homes of jackals.

text: O chaste and auspicious woman, when I left home for other
sanskrit:
places, were you in so much anxiety that you did not offer oblations of
ghee into the fire?

text: By worshiping the fire and the brähmaëas, a householder
sanskrit:
can achieve the desired goal of residing in the higher planets, for the
sacrificial fire and the brähmaëas are to be considered the mouth of
Lord Viñëu, who is the Supersoul of all the demigods.

text: O great-minded lady, are all your sons faring well? Seeing
sanskrit:
your withered face, I can perceive that your mind is not tranquil. How
is this so?

text: Aditi said: O my respected brähmaëa husband, all is well
sanskrit:
with the brähmaëas, the cows, religion and the welfare of other
people. O master of the house, the three principles of dharma, artha and
käma flourish in household life, which is consequently full of good
fortune.

text: O beloved husband, the fires, guests, servants and beggars
sanskrit:
are all being properly cared for by me. Because I always think of you,
there is no possibility that any of the religious principles will be
neglected.

text: O my lord, since you are a Prajäpati and are personally my
sanskrit:
instructor in the principles of religion, where is the possibility that
all my desires will not be fulfilled?

text: O son of Maréci, because you are a great personality you
sanskrit:
are equal toward all the demons and demigods, who are born either from
your body or from your mind and who possess one or another of the three
qualities-sattva-guëa, rajo-guëa or tamo-guëa. But although the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, the supreme controller, is equal toward
all living entities, He is especially favorable to the devotees.

text: Therefore, most gentle lord, kindly favor your maidservant.
sanskrit:
We have now been deprived of our opulence and residence by our
competitors, the demons. Kindly give us protection.

text: The demons, our formidably powerful enemies, have taken
sanskrit:
away our opulence, our beauty, our fame and even our residence. Indeed,
we have now been exiled, and we are drowning in an ocean of trouble.

text: O best of sages, best of all those who grant auspicious
sanskrit:
benedictions, please consider our situation and bestow upon my sons the
benedictions by which they can regain what they have lost.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: When Kaçyapa Muni was thus
sanskrit:
requested by Aditi, he slightly smiled. "Alas," he said, "how powerful
is the illusory energy of Lord Viñëu, by which the entire world is
bound by affection for children!"

text: Kaçyapa Muni continued: What is this material body, made
sanskrit:
of five elements? It is different from the spirit soul. Indeed, the
spirit soul is completely different from the material elements from
which the body is made. But because of bodily attachment, one is
regarded as a husband or son. These illusory relationships are caused by
misunderstanding.

text: My dear Aditi, engage in devotional service to the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, who is the master of everything, who can subdue
everyone's enemies, and who sits within everyone's heart. Only that
Supreme Person-Kåñëa, or Väsudeva-can bestow all auspicious
benedictions upon everyone, for He is the spiritual master of the
universe.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is very merciful to
sanskrit:
the poor, will fulfill all of your desires, for devotional service unto
Him is infallible. Any method other than devotional service is useless.
That is my opinion.

text: Çrématé Aditi said: O brähmaëa, tell me the regulative
sanskrit:
principles by which I may worship the supreme master of the world so
that the Lord will be pleased with me and fulfill all my desires.

text: O best of the brähmaëas, kindly instruct me in the
sanskrit:
perfect method of worshiping the Supreme Personality of Godhead in
devotional service, by which the Lord may very soon be pleased with me
and save me, along with my sons, from this most dangerous condition.

text: Çré Kaçyapa Muni said: When I desired offspring, I
sanskrit:
placed inquiries before Lord Brahmä, who is born from a lotus flower.
Now I shall explain to you the same process Lord Brahmä instructed me,
by which Keçava, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is satisfied.

text: In the bright fortnight of the month of Phälguna [February
sanskrit:
and March], for twelve days ending with Dvädaçé, one should observe
the vow of subsisting only on milk and should worship the lotus-eyed
Supreme Personality of Godhead with all devotion.

text: If dirt dug up by a boar is available, on the day of the
sanskrit:
dark moon one should smear this dirt on his body and then bathe in a
flowing river. While bathing, one should chant the following mantra.

text: O mother earth, you were raised by the Supreme Personality
sanskrit:
of Godhead in the form of a boar because of your desiring to have a
place to stay. I pray that you kindly vanquish all the reactions of my
sinful life. I offer my respectful obeisances unto you.

text: Thereafter, one should perform his daily spiritual duties
sanskrit:
and then, with great attention, offer worship to the Deity of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, and also to the altar, the sun, water,
fire and the spiritual master.

text: O Supreme Personality of Godhead, greatest of all, who
sanskrit:
lives in everyone's heart and in whom everyone lives, O witness of
everything, O Väsudeva, supreme and all-pervading person, I offer my
respectful obeisances unto You.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, the Supreme
sanskrit:
Person. Being very subtle, You are never visible to material eyes. You
are the knower of the twenty-four elements, and You are the inaugurator
of the säìkhya-yoga system.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, who have two heads [präyaëéya and
udäyanéya], three legs [savana-traya], four horns [the four Vedas] and
seven hands [the seven chandas, such as Gäyatré]. I offer my
obeisances unto You, whose heart and soul are the three Vedic rituals
[karma-käëòa, jïäna-käëòa and upäsanä-käëòa] and who expand
these rituals in the form of sacrifice.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, Lord Çiva, or
sanskrit:
Rudra, who are the reservoir of all potencies, the reservoir of all
knowledge, and the master of everyone.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, who are situated
sanskrit:
as Hiraëyagarbha, the source of life, the Supersoul of every living
entity. Your body is the source of the opulence of all mystic power. I
offer my respectful obeisances unto You.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, who are the
sanskrit:
original Personality of Godhead, the witness in everyone's heart, and
the incarnation of Nara-Näräyaëa Åñi in the form of a human being.
O Personality of Godhead, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.

text: My Lord, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, who are
sanskrit:
dressed in yellow garments, whose bodily hue resembles the marakata gem,
and who have full control over the goddess of fortune. O my Lord
Keçava, I offer my respectful obeisances unto You.

text: O most exalted and worshipable Lord, best of those who
sanskrit:
bestow benediction, You can fulfill the desires of everyone, and
therefore those who are sober, for their own welfare, worship the dust
of Your lotus feet.

text: All the demigods, as well as the goddess of fortune, engage
sanskrit:
in the service of His lotus feet. Indeed, they respect the fragrance of
those lotus feet. May the Supreme Personality of Godhead be pleased with
me.

text: Kaçyapa Muni continued: By chanting all these mantras,
sanskrit:
welcoming the Supreme Personality of Godhead with faith and devotion,
and offering Him items of worship [such as pädya and arghya], one
should worship Keçava, Håñékeça, Kåñëa, the Supreme Personality
of Godhead.

text: In the beginning, the devotee should chant the
sanskrit:
dvädaçäkñara-mantra and offer flower garlands, incense and so on.
After worshiping the Lord in this way, one should bathe the Lord with
milk and dress Him with proper garments, a sacred thread, and ornaments.
After offering water to wash the Lord's feet, one should again worship
the Lord with fragrant flowers, incense and other paraphernalia.

text: If one can afford to, one should offer the Deity fine rice
sanskrit:
boiled in milk with clarified butter and molasses. While chanting the
same original mantra, one should offer all this to the fire.

text: One should offer all the prasäda to a Vaiñëava or offer
sanskrit:
him some of the prasäda and then take some oneself. After this, one
should offer the Deity äcamana and then betel nut and then again
worship the Lord.

text: Thereafter, one should silently murmur the mantra 108 times
sanskrit:
and offer prayers to the Lord for His glorification. Then one should
circumambulate the Lord and finally, with great delight and
satisfaction, offer obeisances, falling straight like a rod
[daëòavat].

text: After touching to one's head all the flowers and water
sanskrit:
offered to the Deity, one should throw them into a sacred place. Then
one should feed at least two brähmaëas with sweet rice.

text: One should perfectly honor the respectable brähmaëas
sanskrit:
one has fed, and then, after taking their permission, one should take
prasäda with his friends and relatives. For that night, one should
observe strict celibacy, and the next morning, after bathing again, with
purity and attention one should bathe the Deity of Viñëu with milk and
worship Him according to the methods formerly stated in detail.

text: Worshiping Lord Viñëu with great faith and devotion and
sanskrit:
living only by drinking milk, one should follow this vow. One should
also offer oblations to the fire and feed the brähmaëas as mentioned
before.

text: In this way, until twelve days have passed, one should
sanskrit:
observe this payo-vrata, worshiping the Lord every day, executing the
routine duties, performing sacrifices and feeding the brähmaëas.

text: From pratipat until the thirteenth day of the next bright
sanskrit:
moon [çukla-trayodaçé], one should observe complete celibacy, sleep
on the floor, bathe three times a day and thus execute the vow.

text: During this period, one should not unnecessarily talk of
sanskrit:
material subjects or topics of sense gratification, one should be
completely free from envy of all living entities, and one should be a
pure and simple devotee of Lord Väsudeva.

text: Thereafter, following the directions of the çästra with
sanskrit:
help from brähmaëas who know the çästra, on the thirteenth day of
the moon one should bathe Lord Viñëu with five substances [milk,
yogurt, ghee, sugar and honey].

text: Giving up the miserly habit of not spending money, one
sanskrit:
should arrange for the gorgeous worship of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, Viñëu, who is situated in the heart of every living entity.
With great attention, one must prepare an oblation of grains boiled in
ghee and milk and must chant the Puruña-sükta mantra. The offerings of
food should be of varieties of tastes. In this way, one should worship
the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: One should satisfy the spiritual master [äcärya], who is
sanskrit:
very learned in Vedic literature, and should satisfy his assistant
priests [known as hotä, udgätä, adhvaryu and brahma]. One should
please them by offering them clothing, ornaments and cows. This is the
ceremony called viñëu-ärädhana, or worship of Lord Viñëu.

text: O most auspicious lady, one should perform all the
sanskrit:
ceremonies under the direction of learned äcäryas and should satisfy
them and their priests. By distributing prasäda, one should also
satisfy the brähmaëas and others who have assembled.

text: One should satisfy the spiritual master and assistant
sanskrit:
priests by giving them cloth, ornaments, cows and also some monetary
contribution. And by distributing prasäda one should satisfy everyone
assembled, including even the lowest of men, the caëòälas [eaters of
dog flesh].

text: One should distribute viñëu-prasäda to everyone,
sanskrit:
including the poor man, the blind man, the nondevotee and the
non-brähmaëa. Knowing that Lord Viñëu is very pleased when everyone
is sumptuously fed with viñëu-prasäda, the performer of yajïa should
then take prasäda with his friends and relatives.

text: Every day from pratipat to trayodaçé, one should continue
sanskrit:
the ceremony, to the accompaniment of dancing, singing, the beating of a
drum, the chanting of prayers and all-auspicious mantras, and recitation
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam. In this way, one should worship the Supreme
Personality of Godhead.

text: This is the religious ritualistic ceremony known as
sanskrit:
payo-vrata, by which one may worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
I received this information from Brahmä, my grandfather, and now I have
described it to you in all details.

text: O most fortunate lady, establishing your mind in a good
sanskrit:
spirit, execute this process of payo-vrata and thus worship the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, Keçava, who is inexhaustible.

text: This payo-vrata is also known as sarva-yajïa. In other
sanskrit:
words, by performing this sacrifice one can perform all other sacrifices
automatically. This is also acknowledged to be the best of all
ritualistic ceremonies. O gentle lady, it is the essence of all
austerities, and it is the process of giving charity and pleasing the
supreme controller.

text: This is the best process for pleasing the transcendental
sanskrit:
Supreme Personality of Godhead, known as Adhokñaja. It is the best of
all regulative principles, the best austerity, the best process of
giving charity, and the best process of sacrifice.

text: Therefore, my dear gentle lady, follow this ritualistic
sanskrit:
vow, strictly observing the regulative principles. By this process, the
Supreme Person will very soon be pleased with you and will satisfy all
your desires.

ghee and milk and must chant the Puruña-sükta mantra. The offerings of
food should be of varieties of tastes. In this way, one should worship
the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: One should satisfy the spiritual master [äcärya], who is
sanskrit:
very learned in Vedic literature, and should satisfy his assistant
priests [known as hotä, udgätä, adhvaryu and brahma]. One should
please them by offering them clothing, ornaments and cows. This is the
ceremony called viñëu-ärädhana, or worship of Lord Viñëu.

text: O most auspicious lady, one should perform all the
sanskrit:
ceremonies under the direction of learned äcäryas and should satisfy
them and their priests. By distributing prasäda, one should also
satisfy the brähmaëas and others who have assembled.

text: One should satisfy the spiritual master and assistant
sanskrit:
priests by giving them cloth, ornaments, cows and also some monetary
contribution. And by distributing prasäda one should satisfy everyone
assembled, including even the lowest of men, the caëòälas [eaters of
dog flesh].

text: One should distribute viñëu-prasäda to everyone,
sanskrit:
including the poor man, the blind man, the nondevotee and the
non-brähmaëa. Knowing that Lord Viñëu is very pleased when everyone
is sumptuously fed with viñëu-prasäda, the performer of yajïa should
then take prasäda with his friends and relatives.

text: Every day from pratipat to trayodaçé, one should continue
sanskrit:
the ceremony, to the accompaniment of dancing, singing, the beating of a
drum, the chanting of prayers and all-auspicious mantras, and recitation
of Çrémad-Bhägavatam. In this way, one should worship the Supreme
Personality of Godhead.

text: This is the religious ritualistic ceremony known as
sanskrit:
payo-vrata, by which one may worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
I received this information from Brahmä, my grandfather, and now I have
described it to you in all details.

text: O most fortunate lady, establishing your mind in a good
sanskrit:
spirit, execute this process of payo-vrata and thus worship the Supreme
Personality of Godhead, Keçava, who is inexhaustible.

text: This payo-vrata is also known as sarva-yajïa. In other
sanskrit:
words, by performing this sacrifice one can perform all other sacrifices
automatically. This is also acknowledged to be the best of all
ritualistic ceremonies. O gentle lady, it is the essence of all
austerities, and it is the process of giving charity and pleasing the
supreme controller.

text: This is the best process for pleasing the transcendental
sanskrit:
Supreme Personality of Godhead, known as Adhokñaja. It is the best of
all regulative principles, the best austerity, the best process of
giving charity, and the best process of sacrifice.

text: Therefore, my dear gentle lady, follow this ritualistic
sanskrit:
vow, strictly observing the regulative principles. By this process, the
Supreme Person will very soon be pleased with you and will satisfy all
your desires.

sanskrit:
prayers to the Lord. Because of transcendental bliss, tears filled her

text: O Mahäräja Parékñit, the demigoddess Aditi then began
sanskrit:
offering her prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead in a

text: The goddess Aditi said: O master and enjoyer of all
sanskrit:
sacrificial ceremonies, O infallible and most famous person, whose name,
when chanted, spreads all good fortune! O original Supreme Personality
of Godhead, supreme controller, shelter of all holy places, You are the
shelter of all poor, suffering living entities, and You have appeared to
diminish their suffering. Please be kind to us and spread our good
fortune.

text: My Lord, You are the all-pervading universal form, the fully
sanskrit:
independent creator, maintainer and destroyer of this universe. Although

original form and never fall from that position, for Your knowledge is
infallible and always suitable to any situation. You are never

unto You.

text: O unlimited one, if Your Lordship is satisfied, one can
sanskrit:
very easily obtain a lifetime as long as that of Lord Brahmä, a body

material opulence, religion, economic development and satisfaction of
the senses, full transcendental knowledge, and the eight yogic

Bharata dynasty, when the lotus-eyed Lord, the Supersoul of all living

sanskrit:
demigods, I have already understood your long-cherished desires for the

sanskrit: opulence and live again on their heavenly planet as usual.

sanskrit:
chiefs of the demons are now unconquerable, for they are being protected

sanskrit:

Supreme Personality of Godhead disappeared from that very spot. Aditi,

whose vision is never mistaken, could see that a plenary portion of the

sanskrit:
wood and thus gives rise to fire, Kaçyapa Muni, whose transcendental
