text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: After Lord Brahmä had thus
sanskrit:
spoken, glorifying the Supreme Lord's activities and prowess, the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is never subject to death like an
ordinary living being, appeared from the womb of Aditi. His four hands
were decorated with a conchshell, club, lotus and disc, He was dressed
in yellow garments, and His eyes appeared like the petals of a blooming
lotus.

text: The body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, blackish in
sanskrit:
complexion, was free from all inebrieties. His lotus face, decorated
with earrings resembling sharks, appeared very beautiful, and on His
bosom was the mark of Çrévatsa. He wore bangles on His wrists, armlets
on His arms, a helmet on His head, a belt on His waist, a sacred thread
across His chest, and ankle bells decorating His lotus feet.

text: An uncommonly beautiful garland of flowers decorated His
sanskrit:
bosom, and because the flowers were extremely fragrant, a large group of
bees, making their natural humming sounds, invaded them for honey. When
the Lord appeared, wearing the Kaustubha gem on His neck, His effulgence
vanquished the darkness in the home of the Prajäpati Kaçyapa.

text: At that time, there was happiness in all directions, in the
sanskrit:
reservoirs of water like the rivers and oceans, and in the core of
everyone's heart. The various seasons displayed their respective
qualities, and all living entities in the upper planetary system, in
outer space and on the surface of the earth were jubilant. The demigods,
the cows, the brähmaëas and the hills and mountains were all filled
with joy.

text: On the day of Çravaëa-dvädaçé [the twelfth day of the
sanskrit:
bright fortnight in the month of Bhädra], when the moon came into the
lunar mansion Çravaëa, at the auspicious moment of Abhijit, the Lord
appeared in this universe. Considering the Lord's appearance very
auspicious, all the stars and planets, from the sun to Saturn, were
munificently charitable.

text: O King, when the Lord appeared-on dvädaçé, the twelfth
sanskrit:
day of the moon-the sun was at the meridian, as every learned scholar
knows. This dvädaçé is called Vijayä.

text: Conchshells, kettledrums, drums, paëavas and änakas
sanskrit:
vibrated in concert. The sound of these and various other instruments
was tumultuous.

text: Being very pleased, the celestial dancing girls [Apsaräs]
sanskrit:
danced in jubilation, the best of the Gandharvas sang songs, and the
great sages, demigods, Manus, Pitäs and fire-gods offered prayers to
satisfy the Lord.

text: The Siddhas, Vidyädharas, Kimpuruñas, Kinnaras,
sanskrit:
Cäraëas, Yakñas, Räkñasas, Suparëas, the best of serpents, and the
followers of the demigods all showered flowers on Aditi's residence,
covering the entire house, while glorifying and praising the Lord and
dancing.

text: When Aditi saw the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who had
sanskrit:
appeared from her own womb, having accepted a transcendental body by His
own spiritual potency, she was struck with wonder and was very happy.
Upon seeing the child, Prajäpati Kaçyapa exclaimed, "Jaya! Jaya!" in
great happiness and wonder.

text: The Lord appeared in His original form, with ornaments and
sanskrit:
weapons in His hands. Although this ever-existing form is not visible in
the material world, He nonetheless appeared in this form. Then, in the
presence of His father and mother, He assumed the form of Vämana, a
brähmaëa-dwarf, a brahmacäré, just like a theatrical actor.

ceremonies, such as the birthday ceremony.

text: At the sacred thread ceremony of Vämanadeva, the sun-god
sanskrit:
personally uttered the Gäyatré mantra, Båhaspati offered the sacred
thread, and Kaçyapa Muni offered a straw belt.

text: Mother earth gave Him a deerskin, and the demigod of the
sanskrit:
moon, who is the king of the forest, gave Him a brahma-daëòa [the rod
of a brahmacäré]. His mother, Aditi, gave Him cloth for underwear, and
the deity presiding over the heavenly kingdom offered Him an umbrella.

text: O King, Lord Brahmä offered a waterpot to the
sanskrit:
inexhaustible Supreme Personality of Godhead, the seven sages offered
Him kuça grass, and mother Sarasvaté gave Him a string of Rudräkña
beads.

text: When Vämanadeva had thus been given the sacred thread,
sanskrit:
Kuvera, King of the Yakñas, gave Him a pot for begging alms, and mother
Bhagavaté, the wife of Lord Çiva and most chaste mother of the entire
universe, gave Him His first alms.

text: Having thus been welcomed by everyone, Lord Vämanadeva,
sanskrit:
the best of the brahmacärés, exhibited His Brahman effulgence. Thus He
surpassed in beauty that entire assembly, which was filled with great
saintly brähmaëas.

text: After Lord Çré Vämanadeva set a sacrificial fire, He
sanskrit: offered worship and performed a fire sacrifice on the sacrificial field.

text: When the Lord heard that Bali Mahäräja was performing
sanskrit:
açvamedha sacrifices under the patronage of brähmaëas belonging to
the Bhågu dynasty, the Supreme Lord, who is full in every respect,
proceeded there to show His mercy to Bali Mahäräja. By His weight, He
pushed down the earth with every step.

text: While engaged in performing the sacrifice in the field
sanskrit:
known as Bhågukaccha, on the northern bank of the Narmadä River, the
brahminical priests, the descendants of Bhågu, saw Vämanadeva to be
like the sun rising nearby.

text: O King, because of Vämanadeva's bright effulgence, the
sanskrit:
priests, along with Bali Mahäräja and all the members of the assembly,
were robbed of their splendor. Thus they began to ask one another
whether the sun-god himself, Sanat-kumära or the fire-god had
personally come to see the sacrificial ceremony.

text: While the priests of the Bhågu dynasty and their disciples
sanskrit:
talked and argued in various ways, the Supreme Personality of Godhead,
Vämanadeva, holding in His hands the rod, the umbrella and a waterpot
full of water, entered the arena of the açvamedha sacrifice.

text: Appearing as a brähmaëa boy, wearing a belt of straw,
sanskrit:
a sacred thread, an upper garment of deerskin, and matted locks of hair,
Lord Vämanadeva entered the arena of sacrifice. His brilliant
effulgence diminished the brilliance of all the priests and their
disciples, who thus stood from their seats and welcomed the Lord
properly by offering obeisances.

text: Bali Mahäräja, jubilant at seeing Lord Vämanadeva, whose
sanskrit:
beautiful limbs contributed equally to the beauty of His entire body,
offered Him a seat with great satisfaction.

text: Thus offering a proper reception to the Supreme Personality
sanskrit:
of Godhead, who is always beautiful to the liberated souls, Bali
Mahäräja worshiped Him by washing His lotus feet.

text: Lord Çiva, the best of demigods, who carries on his
sanskrit:
forehead the emblem of the moon, receives on his head with great
devotion the Ganges water emanating from the toe of Viñëu. Being aware
of religious principles, Bali Mahäräja knew this. Consequently,
following in the footsteps of Lord Çiva, he also placed on his head the
water that had washed the Lord's lotus feet.

text: Bali Mahäräja then said to Lord Vämanadeva: O
sanskrit:
brähmaëa, I offer You my hearty welcome and my respectful obeisances.
Please let us know what we may do for You. We think of You as the
personified austerity of the great brähmaëa-sages.

text: O my Lord, because You have kindly arrived at our home, all
sanskrit:
my forefathers are satisfied, our family and entire dynasty have been
sanctified, and the sacrifice we are performing is now complete because
of Your presence.

text: O son of a brähmaëa, today the fire of sacrifice is
sanskrit:
ablaze according to the injunction of the çästra, and I have been
freed from all the sinful reactions of my life by the water that has
washed Your lotus feet. O my Lord, by the touch of Your small lotus feet
the entire surface of the world has been sanctified.

text: O son of a brähmaëa, it appears that You have come here
sanskrit:
to ask me for something. Therefore, whatever You want You may take from
me. O best of those who are worshipable. You may take from me a cow,
gold, a furnished house, palatable food and drink, the daughter of a
brähmaëa for Your wife, prosperous villages, horses, elephants,
chariots or whatever You desire.
18. SB 8.18.1 - Çukadeva Gosvämé said: After Lord Brahmä had thus
spoken, glorifying the Supreme Lord's activities and prowess, the
Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is never subject to death like an
ordinary living being, appeared from the womb of Aditi. His four hands
were decorated with a conchshell, club, lotus and disc, He was dressed
in yellow garments, and His eyes appeared like the petals of a blooming
lotus.

text: The body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, blackish in
sanskrit:
complexion, was free from all inebrieties. His lotus face, decorated
with earrings resembling sharks, appeared very beautiful, and on His
bosom was the mark of Çrévatsa. He wore bangles on His wrists, armlets
on His arms, a helmet on His head, a belt on His waist, a sacred thread
across His chest, and ankle bells decorating His lotus feet.

text: An uncommonly beautiful garland of flowers decorated His
sanskrit:
bosom, and because the flowers were extremely fragrant, a large group of
bees, making their natural humming sounds, invaded them for honey. When
the Lord appeared, wearing the Kaustubha gem on His neck, His effulgence
vanquished the darkness in the home of the Prajäpati Kaçyapa.

text: At that time, there was happiness in all directions, in the
sanskrit:
reservoirs of water like the rivers and oceans, and in the core of
everyone's heart. The various seasons displayed their respective
qualities, and all living entities in the upper planetary system, in
outer space and on the surface of the earth were jubilant. The demigods,
the cows, the brähmaëas and the hills and mountains were all filled
with joy.

text: On the day of Çravaëa-dvädaçé [the twelfth day of the
sanskrit:
bright fortnight in the month of Bhädra], when the moon came into the
lunar mansion Çravaëa, at the auspicious moment of Abhijit, the Lord
appeared in this universe. Considering the Lord's appearance very
auspicious, all the stars and planets, from the sun to Saturn, were
munificently charitable.

text: O King, when the Lord appeared-on dvädaçé, the twelfth
sanskrit:
day of the moon-the sun was at the meridian, as every learned scholar
knows. This dvädaçé is called Vijayä.

text: Conchshells, kettledrums, drums, paëavas and änakas
sanskrit:
vibrated in concert. The sound of these and various other instruments
was tumultuous.

text: Being very pleased, the celestial dancing girls [Apsaräs]
sanskrit:
danced in jubilation, the best of the Gandharvas sang songs, and the
great sages, demigods, Manus, Pitäs and fire-gods offered prayers to
satisfy the Lord.

text: The Siddhas, Vidyädharas, Kimpuruñas, Kinnaras,
sanskrit:

Translations 1-32

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: When the Supreme Personality
sanskrit:
of Godhead, Vämanadeva, heard Bali Mahäräja speaking in this pleasing
way, He was very satisfied, for Bali Mahäräja had spoken in terms of
religious principles. Thus the Lord began to praise him.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O King, you are
sanskrit:
indeed exalted because your present advisors are the brähmaëas who are
descendants of Bhågu and because your instructor for your future life
is your grandfather, the peaceful and venerable Prahläda Mahäräja.
Your statements are very true, and they completely agree with religious
etiquette. They are in keeping with the behavior of your family, and
they enhance your reputation.

text: I know that even until now, no one taking birth in your
sanskrit:
family has been poor-minded or miserly. No one has refused to give
charity to brähmaëas, nor after promising to give charity has anyone
failed to fulfill his promise.

text: O King Bali, never in your dynasty has the low-minded King
sanskrit:
been born who upon being requested has refused charity to brähmaëas in
holy places or a fight to kñatriyas on a battlefield. And your dynasty
is even more glorious due to the presence of Prahläda Mahäräja, who
is like the beautiful moon in the sky.

text: It was in your dynasty that Hiraëyäkña was born. Carrying
sanskrit:
only his own club, he wandered the globe alone, without assistance, to
conquer all directions, and no hero he met could rival him.

text: When delivering the earth from the Garbhodaka Sea, Lord
sanskrit:
Viñëu, in His incarnation as a boar, killed Hiraëyäkña, who had
appeared before Him. The fight was severe, and the Lord killed
Hiraëyäkña with great difficulty. Later, as the Lord thought about
the uncommon prowess of Hiraëyäkña, He felt Himself victorious
indeed.

text: When Hiraëyakaçipu heard the news of his brother's being
sanskrit:
killed, with great anger he went to the residence of Viñëu, the killer
of his brother, wanting to kill Lord Viñëu.

text: Seeing Hiraëyakaçipu coming forward bearing a trident in
sanskrit:
his hand like personified death, Lord Viñëu, the best of all mystics
and the knower of the progress of time, thought as follows.

text: Wheresoever I go, Hiraëyakaçipu will follow Me, as death
sanskrit:
follows all living entities. Therefore it is better for Me to enter the
core of his heart, for then, because of his power to see only
externally, he will not see Me.

text: Lord Vämanadeva continued: O King of the demons, after
sanskrit:
Lord Viñëu made this decision, He entered the body of His enemy
Hiraëyakaçipu, who was running after Him with great force. In a subtle
body inconceivable to Hiraëyakaçipu, Lord Viñëu, who was in great
anxiety, entered Hiraëyakaçipu's nostril along with his breath.

text: Upon seeing that the residence of Lord Viñëu was vacant,
sanskrit:
Hiraëyakaçipu began searching for Lord Viñëu everywhere. Angry at
not seeing Him, Hiraëyakaçipu screamed loudly and searched the entire
universe, including the surface of the earth, the higher planetary
systems, all directions and all the caves and oceans. But
Hiraëyakaçipu, the greatest hero, did not see Viñëu anywhere.

text: Unable to see Him, Hiraëyakaçipu said, "I have searched
sanskrit:
the entire universe, but I could not find Viñëu, who has killed my
brother. Therefore, He must certainly have gone to that place from which
no one returns. [In other words, He must now be dead.]"

text: Hiraëyakaçipu's anger against Lord Viñëu persisted
sanskrit:
until his death. Other people in the bodily concept of life maintain
anger only because of false ego and the great influence of ignorance.

text: Your father, Virocana, the son of Mahäräja Prahläda, was
sanskrit:
very affectionate toward brähmaëas. Although he knew very well that it
was the demigods who had come to him in the dress of brähmaëas, at
their request he delivered to them the duration of his life.

text: You also have observed the principles followed by great
sanskrit:
personalities who are householder brähmaëas, by your forefathers and
by great heroes who are extremely famous for their exalted activities.

text: O King of the Daityas, from Your Majesty, who come from
sanskrit:
such a noble family and who are able to give charity munificently, I ask
only three paces of land, to the measurement of My steps.

text: O King, controller of the entire universe, although you are
sanskrit:
very munificent and are able to give Me as much land as I want, I do not
want anything from you that is unnecessary. If a learned brähmaëa
takes charity from others only according to his needs, he does not
become entangled in sinful activities.

sanskrit:

sanskrit:

sanskrit:
begins to dry up. Similarly, if one doesn't take care of the body, which
is supposed to be untruth-in other words, if the untruth is uprooted-the
body undoubtedly becomes dry.

sanskrit:
one's monetary assets. In other words, by uttering this word one becomes
free from attachment to money because his money is taken away from him.

cannot fulfill one's desires. In other words, by using the word oà one

sanskrit:
falsehood, it protects one completely, it draws the compassion of others

Personality of Godhead, Vämanadeva, heard Bali Mahäräja speaking in
this pleasing way, He was very satisfied, for Bali Mahäräja had spoken
in terms of religious principles. Thus the Lord began to praise him.

sanskrit:
indeed exalted because your present advisors are the brähmaëas who are
descendants of Bhågu and because your instructor for your future life
is your grandfather, the peaceful and venerable Prahläda Mahäräja.

etiquette. They are in keeping with the behavior of your family, and
they enhance your reputation.

text: I know that even until now, no one taking birth in your
sanskrit:
family has been poor-minded or miserly. No one has refused to give
charity to brähmaëas, nor after promising to give charity has anyone
failed to fulfill his promise.

text: O King Bali, never in your dynasty has the low-minded King
sanskrit:
been born who upon being requested has refused charity to brähmaëas in
holy places or a fight to kñatriyas on a battlefield. And your dynasty
is even more glorious due to the presence of Prahläda Mahäräja, who
is like the beautiful moon in the sky.

text: It was in your dynasty that Hiraëyäkña was born. Carrying
sanskrit:
only his own club, he wandered the globe alone, without assistance, to
conquer all directions, and no hero he met could rival him.

text: When delivering the earth from the Garbhodaka Sea, Lord
sanskrit:
Viñëu, in His incarnation as a boar, killed Hiraëyäkña, who had
appeared before Him. The fight was severe, and the Lord killed
Hiraëyäkña with great difficulty. Later, as the Lord thought about
the uncommon prowess of Hiraëyäkña, He felt Himself victorious
indeed.

text: When Hiraëyakaçipu heard the news of his brother's being
sanskrit:
killed, with great anger he went to the residence of Viñëu, the killer
of his brother, wanting to kill Lord Viñëu.

text: Seeing Hiraëyakaçipu coming forward bearing a trident in
sanskrit:
his hand like personified death, Lord Viñëu, the best of all mystics
and the knower of the progress of time, thought as follows.

text: Wheresoever I go, Hiraëyakaçipu will follow Me, as death
sanskrit:
follows all living entities. Therefore it is better for Me to enter the
core of his heart, for then, because of his power to see only
externally, he will not see Me.

text: Lord Vämanadeva continued: O King of the demons, after
sanskrit:
Lord Viñëu made this decision, He entered the body of His enemy

body inconceivable to Hiraëyakaçipu, Lord Viñëu, who was in great
anxiety, entered Hiraëyakaçipu's nostril along with his breath.

text: Upon seeing that the residence of Lord Viñëu was vacant,
sanskrit:
Hiraëyakaçipu began searching for Lord Viñëu everywhere. Angry at
not seeing Him, Hiraëyakaçipu screamed loudly and searched the entire

sanskrit:
the entire universe, but I could not find Viñëu, who has killed my

sanskrit:
until his death. Other people in the bodily concept of life maintain

very affectionate toward brähmaëas. Although he knew very well that it

sanskrit:
personalities who are householder brähmaëas, by your forefathers and

the Bahvåca-çruti, which says that a promise is truthful preceded by
the word oà and untruthful if not.

text: The Vedas enjoin that the factual result of the tree of the
sanskrit:
body is the good fruits and flowers derived from it. But if the bodily
tree does not exist, there is no possibility of factual fruits and
flowers. Even if the body is based on untruth, there cannot be factual
fruits and flowers without the help of the bodily tree.

text: When a tree is uprooted it immediately falls down and
sanskrit:
begins to dry up. Similarly, if one doesn't take care of the body, which
is supposed to be untruth-in other words, if the untruth is uprooted-the
body undoubtedly becomes dry.

text: The utterance of the word oà signifies separation from
sanskrit:
one's monetary assets. In other words, by uttering this word one becomes
free from attachment to money because his money is taken away from him.
To be without money is not very satisfactory, for in that position one
cannot fulfill one's desires. In other words, by using the word oà one
becomes poverty-stricken. Especially when one gives charity to a poor
man or beggar, one remains unfulfilled in self-realization and in sense
gratification.

text: Therefore, the safe course is to say no. Although it is a
sanskrit:
falsehood, it protects one completely, it draws the compassion of others
toward oneself, and it gives one full facility to collect money from
others for oneself. Nonetheless, if one always pleads that he has
nothing, he is condemned, for he is a dead body while living, or while
still breathing he should be killed.

text: In flattering a woman to bring her under control, in
sanskrit:
joking, in a marriage ceremony, in earning one's livelihood, when one's
life is in danger, in protecting cows and brahminical culture, or in
protecting a person from an enemy's hand, falsity is never condemned.
Translations 1-43

text: Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King Parékñit, when Bali
sanskrit:
Mahäräja was thus advised by his spiritual master, Çukräcärya, his
family priest, he remained silent for some time, and then, after full
deliberation, he replied to his spiritual master as follows.

text: Bali Mahäräja said: As you have already stated, the
sanskrit:
principle of religion that does not hinder one's economic development,
sense gratification, fame and means of livelihood is the real
occupational duty of the householder. I also think that this religious
principle is correct.

text: I am the grandson of Mahäräja Prahläda. How can I
sanskrit:
withdraw my promise because of greed for money when I have already said
that I shall give this land? How can I behave like an ordinary cheater,
especially toward a brähmaëa?

text: There is nothing more sinful than untruthfulness. Because of
sanskrit:
this, mother earth once said, "I can bear any heavy thing except a
person who is a liar."

text: I do not fear hell, poverty, an ocean of distress, falldown
sanskrit:
from my position or even death itself as much as I fear cheating a
brähmaëa.

text: My lord, you can also see that all the material opulences of
sanskrit:
this world are certainly separated from their possessor at death.
Therefore, if the brähmaëa Vämanadeva is not satisfied by whatever
gifts one has given, why not please Him with the riches one is destined
to lose at death?

text: Dadhéci, Çibi and many other great personalities were
sanskrit:
willing to sacrifice even their lives for the benefit of the people in
general. This is the evidence of history. So why not give up this
insignificant land? What is the serious consideration against it?

text: O best of the brähmaëas, certainly the great demoniac
sanskrit:
kings who were never reluctant to fight enjoyed this world, but in due
course of time everything they had was taken away, except their
reputation, by which they continue to exist. In other words, one should
try to achieve a good reputation instead of anything else.

text: O best of the brähmaëas, many men have laid down their
sanskrit:
lives on the battlefield, being unafraid of fighting, but rarely has one
gotten the chance to give his accumulated wealth faithfully to a saintly
person who creates holy places.

text: By giving charity, a benevolent and merciful person
sanskrit:
undoubtedly becomes even more auspicious, especially when he gives
charity to a person like your good self. Under the circumstances, I must
give this little brahmacäré whatever charity He wants from me.

text: O great sage, great saintly persons like you, being
sanskrit:
completely aware of the Vedic principles for performing ritualistic
ceremonies and yajïas, worship Lord Viñëu in all circumstances.
Therefore, whether that same Lord Viñëu has come here to give me all
benedictions or to punish me as an enemy, I must carry out His order and
give Him the requested tract of land without hesitation.

text: Although He is Viñëu Himself, out of fear He has covered
sanskrit:
Himself in the form of a brähmaëa to come to me begging. Under the
circumstances, because He has assumed the form of a brähmaëa, even if
He irreligiously arrests me or even kills me, I shall not retaliate,
although He is my enemy.

text: If this brähmaëa really is Lord Viñëu, who is worshiped
sanskrit:
by Vedic hymns, He would never give up His widespread reputation; either
He would lie down having been killed by me, or He would kill me in a
fight.

text: Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: Thereafter, the
sanskrit:
spiritual master, Çukräcärya, being inspired by the Supreme Lord,
cursed his exalted disciple Bali Mahäräja, who was so magnanimous and
fixed in truthfulness that instead of respecting his spiritual master's
instructions, he wanted to disobey his order.

text: Although you have no knowledge, you have become a so-called
sanskrit:
learned person, and therefore you dare be so impudent as to disobey my
order. Because of disobeying me, you shall very soon be bereft of all
your opulence.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: Even after being cursed in
sanskrit:
this way by his own spiritual master, Bali Mahäräja, being a great
personality, never deviated from his determination. Therefore, according
to custom, he first offered water to Vämanadeva and then offered Him
the gift of land he had promised.

text: Bali Mahäräja's wife, known as Vindhyävali, who was
sanskrit:
decorated with a necklace of pearls, immediately came and had a large
golden waterpot brought there, full of water with which to worship the
Lord by washing His feet.

text: Bali Mahäräja, the worshiper of Lord Vämanadeva,
sanskrit:
jubilantly washed the Lord's lotus feet and then took the water on his
head, for that water delivers the entire universe.

text: At that time, the residents of the higher planetary system,
sanskrit:
namely the demigods, the Gandharvas, the Vidyädharas, the Siddhas and
the Cäraëas, all being very pleased by Bali Mahäräja's simple,
nonduplicitous act, praised his qualities and showered upon him millions
of flowers.

text: The Gandharvas, the Kimpuruñas and the Kinnaras sounded
sanskrit:
thousands and thousands of kettledrums and trumpets again and again, and
they sang in great jubilation, declaring, "How exalted a person is Bali
Mahäräja, and what a difficult task he has performed! Even though he
knew that Lord Viñëu was on the side of his enemies, he nonetheless
gave the Lord the entire three worlds in charity."

text: The unlimited Supreme Personality of Godhead, who had
sanskrit:
assumed the form of Vämana, then began increasing in size, acting in
terms of the material energy, until everything in the universe was
within His body, including the earth, the planetary systems, the sky,
the directions, the various holes in the universe, the seas, the oceans,
the birds, beasts, human beings, the demigods and the great saintly
persons.

text: Bali Mahäräja, along with all the priests, äcäryas and
sanskrit:
members of the assembly, observed the Supreme Personality of Godhead's
universal body, which was full of six opulences. That body contained
everything within the universe, including all the gross material
elements, the senses, the sense objects, the mind, intelligence and
false ego, the various kinds of living entities, and the actions and
reactions of the three modes of material nature.

text: Thereafter, Bali Mahäräja, who was occupying the seat of
sanskrit:
King Indra, could see the lower planetary systems, such as Rasätala, on
the soles of the feet of the Lord's universal form. He saw on the Lord's
feet the surface of the globe, on the surface of His calves all the
mountains, on His knees the various birds, and on His thighs the
varieties of air.

text: Bali Mahäräja saw beneath the garments of the Lord, who
sanskrit:
acts wonderfully, the evening twilight. In the Lord's private parts he
saw the Prajäpatis, and in the round portion of the waist he saw
himself with his confidential associates. In the Lord's navel he saw the
sky, on the Lord's waist he saw the seven oceans, and on the Lord's
bosom he saw all the clusters of stars.

text: My dear King, on the heart of Lord Muräri he saw
sanskrit:
religion; on the chest, both pleasing words and truthfulness; in the
mind, the moon; on the bosom, the goddess of fortune, with a lotus
flower in her hand; on the neck, all the Vedas and all sound vibrations;
on the arms, all the demigods, headed by King Indra; in both ears, all
the directions; on the head, the upper planetary systems; on the hair,
the clouds; in the nostrils, the wind; on the eyes, the sun; and in the
mouth, fire. From His words came all the Vedic mantras, on His tongue
was the demigod of water, Varuëadeva, on His eyebrows were the
regulative principles, and on His eyelids were day and night. [When His
eyes were open it was daytime, and when they were closed it was night.]
On His forehead was anger, and on His lips was greed. O King, in His
touch were lusty desires, in His semen were all the waters, on His back
was irreligion, and in His wonderful activities or steps was the fire of
sacrifice. On His shadow was death, in His smile was the illusory
energy, and on the h

text: O King, when all the demons, the followers of Mahäräja
sanskrit:
Bali, saw the universal form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who
held everything within His body, when they saw in the Lord's hand His
disc, known as the Sudarçana cakra, which generates intolerable heat,
and when they heard the tumultuous sound of His bow, all of these caused
lamentation within their hearts.

text: The Lord's conchshell, named Päïcajanya, which made
sanskrit:
sounds like that of a cloud; the very forceful club named Kaumodaké;
the sword named Vidyädhara, with a shield decorated with hundreds of
moonlike spots; and also Akñayasäyaka, the best of quivers-all of
these appeared together to offer prayers to the Lord.

text: These associates, headed by Sunanda and other chief
sanskrit:
associates and accompanied by all the predominating deities of the
various planets, offered prayers to the Lord, who wore a brilliant
helmet, bracelets, and glittering earrings that resembled fish. On the
Lord's bosom were the lock of hair called Çrévatsa and the
transcendental jewel named Kaustubha. He wore a yellow garment, covered
by a belt, and He was decorated by a flower garland, surrounded by bees.
Manifesting Himself in this way, O King, the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, whose activities are wonderful, covered the entire surface of
the earth with one footstep, the sky with His body, and all directions
with His arms.

text: As the Lord took His second step, He covered the heavenly
sanskrit:
planets. And not even a spot remained for the third step, for the Lord's
foot extended higher and higher, beyond Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka
and even Satyaloka.

acts wonderfully, the evening twilight. In the Lord's private parts he
saw the Prajäpatis, and in the round portion of the waist he saw
himself with his confidential associates. In the Lord's navel he saw the
sky, on the Lord's waist he saw the seven oceans, and on the Lord's
bosom he saw all the clusters of stars.

text: My dear King, on the heart of Lord Muräri he saw
sanskrit:
religion; on the chest, both pleasing words and truthfulness; in the
mind, the moon; on the bosom, the goddess of fortune, with a lotus
flower in her hand; on the neck, all the Vedas and all sound vibrations;
on the arms, all the demigods, headed by King Indra; in both ears, all
the directions; on the head, the upper planetary systems; on the hair,
the clouds; in the nostrils, the wind; on the eyes, the sun; and in the
mouth, fire. From His words came all the Vedic mantras, on His tongue
was the demigod of water, Varuëadeva, on His eyebrows were the
regulative principles, and on His eyelids were day and night. [When His
eyes were open it was daytime, and when they were closed it was night.]
On His forehead was anger, and on His lips was greed. O King, in His
touch were lusty desires, in His semen were all the waters, on His back
was irreligion, and in His wonderful activities or steps was the fire of
sacrifice. On His shadow was death, in His smile was the illusory
energy, and on the h

text: O King, when all the demons, the followers of Mahäräja
sanskrit:
Bali, saw the universal form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who
held everything within His body, when they saw in the Lord's hand His
disc, known as the Sudarçana cakra, which generates intolerable heat,
and when they heard the tumultuous sound of His bow, all of these caused
lamentation within their hearts.

text: The Lord's conchshell, named Päïcajanya, which made
sanskrit:
sounds like that of a cloud; the very forceful club named Kaumodaké;
the sword named Vidyädhara, with a shield decorated with hundreds of
moonlike spots; and also Akñayasäyaka, the best of quivers-all of
these appeared together to offer prayers to the Lord.

text: These associates, headed by Sunanda and other chief
sanskrit:
associates and accompanied by all the predominating deities of the
various planets, offered prayers to the Lord, who wore a brilliant
helmet, bracelets, and glittering earrings that resembled fish. On the
Lord's bosom were the lock of hair called Çrévatsa and the
transcendental jewel named Kaustubha. He wore a yellow garment, covered
by a belt, and He was decorated by a flower garland, surrounded by bees.
Manifesting Himself in this way, O King, the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, whose activities are wonderful, covered the entire surface of
the earth with one footstep, the sky with His body, and all directions
with His arms.

text: As the Lord took His second step, He covered the heavenly
sanskrit:
planets. And not even a spot remained for the third step, for the Lord's
foot extended higher and higher, beyond Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka
and even Satyaloka.
Translations 1-34

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: When Lord Brahmä, who was
sanskrit:
born of a lotus flower, saw that the effulgence of his residence,
Brahmaloka, had been reduced by the glaring effulgence from the toenails
of Lord Vämanadeva, he approached the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
Lord Brahmä was accompanied by all the great sages, headed by Maréci,
and by yogés like Sanandana, but in the presence of that glaring
effulgence, O King, even Lord Brahmä and his associates seemed
insignificant.

text: Among the great personalities who came to worship the
sanskrit:
lotus feet of the Lord were those who had attained perfection in
self-control and regulative principles, as well as experts in logic,
history, general education and the Vedic literature known as kalpe
[dealing with old historical incidents]. Others were experts in the
Vedic corollaries like Brahma-saàhitä, all the other knowledge of the
Vedas [Säma, Yajur, Åg and Atharva], and also the supplementary Vedic
knowledge [Äyur-veda, Dhanur-veda, etc.]. Others were those who had
been freed of the reactions to fruitive activities by transcendental
knowledge awakened by practice of yoga. And still others were those who
had attained residence in Brahmaloka not by ordinary karma but by
advanced Vedic knowledge. After devotedly worshiping the upraised lotus
feet of the Supreme Lord with oblations of water, Lord Brahmä, who was
born of the lotus emanating from Lord Viñëu's navel, offered prayers
to the Lord.

text: O King, the water from Lord Brahmä's kamaëòalu washed the
sanskrit:
lotus feet of Lord Vämanadeva, who is known as Urukrama, the wonderful
actor. Thus that water became so pure that it was transformed into the
water of the Ganges, which went flowing down from the sky, purifying the
three worlds like the pure fame of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: Lord Brahmä and all the predominating deities of the
sanskrit:
various planetary systems began to worship Lord Vämanadeva, their
supreme master, who had reduced Himself from His all-pervading form to
His original form. They collected all the ingredients and paraphernalia
for this worship.

text: They worshiped the Lord by offering fragrant flowers,
sanskrit:
water, pädya and arghya, sandalwood pulp and aguru pulp, incense,
lamps, fused rice, unbroken grains, fruits, roots and sprouts. While so
doing, they offered prayers indicating the glorious activities of the
Lord and shouted "Jaya! Jaya!" They also danced, played instruments,
sang, sounded conchshells and beat kettledrums, in this way worshiping
the Lord.

text: Jämbavän, king of the bears, also joined in the ceremony.
sanskrit:
Sounding his bugle in all directions, he declared a great festival for
Lord Vämanadeva's victory.

text: When the demoniac followers of Mahäräja Bali saw that
sanskrit:
their master, who had been determined in performing sacrifice, had lost
all his possessions to Vämanadeva, who had taken them away on the plea
of begging three paces of land, they were very angry and spoke as
follows.

text: "This Vämana is certainly not a brähmaëa but the best of
sanskrit:
cheaters, Lord Viñëu. Assuming the form of a brähmaëa, He has
covered His own form, and thus He is working for the interests of the
demigods.

text: "Our lord, Bali Mahäräja, because of his position in
sanskrit:
performing the yajïa, has given up the power to punish. Taking
advantage of this, our eternal enemy, Viñëu, dressed in the form of a
brahmacäré beggar, has taken away all his possessions.

text: "Our lord, Bali Mahäräja, is always fixed in
sanskrit:
truthfulness, and this is especially so at present, since he has been
initiated into performing a sacrifice. He is always kind and merciful
toward the brähmaëas, and he cannot at any time speak lies.

text: "Therefore it is our duty to kill this Vämanadeva, Lord
sanskrit:
Viñëu. It is our religious principle and the way to serve our master."
After making this decision, the demoniac followers of Mahäräja Bali
took up their various weapons with a view to killing Vämanadeva.

text: O King, the demons, aggravated by their usual anger, took
sanskrit:
their lances and tridents in hand, and against the will of Bali
Mahäräja they pushed forward to kill Lord Vämanadeva.

text: O King, when the associates of Lord Viñëu saw the
sanskrit:
soldiers of the demons coming forward in violence, they smiled. Taking
up their weapons, they forbade the demons to continue their attempt.

text: Nanda, Sunanda, Jaya, Vijaya, Prabala, Bala, Kumuda,
sanskrit:
Kumudäkña, Viñvaksena, Patattriräö [Garuòa], Jayanta, Çrutadeva,
Puñpadanta and Sätvata were all associates of Lord Viñëu. They were
as powerful as ten thousand elephants, and now they began killing the
soldiers of the demons.

text: When Bali Mahäräja saw that his own soldiers were being
sanskrit:
killed by the associates of Lord Viñëu, he remembered the curse of
Çukräcärya and forbade his soldiers to continue fighting.

text: O Vipracitti, O Rähu, O Nemi, please hear my words! Don't
sanskrit: fight. Stop immediately, for the present time is not in our favor.

text: O Daityas, by human efforts no one can supersede the
sanskrit:
Supreme Personality of Godhead, who can bring happiness and distress to
all living entities.

text: The supreme time factor, which represents the Supreme
sanskrit:
Person, was previously in our favor and not in favor of the demigods,
but now that same time factor is against us.

text: No one can surpass the time representation of the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead by material power, by the counsel of ministers,
by intelligence, by diplomacy, by fortresses, by mystic mantras, by
drugs, by herbs or by any other means.

text: Previously, being empowered by providence, you defeated a
sanskrit:
great number of such followers of Lord Viñëu. But today those same
followers, having defeated us, are roaring in jubilation like lions.

text: Unless providence is in our favor, we shall not be able to
sanskrit:
gain victory. Therefore we must wait for that favorable time when our
defeating them will be possible.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: O King, in accordance with
sanskrit:
the order of their master, Bali Mahäräja, all the chiefs of the demons
and the Daityas entered the lower regions of the universe, to which they
were driven by the soldiers of Viñëu.

text: Thereafter, on the day of soma-päna, after the sacrifice
sanskrit:
was finished, Garuòa, king of the birds, understanding the desire of
his master, arrested Bali Mahäräja with the ropes of Varuëa.

text: When Bali Mahäräja was thus arrested by Lord Viñëu, who
sanskrit:
is the most powerful, there was a great roar of lamentation in all
directions throughout the upper and lower planetary systems of the
universe.

text: O King, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vämanadeva,
sanskrit:
then spoke to Bali Mahäräja, the most liberal and celebrated
personality whom He had arrested with the ropes of Varuëa. Bali
Mahäräja had lost all bodily luster, but he was nonetheless fixed in
his determination.

text: O King of the demons, you have promised to give Me three
sanskrit:
steps of land, but I have occupied the entire universe with two steps.
Now think about where I should put My third.

text: As far as the sun and moon shine with the stars and as far
sanskrit:
as the clouds pour rain, all the land throughout the universe is in your
possession.

text: Of these possessions, with one step I have occupied
sanskrit:
Bhürloka, and with My body I have occupied the entire sky and all
directions. And in your presence, with My second step, I have occupied
the upper planetary system.

text: Because you have been unable to give charity according to
sanskrit:
your promise, the rule is that you should go down to live in the hellish
planets. Therefore, in accordance with the order of Çukräcärya, your
spiritual master, now go down and live there.

text: Far from being elevated to the heavenly planets or
sanskrit:
fulfilling one's desire, one who does not properly give a beggar what he
has promised falls down to a hellish condition of life.

text: Being falsely proud of your possessions, you promised to
sanskrit:
give Me land, but you could not fulfill your promise. Therefore, because
your promise was false, you must live for a few years in hellish life.

sanskrit:
give Me land, but you could not fulfill your promise. Therefore, because
your promise was false, you must live for a few years in hellish life.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, although the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead was superficially seen to have acted
mischievously toward Bali Mahäräja, Bali Mahäräja was fixed in his
determination. Considering himself not to have fulfilled his promise, he
spoke as follows.

text: Bali Mahäräja said: O best Personality of Godhead, most
sanskrit:
worshipable for all the demigods, if You think that my promise has
become false, I shall certainly rectify matters to make it truthful. I
cannot allow my promise to be false. Please, therefore, place Your third
lotus footstep on my head.

text: I do not fear being deprived of all my possessions, living
sanskrit:
in hellish life, being arrested for poverty by the ropes of Varuëa or
being punished by You as much as I fear defamation.

text: Although a father, mother, brother or friend may sometimes
sanskrit:
punish one as a well-wisher, they never punish their subordinate like
this. But because You are the most worshipable Lord, I regard the
punishment You have given me as most exalted.

text: Since Your Lordship is indirectly the greatest well-wisher
sanskrit:
of us demons, You act for our best welfare by posing as if our enemy.
Because demons like us always aspire for a position of false prestige,
by chastising us You give us the eyes by which to see the right path.

text: Many demons who were continuously inimical toward You
sanskrit:
finally achieved the perfection of great mystic yogés. Your Lordship
can perform one work to serve many purposes, and consequently, although
You have punished me in many ways, I do not feel ashamed of having been
arrested by the ropes of Varuëa, nor do I feel aggrieved.

text: My grandfather Prahläda Mahäräja is famous, being
sanskrit:
recognized by all Your devotees. Although harassed in many ways by his
father, Hiraëyakaçipu, he still remained faithful, taking shelter at
Your lotus feet.

text: What is the use of the material body, which automatically
sanskrit:
leaves its owner at the end of life? And what is the use of all one's
family members, who are actually plunderers taking away money that is
useful for the service of the Lord in spiritual opulence? What is the
use of a wife? She is only the source of increasing material conditions.
And what is the use of family, home, country and community? Attachment
for them merely wastes the valuable energy of one's lifetime.

text: My grandfather, the best of all men, who achieved unlimited
sanskrit:
knowledge and was worshipable for everyone, was afraid of the common men
in this world. Being fully convinced of the substantiality afforded by
shelter at Your lotus feet, He took shelter of Your lotus feet, against
the will of his father and demoniac friends, who were killed by Your own
self.

text: Only by providence have I been forcibly brought under Your
sanskrit:
lotus feet and deprived of all my opulence. Because of the illusion
created by temporary opulence, people in general, who live under
material conditions, facing accidental death at every moment, do not
understand that this life is temporary. Only by providence have I been
saved from that condition.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O best of the Kurus, while Bali
sanskrit:
Mahäräja was describing his fortunate position in this way, the most
dear devotee of the Lord, Prahläda Mahäräja, appeared there, like the
moon rising in the nighttime.

text: Then Bali Mahäräja saw his grandfather Prahläda
sanskrit:
Mahäräja, the most fortunate personality, whose dark body resembled
black ointment for the eyes. His tall, elegant figure was dressed in
yellow garments, he had long arms, and his beautiful eyes were like the
petals of a lotus. He was very dear and pleasing to everyone.

text: Being bound by the ropes of Varuëa, Bali Mahäräja could
sanskrit:
not offer befitting respect to Prahläda Mahäräja as he had before.
Rather, he simply offered respectful obeisances with his head, his eyes
being inundated with tears and his face lowered in shame.

text: When the great personality Prahläda Mahäräja saw that
sanskrit:
the Supreme Lord was sitting there, surrounded and worshiped by His
intimate associates like Sunanda, he was overwhelmed with tears of
jubilation. Approaching the Lord and falling to the ground, he offered
obeisances to the Lord with his head.

text: Prahläda Mahäräja said: My Lord, it is Your Lordship who
sanskrit:
gave this Bali the very great opulence of the post of heavenly king, and
now, today, it is You who have taken it all away. I think You have acted
with equal beauty in both ways. Because his exalted position as King of
heaven was putting him in the darkness of ignorance, You have done him a
very merciful favor by taking away all his opulence.

text: Material opulence is so bewildering that it makes even a
sanskrit:
learned, self-controlled man forget to search for the goal of
self-realization. But the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Näräyaëa,
the Lord of the universe, can see everything by His will. Therefore I
offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: O King Parékñit, Lord
sanskrit:
Brahmä then began to speak to the Supreme Personality of Godhead,
within the hearing of Prahläda Mahäräja, who stood nearby with folded
hands.

text: But Bali Mahäräja's chaste wife, afraid and aggrieved at
sanskrit:
seeing her husband arrested, immediately offered obeisances to Lord
Vämanadeva [Upendra]. She folded her hands and spoke as follows.

text: Çrématé Vindhyävali said: O my Lord, You have created
sanskrit:
the entire universe for the enjoyment of Your personal pastimes, but
foolish, unintelligent men have claimed proprietorship for material
enjoyment. Certainly they are shameless agnostics. Falsely claiming
proprietorship, they think they can give charity and enjoy. In such a
condition, what good can they do for You, who are the independent
creator, maintainer and annihilator of this universe?

text: Lord Brahmä said: O well-wisher and master of all living
sanskrit:
entities, O worshipable Deity of all the demigods, O all-pervading
Personality of Godhead, now this man has been sufficiently punished, for
You have taken everything. Now You can release him. He does not deserve
to be punished more.

text: Bali Mahäräja had already offered everything to Your
sanskrit:
Lordship. Without hesitation, he has offered his land, the planets and
whatever else he earned by his pious activities, including even his own
body.

text: By offering even water, newly grown grass, or flower buds
sanskrit:
at Your lotus feet, those who maintain no mental duplicity can achieve
the most exalted position within the spiritual world. This Bali
Mahäräja, without duplicity, has now offered everything in the three
worlds. How then can he deserve to suffer from arrest?

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: My dear Lord
sanskrit:
Brahmä, because of material opulence a foolish person becomes
dull-witted and mad. Thus he has no respect for anyone within the three
worlds and defies even My authority. To such a person I show special
favor by first taking away all his possessions.

text: While rotating in the cycle of birth and death again and
sanskrit:
again in different species because of his own fruitive activities, the
dependent living entity, by good fortune, may happen to become a human
being. This human birth is very rarely obtained.

text: If a human being is born in an aristocratic family or a
sanskrit:
higher status of life, if he performs wonderful activities, if he is
youthful, if he has personal beauty, a good education and good wealth,
and if he is nonetheless not proud of his opulences, it is to be
understood that he is especially favored by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead.

text: Although aristocratic birth and other such opulences are
sanskrit:
impediments to advancement in devotional service because they are causes
of false prestige and pride, these opulences never disturb a pure
devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

text: Bali Mahäräja has become the most famous among the demons
sanskrit:
and nonbelievers, for in spite of being bereft of all material
opulences, he is fixed in his devotional service.

text: Although bereft of his riches, fallen from his original
sanskrit:
position, defeated and arrested by his enemies, rebuked and deserted by
his relatives and friends, although suffering the pain of being bound
and although rebuked and cursed by his spiritual master, Bali
Mahäräja, being fixed in his vow, did not give up his truthfulness. It
was certainly with pretension that I spoke about religious principles,
but he did not give up religious principles, for he is true to his word.

text: The Lord continued: Because of his great tolerance, I have
sanskrit:
given him a place not obtainable even by the demigods. He will become
King of the heavenly planets during the period of the Manu known as
Sävarëi.

text: Until Bali Mahäräja achieves the position of King of
sanskrit:
heaven, he shall live on the planet Sutala, which was made by
Viçvakarmä according to My order. Because it is especially protected
by Me, it is free from mental and bodily miseries, fatigue, dizziness,
defeat and all other disturbances. Bali Mahäräja, you may now go live
there peacefully.

text: O Bali Mahäräja [Indrasena], now you may go to the planet
sanskrit:
Sutala, which is desired even by the demigods. Live there peacefully,
surrounded by your friends and relatives. All good fortune unto you.

text: On the planet Sutala, not even the predominating deities of
sanskrit:
other planets, what to speak of ordinary people, will be able to conquer
you. As far as the demons are concerned, if they transgress your rule,
My disc will kill them.

text: O great hero, I shall always be with you and give you
sanskrit:
protection in all respects along with your associates and paraphernalia.
Moreover, you will always be able to see Me there.

text: Because there you will see My supreme prowess, your
sanskrit:
materialistic ideas and anxieties that have arisen from your association
with the demons and Dänavas will immediately be vanquished.

heaven, he shall live on the planet Sutala, which was made by
Viçvakarmä according to My order. Because it is especially protected
by Me, it is free from mental and bodily miseries, fatigue, dizziness,
defeat and all other disturbances. Bali Mahäräja, you may now go live
there peacefully.

text: O Bali Mahäräja [Indrasena], now you may go to the planet
sanskrit:
Sutala, which is desired even by the demigods. Live there peacefully,
surrounded by your friends and relatives. All good fortune unto you.

text: On the planet Sutala, not even the predominating deities of
sanskrit:
other planets, what to speak of ordinary people, will be able to conquer
you. As far as the demons are concerned, if they transgress your rule,
My disc will kill them.

text: O great hero, I shall always be with you and give you
sanskrit:
protection in all respects along with your associates and paraphernalia.
Moreover, you will always be able to see Me there.

text: Because there you will see My supreme prowess, your
sanskrit:
materialistic ideas and anxieties that have arisen from your association
with the demons and Dänavas will immediately be vanquished.
Translations 1-36

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: When the supreme, ancient, eternal
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead had thus spoken to Bali Mahäräja, who is
universally accepted as a pure devotee of the Lord and therefore a great
soul, Bali Mahäräja, his eyes filled with tears, his hands folded and
his voice faltering in devotional ecstasy, responded as follows.

text: Bali Mahäräja said: What a wonderful effect there is in
sanskrit:
even attempting to offer respectful obeisances to You! I merely
endeavored to offer You obeisances, but nonetheless the attempt was as
successful as those of pure devotees. The causeless mercy You have shown
to me, a fallen demon, was never achieved even by the demigods or the
leaders of the various planets.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: After speaking in this way,
sanskrit:
Bali Mahäräja offered his obeisances first to the Supreme Personality
of Godhead, Hari, and then to Lord Brahmä and Lord Çiva. Thus he was
released from the bondage of the näga-päça [the ropes of Varuëa],
and in full satisfaction he entered the planet known as Sutala.

text: Thus having delivered the proprietorship of the heavenly
sanskrit:
planets to Indra and having fulfilled the desire of Aditi, mother of the
demigods, the Supreme Personality of Godhead ruled the affairs of the
universe.

text: When Prahläda Mahäräja heard how Bali Mahäräja, his
sanskrit:
grandson and descendant, had been released from bondage and had achieved
the benediction of the Lord, he spoke as follows in a tone of greatly
ecstatic devotion.

text: Prahläda Mahäräja said: O Supreme Personality of Godhead,
sanskrit:
You are universally worshiped; even Lord Brahmä and Lord Çiva worship
Your lotus feet. Yet although You are such a great personality, You have
kindly promised to protect us, the demons. I think that such kindness
has never been achieved even by Lord Brahmä, Lord Çiva or the goddess
of fortune, Lakñmé, what to speak of other demigods or common people.

text: O supreme shelter of everyone, great personalities like
sanskrit:
Brahmä enjoy their perfection simply by tasting the honey of rendering
service at Your lotus feet. But as for us, who are all rogues and
debauchees born of an envious family of demons, how have we received
Your mercy? It has been possible only because Your mercy is causeless.

text: O my Lord, Your pastimes are all wonderfully performed by
sanskrit:
Your inconceivable spiritual energy; and by her perverted reflection,
the material energy, You have created all the universes. As the
Supersoul of all living entities, You are aware of everything, and
therefore You are certainly equal toward everyone. Nonetheless, You
favor Your devotees. This is not partiality, however, for Your
characteristic is just like that of a desire tree, which yields
everything according to one's desire.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: My dear son
sanskrit:
Prahläda, all good fortune unto you. For the time being, please go to
the place known as Sutala and there enjoy happiness with your grandson
and your other relatives and friends.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead assured Prahläda
sanskrit:
Mahäräja: You shall be able to see Me there in My usual feature with
conchshell, disc, club and lotus in My hand. Because of your
transcendental bliss due to always personally seeing Me, you will have
no further bondage to fruitive activities.

text: Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé said: Accompanied by Bali
sanskrit:
Mahäräja, my dear King Parékñit, Prahläda Mahäräja, the master of
all the chiefs of the demons, took the Supreme Lord's order on his head
with folded hands. After saying yes to the Lord, circumambulating Him
and offering Him respectful obeisances, he entered the lower planetary
system known as Sutala.

text: Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Näräyaëa,
sanskrit:
thereafter addressed Çukräcärya, who was sitting nearby in the midst
of the assembly with the priests [brahma, hotä, udgätä and adhvaryu].
O Mahäräja Parékñit, these priests were all brahma-vädés,
followers of the Vedic principles for performing sacrifices.

text: O best of the brähmaëas, Çukräcärya, please describe
sanskrit:
the fault or discrepancy in your disciple Bali Mahäräja, who engaged
in performing sacrifices. This fault will be nullified when judged in
the presence of qualified brähmaëas.

text: Çukräcärya said: My Lord, You are the enjoyer and
sanskrit:
lawgiver in all performances of sacrifice, and You are the
yajïa-puruña, the person to whom all sacrifices are offered. If one
has fully satisfied You, where is the chance of discrepancies or faults
in his performances of sacrifice?

text: There may be discrepancies in pronouncing the mantras and
sanskrit:
observing the regulative principles, and, moreover, there may be
discrepancies in regard to time, place, person and paraphernalia. But
when Your Lordship's holy name is chanted, everything becomes faultless.

text: Lord Viñëu, I must nonetheless act in obedience to Your
sanskrit:
order because obeying Your order is most auspicious and is the first
duty of everyone.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: In this way, the most
sanskrit:
powerful Çukräcärya accepted the order of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead with full respect. Along with the best brähmaëas, he began to
compensate for the discrepancies in the sacrifices performed by Bali
Mahäräja.

text: O King Parékñit, thus having taken all the land of Bali
sanskrit:
Mahäräja by begging, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord
Vämanadeva, delivered to His brother Indra all the land taken away by
Indra's enemy.

text: Lord Brahmä [the master of King Dakña and all other
sanskrit:
Prajäpatis], accompanied by all the demigods, the great saintly
persons, the inhabitants of Pitåloka, the Manus, the munis, and such
leaders as Dakña, Bhågu and Aìgirä, as well as Kärttikeya and Lord
Çiva, accepted Lord Vämanadeva as the protector of everyone. He did
this for the pleasure of Kaçyapa Muni and his wife Aditi and for the
welfare of all the inhabitants of the universe, including their various
leaders.

text: O King Parékñit, Indra was considered the King of all
sanskrit:
the universe, but the demigods, headed by Lord Brahmä, wanted Upendra,
Lord Vämanadeva, as the protector of the Vedas, the principles of
religion, fame, opulence, auspiciousness, vows, elevation to the higher
planetary system, and liberation. Thus they accepted Upendra, Lord
Vämanadeva, as the supreme master of everything. This decision made all
living entities extremely happy.

text: Thereafter, along with all the leaders of the heavenly
sanskrit:
planets, Indra, the King of heaven, placed Lord Vämanadeva before him
and, with the approval of Lord Brahmä, brought Him to the heavenly
planet in a celestial airplane.

text: Indra, King of heaven, being protected by the arms of
sanskrit:
Vämanadeva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, thus regained his rule
of the three worlds and was reinstated in his own position, supremely
opulent, fearless and fully satisfied.

text: Lord Brahmä, Lord Çiva, Lord Kärttikeya, the great
sanskrit:
sage Bhågu, other saintly persons, the inhabitants of Pitåloka and all
other living entities present, including the inhabitants of Siddhaloka
and living entities who travel in outer space by airplane, all glorified
the uncommon activities of Lord Vämanadeva. O King, while chanting
about and glorifying the Lord, they returned to their respective
heavenly planets. They also praised the position of Aditi.

text: O Mahäräja Parékñit, pleasure of your dynasty, I have
sanskrit:
now described to you everything about the wonderful activities of the
Supreme Personality of Godhead Vämanadeva. Those who hear about this
are certainly freed from all the results of sinful activities.

text: One who is subject to death cannot measure the glories of
sanskrit:
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Trivikrama, Lord Viñëu, any more
than he can count the number of atoms on the entire planet earth. No
one, whether born already or destined to take birth, is able to do this.
This has been sung by the great sage Vasiñöha.

text: If one hears about the uncommon activities of the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead in His various incarnations, he is certainly
elevated to the higher planetary system or even brought back home, back
to Godhead.

text: Whenever the activities of Vämanadeva are described in the
sanskrit:
course of a ritualistic ceremony, whether the ceremony be performed to
please the demigods, to please one's forefathers in Pitåloka, or to
celebrate a social event like a marriage, that ceremony should be
understood to be extremely auspicious.

Translations 1-31

text: Mahäräja Parékñit said: The Supreme Personality of
sanskrit:
Godhead, Hari, is eternally situated in His transcendental position, yet
He descends to this material world and manifests Himself in various
incarnations. His first incarnation was that of a great fish. O most
powerful Çukadeva Gosvämé, I wish to hear from you the pastimes of
that fish incarnation.

text: What was the purpose for which the Supreme Personality of
sanskrit:
Godhead accepted the abominable form of a fish, exactly as an ordinary
living being accepts different forms under the laws of karma? The form
of a fish is certainly condemned and full of terrible pain. O my lord,
what was the purpose of this incarnation? Kindly explain this to us, for
hearing about the pastimes of the Lord is auspicious for everyone.

Godhead accepted the abominable form of a fish, exactly as an ordinary
living being accepts different forms under the laws of karma? The form
of a fish is certainly condemned and full of terrible pain. O my lord,
what was the purpose of this incarnation? Kindly explain this to us, for
hearing about the pastimes of the Lord is auspicious for everyone.

text: Süta Gosvämé said: When Parékñit Mahäräja thus
sanskrit:
inquired from Çukadeva Gosvämé, that most powerful saintly person
began describing the pastimes of the Lord's incarnation as a fish.

text: Çré Çukadeva Gosvämé said: O King, for the sake of
sanskrit:
protecting the cows, brähmaëas, demigods, devotees, the Vedic
literature, religious principles, and principles to fulfill the purpose
of life, the Supreme Personality of Godhead accepts the forms of
incarnations.

text: Like the air passing through different types of atmosphere,
sanskrit:
the Supreme Personality of Godhead, although appearing sometimes as a
human being and sometimes as a lower animal, is always transcendental.
Because He is above the material modes of nature, He is unaffected by
higher and lower forms.

text: O King Parékñit, at the end of the past millennium, at the
At the end of Brahmä's day, when Brahmä felt sleepy and
sanskrit:
desired to lie down, the Vedas were emanating from his mouth, and the
great demon named Hayagréva stole the Vedic knowledge.

text: Understanding the acts of the great demon Hayagréva, the
sanskrit:
Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, who is full of all opulences,
assumed the form of a fish and saved the Vedas by killing the demon.

text: During the Cäkñuña-manvantara there was a great king
sanskrit:
named Satyavrata who was a great devotee of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead. Satyavrata performed austerities by subsisting only on water.

text: In this [the present] millennium King Satyavrata later
sanskrit:
became the son of Vivasvän, the king of the sun planet, and was known
as Çräddhadeva. By the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he
was given the post of Manu.

text: One day while King Satyavrata was performing austerities by
sanskrit:
offering water on the bank of the River Kåtamälä, a small fish
appeared in the water in his palms.

text: Satyavrata, the King of Draviòadeça, threw the fish into
sanskrit:
the water of the river along with the water in his palm, O King
Parékñit, descendant of Bharata.

text: With an appealing voice, the poor small fish said to King
sanskrit:
Satyavrata, who was very merciful: My dear King, protector of the poor,
why are you throwing Me in the water of the river, where there are other
aquatics who can kill Me? I am very much afraid of them.

text: To please himself, King Satyavrata, not knowing that the
sanskrit:
fish was the Supreme Personality of Godhead, decided with great pleasure
to give the fish protection.

text: The merciful King, being moved by the pitiable words of the
sanskrit:
fish, placed the fish in a water jug and brought Him to his own
residence.

text: But in one night that fish grew so much that He could not
sanskrit:
move His body comfortably in the water of the pot. He then spoke to the
King as follows.

text: O My dear King, I do not like living in this waterpot with
sanskrit:
such great difficulty. Therefore, please find some better reservoir of
water where I can live comfortably.

text: Then, taking the fish out of the waterpot, the King threw
sanskrit:
Him in a large well. But within a moment the fish developed to the
length of three cubits.

text: The fish then said: My dear King, this reservoir of water
sanskrit:
is not fit for My happy residence. Please give Me a more extensive pool
of water, for I have taken shelter of you.

text: O Mahäräja Parékñit, the King took the fish from the
sanskrit:
well and threw Him in a lake, but the fish then assumed a gigantic form
exceeding the extent of the water.

text: The fish then said: O King, I am a large aquatic, and this
sanskrit:
water is not at all suitable for Me. Now kindly find some way to save
Me. It would be better to put Me in the water of a lake that will never
reduce.

text: When thus requested, King Satyavrata took the fish to the
sanskrit:
largest reservoir of water. But when that also proved insufficient, the
King at last threw the gigantic fish into the ocean.

text: While being thrown in the ocean, the fish said to King
sanskrit:
Satyavrata: O hero, in this water there are very powerful and dangerous
sharks that will eat Me. Therefore you should not throw Me in this
place.

text: After hearing these sweet words from the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead in the form of a fish, the King, being
bewildered, asked Him: Who are You, sir? You simply bewilder us.

text: My Lord, in one day You have expanded Yourself for hundreds
sanskrit:
of miles, covering the water of the river and the ocean. Before this I
had never seen or heard of such an aquatic animal.

text: My Lord, You are certainly the inexhaustible Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, Näräyaëa, Çré Hari. It is to show Your
mercy to the living entities that You have now assumed the form of an
aquatic.

text: O my Lord, master of creation, maintenance and
sanskrit:
annihilation, O best of enjoyers, Lord Viñëu, You are the leader and
destination of surrendered devotees like us. Therefore let me offer my
respectful obeisances unto You.

text: All Your pastimes and incarnations certainly appear for the
sanskrit:
welfare of all living entities. Therefore, my Lord, I wish to know the
purpose for which You have assumed this form of a fish.

text: O my Lord, possessing eyes like the petals of a lotus, the
sanskrit:
worship of the demigods, who are in the bodily concept of life, is
fruitless in all respects. But because You are the supreme friend and
dearmost Supersoul of everyone, worship of Your lotus feet is never
useless. You have therefore manifested Your form as a fish.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: When King Satyavrata spoke in
sanskrit:
this way, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who at the end of the yuga
had assumed the form of a fish to benefit His devotee and enjoy His
pastimes in the water of inundation, responded as follows.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O King, who can
sanskrit:
subdue your enemies, on the seventh day from today the three
worlds-Bhüù, Bhuvaù and Svaù-will all merge into the water of
inundation.

text: When all the three worlds merge into the water, a large
sanskrit: boat sent by Me will appear before you.

text: Thereafter, O King, you shall collect all types of herbs
sanskrit:
and seeds and load them on that great boat. Then, accompanied by the
seven åñis and surrounded by all kinds of living entities, you shall
get aboard that boat, and without moroseness you shall easily travel
with your companions on the ocean of inundation, the only illumination
being the effulgence of the great åñis.

text: Then, as the boat is tossed about by the powerful winds,
sanskrit:
attach the vessel to My horn by means of the great serpent Väsuki, for
I shall be present by your side.

text: Pulling the boat, with you and all the åñis in it, O
sanskrit:
King, I shall travel in the water of devastation until the night of Lord
Brahmä's slumber is over.

text: You will be thoroughly advised and favored by Me, and
sanskrit:
because of your inquiries, everything about My glories, which are known
as paraà brahma, will be manifest within your heart. Thus you will know
everything about Me.

text: After thus instructing the King, the Supreme Personality of
sanskrit:
Godhead immediately disappeared. Then King Satyavrata began to wait for
that time of which the Lord had instructed.

text: After spreading kuça with its tips pointing east, the
sanskrit:
saintly King, himself facing the northeast, sat down on the grass and
began to meditate upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viñëu, who
had assumed the form of a fish.

text: Thereafter, gigantic clouds pouring incessant water swelled
sanskrit:
the ocean more and more. Thus the ocean began to overflow onto the land
and inundate the entire world.

text: As Satyavrata remembered the order of the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, he saw a boat coming near him. Thus he collected
herbs and creepers, and, accompanied by saintly brähmaëas, he got
aboard the boat.

text: The saintly brähmaëas, being pleased with the King, said
sanskrit:
to him: O King, please meditate upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead,
Keçava. He will save us from this impending danger and arrange for our
well-being.

text: Then, while the King constantly meditated upon the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, a large golden fish appeared in the ocean of
inundation. The fish had one horn and was eight million miles long.

text: Following the instructions formerly given by the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, the King anchored the boat to the fish's horn,
using the serpent Väsuki as a rope. Thus being satisfied, he began
offering prayers to the Lord.

text: The King said: By the grace of the Lord, those who have
sanskrit:
lost their self-knowledge since time immemorial, and who because of this
ignorance are involved in a material, conditional life full of miseries,
obtain the chance to meet the Lord's devotee. I accept that Supreme
Personality of Godhead as the supreme spiritual master.

text: In hopes of becoming happy in this material world, the
sanskrit:
foolish conditioned soul performs fruitive activities that result only
in suffering. But by rendering service to the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, one becomes free from such false desires for happiness. May my
supreme spiritual master cut the knot of false desires from the core of
my heart.

text: One who wants to be free of material entanglement should
sanskrit:
take to the service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and give up
the contamination of ignorance, involving pious and impious activities.
Thus one regains his original identity, just as a block of gold or
silver sheds all dirt and becomes purified when treated with fire. May
that inexhaustible Supreme Personality of Godhead become our spiritual
master, for He is the original spiritual master of all other spiritual
masters.

text: Neither all the demigods, nor the so-called gurus nor all
sanskrit:
other people, either independently or together, can offer mercy that
equals even one ten-thousandth of Yours. Therefore I wish to take
shelter of Your lotus feet.

text: As a blind man, being unable to see, accepts another blind
sanskrit:
man as his leader, people who do not know the goal of life accept
someone as a guru who is a rascal and a fool. But we are interested in
self-realization. Therefore we accept You, the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, as our spiritual master, for You are able to see in all
directions and are omniscient like the sun.

text: A materialistic so-called guru instructs his materialistic
sanskrit:
disciples about economic development and sense gratification, and
because of such instructions the foolish disciples continue in the
materialistic existence of ignorance. But Your Lordship gives knowledge
that is eternal, and the intelligent person receiving such knowledge is
quickly situated in his original constitutional position.

text: My Lord, You are the supreme well-wishing friend of
sanskrit:
everyone, the dearmost friend, the controller, the Supersoul, the
supreme instructor and the giver of supreme knowledge and the
fulfillment of all desires. But although You are within the heart, the
foolish, because of lusty desires in the heart, cannot understand You.

text: O Supreme Lord, for self-realization I surrender unto You,
sanskrit:
who are worshiped by the demigods as the supreme controller of
everything. By Your instructions, exposing life's purpose, kindly cut
the knot from the core of my heart and let me know the destination of my
life.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé continued: When Satyavrata had thus
sanskrit:
prayed to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who had assumed the form
of a fish, the Lord, while moving in the water of inundation, explained
to him the Absolute Truth.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead thus explained to King
sanskrit:
Satyavrata the spiritual science known as säìkhya-yoga, the science by
which one distinguishes between matter and spirit [in other words,
bhakti-yoga], along with the instructions contained in the Puräëas
[the old histories] and the saàhitäs. The Lord explained Himself in
all these literatures.

text: While sitting in the boat, King Satyavrata, accompanied by
sanskrit:
the great saintly persons, listened to the instructions of the Supreme
Personality of Godhead in regard to self-realization. These instructions
were all from the eternal Vedic literature [brahma]. Thus the King and
sages had no doubt about the Absolute Truth.

text: At the end of the last inundation [during the period of
sanskrit:
Sväyambhuva Manu] the Supreme Personality of Godhead killed the demon
named Hayagréva and delivered all the Vedic literatures to Lord Brahmä
when Lord Brahmä awakened from sleeping.

text: King Satyavrata was illuminated with all Vedic knowledge by
sanskrit:
the mercy of Lord Viñëu, and in this period he has now taken birth as
Vaivasvata Manu, the son of the sun-god.

text: This story concerning the great King Satyavrata and the
sanskrit:
fish incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viñëu, is a
great transcendental narration. Anyone who hears it is delivered from
the reactions of sinful life.

text: One who narrates this description of the Matsya incarnation
sanskrit:
and King Satyavrata will certainly have all his ambitions fulfilled, and
he will undoubtedly return home, back to Godhead.

text: I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme
sanskrit:
Personality of Godhead, who pretended to be a gigantic fish, who
restored the Vedic literature to Lord Brahmä when Lord Brahmä awakened
from sleep, and who explained the essence of Vedic literature to King
Satyavrata and the great saintly persons.

text:
O learned brähmaëa, Çukadeva Gosvämé, the great learned persons who are completely intelligent describe the activities and appearance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead during the various manvantaras. We are very eager to hear about these narrations. Kindly describe them.

The Supreme Personality of Godhead has different varieties of incarnations, including the guëa-avatäras, manvantara-avatäras, lélä-avatäras and yuga-avatäras, all of which are described in the çästras. Without reference to the çästras there can be no question of accepting anyone as an incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore, as especially mentioned here, gåëanti kavayaù: the descriptions of various incarnations are accepted by great learned scholars with perfect intelligence. At the present time, especially in India, so many rascals are claiming to be incarnations, and people are being misled. Therefore, the identity of an incarnation should be confirmed by the descriptions of the çästras and by wonderful activities. As described in this verse by the word mahéyasaù, the activities of an incarnation are not ordinary magic or jugglery, but are wonderful activities. Thus any incarnation of the Supreme Personality of Godhead must be supported by the statements of the çästra and must actually perform wonderful activities. Parékñit Mahäräja was eager to hear about the Manus of different ages. There are fourteen Manus during a day of Brahmä, and the age of each Manu lasts for seventy-one yugas. Thus there are thousands of Manus during the life of Brahmä.

text:
O learned brähmaëa, kindly describe to us whatever activities the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who created this cosmic manifestation, has performed in the past manvantaras, is performing at present, and will perform in the future manvantaras.

In Bhagavad-gétä the Supreme Personality of Godhead said that both He and the other living entities present on the battlefield had existed in the past, they existed at present, and they would continue to exist in the future. Past, present and future always exist, both for the Supreme Personality of Godhead and for ordinary living entities. Nityo nityänäà cetanaç cetanänäm. Both the Lord and the living entities are eternal and sentient, but the difference is that the Lord is unlimited whereas the living entities are limited. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is the creator of everything, and although the living entities are not created but exist with the Lord eternally, their bodies are created, whereas the Supreme Lord's body is never created. There is no difference between the Supreme Lord and His body, but the conditioned soul, although eternal, is different from his body.
