Jayadhvaja, Çürasena, Våñabha, Madhu and Ürjita.

text: Jayadhvaja had a son named Tälajaìgha, who had one
sanskrit:
hundred sons. All the kñatriyas in that dynasty, known as Tälajaìgha,
were annihilated by the great power received by Mahäräja Sagara from
Aurva Åñi.

text: Of the sons of Tälajaìgha, Vétihotra was the eldest. The
sanskrit:
son of Vétihotra named Madhu had a celebrated son named Våñëi. Madhu
had one hundred sons, of whom Våñëi was the eldest. The dynasties
known as Yädava, Mädhava and Våñëi had their origin from Yadu,
Madhu and Våñëi.

text: O Mahäräja Parékñit, because Yadu, Madhu and
sanskrit:
Våñëi each inaugurated a dynasty, their dynasties are known as
Yädava, Mädhava and Våñëi. The son of Yadu named Kroñöä had a
son named Våjinavän. The son of Våjinavän was Svähita; the son of
Svähita, Viñadgu; the son of Viñadgu, Citraratha; and the son of
Citraratha, Çaçabindu. The greatly fortunate Çaçabindu, who was a
great mystic, possessed fourteen opulences and was the owner of fourteen
great jewels. Thus he became the emperor of the world.

text: The famous Çaçabindu had ten thousand wives, and by each
sanskrit:
he begot a lakh of sons. Therefore the number of his sons was ten
thousand lakhs.

text: Among these many sons, six were the foremost, such as
sanskrit:
Påthuçravä and Påthukérti. The son of Påthuçravä was known as
Dharma, and his son was known as Uçanä. Uçanä was the performer of
one hundred horse sacrifices.

text: The son of Uçanä was Rucaka, who had five sons-Purujit,
sanskrit:
Rukma, Rukmeñu, Påthu and Jyämagha. Please hear of these sons from
me.

text: Jyämagha had no sons, but because he was fearful of his
sanskrit:
wife, Çaibyä, he could not accept another wife. Jyämagha once took
from the house of some royal enemy a girl who was a prostitute, but upon
seeing her Çaibyä was very angry and said to her husband, "My husband,
you cheater, who is this girl sitting upon my seat on the chariot?"
Jyämagha then replied, "This girl will be your daughter-in-law." Upon
hearing these joking words, Çaibyä smilingly replied.

text: Çaibyä said, "I am sterile and have no co-wife. How can
sanskrit:
this girl be my daughter-in-law? Please tell me." Jyämagha replied, "My
dear Queen, I shall see that you indeed have a son and that this girl
will be your daughter-in-law."

text: Long, long ago, Jyämagha had satisfied the demigods and
sanskrit:
Pitäs by worshiping them. Now, by their mercy, Jyämagha's words came
true. Although Çaibyä was barren, by the grace of the demigods she
became pregnant and in due course of time gave birth to a child named
Vidarbha. Before the child's birth, the girl had been accepted as a
daughter-in-law, and therefore Vidarbha actually married her when he
grew up.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: By the womb of the girl brought by
sanskrit:
his father, Vidarbha begot three sons, named Kuça, Kratha and
Romapäda. Romapäda was the favorite in the dynasty of Vidarbha.

text: The son of Romapäda was Babhru, from whom there came a son
sanskrit:
named Kåti. The son of Kåti was Uçika, and the son of Uçika was
Cedi. From Cedi was born the king known as Caidya and others.

text: The son of Kratha was Kunti; the son of Kunti, Våñëi;
sanskrit:
the son of Våñëi, Nirvåti; and the son of Nirvåti, Daçärha. From
Daçärha came Vyoma; from Vyoma came Jémüta; from Jémüta, Vikåti;
from Vikåti, Bhémaratha; from Bhémaratha, Navaratha; and from
Navaratha, Daçaratha.

text: From Daçaratha came a son named Çakuni and from Çakuni a
sanskrit:
son named Karambhi. The son of Karambhi was Devaräta, and his son was
Devakñatra. The son of Devakñatra was Madhu, and his son was
Kuruvaça, from whom there came a son named Anu.

text: The son of Anu was Puruhotra, the son of Puruhotra was
sanskrit:
Ayu, and the son of Ayu was Sätvata. O great Äryan King, Sätvata had
seven sons, named Bhajamäna, Bhaji, Divya, Våñëi, Devävådha,
Andhaka and Mahäbhoja. From Bhajamäna by one wife came three
sons-Nimloci, Kiìkaëa and Dhåñöi. And from his other wife came
three other sons-Çatäjit, Sahasräjit and Ayutäjit.

text: The son of Devävådha was Babhru. Concerning Devävådha
sanskrit:
and Babhru there are two famous songs of prayer, which were sung by our
predecessors and which we have heard from a distance. Even now I hear
the same prayers about their qualities [because that which was heard
before is still sung continuously].

text: "It has been decided that among human beings Babhru is
sanskrit:
the best and that Devävådha is equal to the demigods. Because of the
association of Babhru and Devävådha, all of their descendants,
numbering 14,065, achieved liberation." In the dynasty of King
Mahäbhoja, who was exceedingly religious, there appeared the Bhoja
kings.

text: O King, Mahäräja Parékñit, who can suppress your
sanskrit:
enemies, the sons of Våñëi were Sumitra and Yudhäjit. From Yudhäjit
came Çini and Anamitra, and from Anamitra came a son named Nighna.

text: The two sons of Nighna were Saträjita and Prasena. Another
sanskrit: son of Anamitra was another Çini, and his son was Satyaka.

text: The son of Satyaka was Yuyudhäna, whose son was Jaya. From
sanskrit:
Jaya came a son named Kuëi and from Kuëi a son named Yugandhara.
Another son of Anamitra was Våñëi.

text: From Våñëi came the sons named Çvaphalka and
sanskrit:
Citraratha. From Çvaphalka by his wife Gändiné came Akrüra. Akrüra
was the eldest, but there were twelve other sons, all of whom were most
celebrated.

text: The names of these twelve were Äsaìga, Särameya,
sanskrit:
Mådura, Måduvit, Giri, Dharmavåddha, Sukarmä, Kñetropekña,
Arimardana, Çatrughna, Gandhamäda and Pratibähu. These brothers also
had a sister named Sucärä. From Akrüra came two sons, named Devavän
and Upadeva. Citraratha had many sons, headed by Påthu and Vidüratha,
all of whom were known as belonging to the dynasty of Våñëi.

text: Kukura, Bhajamäna, Çuci and Kambalabarhiña were the four
sanskrit: sons of Andhaka. The son of Kukura was Vahni, and his son was Vilomä.

text: The son of Vilomä was Kapotaromä, and his son was Anu,
sanskrit:
whose friend was Tumburu. From Anu came Andhaka; from Andhaka, Dundubhi;
and from Dundubhi, Avidyota. From Avidyota came a son named Punarvasu.

text: Punarvasu had a son and a daughter, named Ähuka and
sanskrit:
Ähuké respectively, and Ähuka had two sons, named Devaka and
Ugrasena. Devaka had four sons, named Devavän, Upadeva, Sudeva and
Devavardhana, and he also had seven daughters, named Çäntidevä,
Upadevä, Çrédevä, Devarakñitä, Sahadevä, Devaké and Dhåtadevä.
Dhåtadevä was the eldest. Vasudeva, the father of Kåñëa, married
all these sisters.

text: Kaàsa, Sunämä, Nyagrodha, Kaìka, Çaìku, Suhü,
sanskrit: Räñörapäla, Dhåñöi and Tuñöimän were the sons of Ugrasena.

text: Kaàsä, Kaàsavaté, Kaìkä, Çürabhü and
sanskrit:
Räñörapälikä were the daughters of Ugrasena. They became the wives
of Vasudeva's younger brothers.

text: The son of Citraratha was Vidüratha, the son of Vidüratha
sanskrit:
was Çüra, and his son was Bhajamäna. The son of Bhajamäna was Çini,
the son of Çini was Bhoja, and the son of Bhoja was Hådika.

text: The three sons of Hådika were Devaméòha, Çatadhanu and
sanskrit:
Kåtavarmä. The son of Devaméòha was Çüra, whose wife was named
Märiñä.

text: Through Märiñä, King Çüra begot Vasudeva,
sanskrit:
Devabhäga, Devaçravä, Änaka, Såïjaya, Çyämaka, Kaìka, Çaméka,
Vatsaka and Våka. These ten sons were spotlessly pious personalities.
When Vasudeva was born, the demigods from the heavenly kingdom sounded
kettledrums. Therefore Vasudeva, who provided the proper place for the
appearance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, was also
known as Änakadundubhi. The five daughters of King Çüra, named
Påthä, Çrutadevä, Çrutakérti, Çrutaçravä and Räjädhidevé,
were Vasudeva's sisters. Çüra gave Påthä to his friend Kunti, who
had no issue, and therefore another name of Påthä was Kunté.

text: Once when Durväsä was a guest at the house of Påthä's
sanskrit:
father, Kunti, Påthä satisfied Durväsä by rendering service.
Therefore she received a mystic power by which she could call any
demigod. To examine the potency of this mystic power, the pious Kunté
immediately called for the sun-god.

text: As soon as Kunté called for the demigod of the sun, he
sanskrit:
immediately appeared before her, and she was very much surprised. She
told the sun-god, "I was simply examining the effectiveness of this
mystic power. I am sorry I have called you unnecessarily. Please return
and excuse me."

text: The sun-god said: O beautiful Påthä, your meeting with
sanskrit:
the demigods cannot be fruitless. Therefore, let me place my seed in
your womb so that you may bear a son. I shall arrange to keep your
virginity intact, since you are still an unmarried girl.

text: After saying this, the sun-god discharged his semen into
sanskrit:
the womb of Påthä and then returned to the celestial kingdom.
Immediately thereafter, from Kunté a child was born, who was like a
second sun-god.

text: Because Kunté feared people's criticisms, with great
sanskrit:
difficulty she had to give up her affection for her child. Unwillingly,
she packed the child in a basket and let it float down the waters of the
river. O Mahäräja Parékñit, your great-grandfather the pious and
chivalrous King Päëòu later married Kunté.

text: Våddhaçarmä, the King of Karüña, married Kunté's
sanskrit:
sister Çrutadevä, and from her womb Dantavakra was born. Having been
cursed by the sages headed by Sanaka, Dantavakra had formerly been born
as the son of Diti named Hiraëyäkña.

text: King Dhåñöaketu, the King of Kekaya, married
sanskrit:
Çrutakérti, another sister of Kunté's. Çrutakérti had five sons,
headed by Santardana.

text: Through the womb of Räjädhidevé, another sister of
sanskrit:
Kunté's, Jayasena begot two sons, named Vinda and Anuvinda. Similarly,
the king of the Cedi state married Çrutaçravä. This king's name was
Damaghoña.

text: The son of Çrutaçravä was Çiçupäla, whose birth has
sanskrit:
already been described [in the Seventh Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam].
Vasudeva's brother named Devabhäga had two sons born of his wife,
Kaàsä. These two sons were Citraketu and Båhadbala.

text: Vasudeva's brother named Devaçravä married Kaàsavaté,
sanskrit:
by whom he begot two sons, named Suvéra and Iñumän. Kaìka, by his
wife Kaìkä, begot three sons, named Baka, Satyajit and Purujit.

text: King Såïjaya, by his wife, Räñörapälikä, begot sons
sanskrit:
headed by Våña and Durmarñaëa. King Çyämaka, by his wife,
Çürabhümi, begot two sons, named Harikeça and Hiraëyäkña.

text: Thereafter, King Vatsaka, by the womb of his wife,
sanskrit:
Miçrakeçé, who was an Apsarä, begot sons headed by Våka. Våka, by
his wife, Durväkñé, begot Takña, Puñkara, Çäla and so on.

text: From Çaméka, by the womb of his wife, Sudämané, came
sanskrit:
Sumitra, Arjunapäla and other sons. King Änaka, by his wife,
Karëikä, begot two sons, namely Åtadhämä and Jaya.

text: Devaké, Pauravé, Rohiëé, Bhadrä, Madirä, Rocanä,
sanskrit:
Ilä and others were all wives of Änakadundubhi [Vasudeva]. Among them
all, Devaké was the chief.

text: Vasudeva, by the womb of his wife Rohiëé, begot sons such
sanskrit: as Bala, Gada, Säraëa, Durmada, Vipula, Dhruva, Kåta and others.

text: From the womb of Pauravé came twelve sons, including
sanskrit:
Bhüta, Subhadra, Bhadrabähu, Durmada and Bhadra. Nanda, Upananda,
Kåtaka, Çüra and others were born from the womb of Madirä. Bhadrä
[Kauçalyä] gave birth to only one son, named Keçé.

text: Vasudeva, by another of his wives, whose name was Rocanä,
sanskrit:
begot Hasta, Hemäìgada and other sons. And by his wife named Ilä he
begot sons headed by Uruvalka, all of whom were chief personalities in
the dynasty of Yadu.

text: From the womb of Dhåtadevä, one of the wives of
sanskrit:
Änakadundubhi [Vasudeva], came a son named Vipåñöha. The sons of
Çäntidevä, another wife of Vasudeva, were Praçama, Prasita and
others.

text: Vasudeva also had a wife named Upadevä, from whom came ten
sanskrit:
sons, headed by Räjanya, Kalpa and Varña. From Çrédevä, another
wife, came six sons, such as Vasu, Haàsa and Suvaàça.

text: By the semen of Vasudeva in the womb of Devarakñitä, nine
sanskrit:
sons were born, headed by Gadä. Vasudeva, who was religion personified,
also had a wife named Sahadevä, by whose womb he begot eight sons,
headed by Çruta and Pravara.

text: The eight sons born of Sahadevä such as Pravara and
sanskrit:
Çruta, were exact incarnations of the eight Vasus in the heavenly
planets. Vasudeva also begot eight highly qualified sons through the
womb of Devaké. These included Kértimän, Suñeëa, Bhadrasena, Åju,
Sammardana, Bhadra and Saìkarñaëa, the controller and serpent
incarnation. The eighth son was the Supreme Personality of Godhead
Himself-Kåñëa. The highly fortunate Subhadrä, the one daughter, was
your grandmother.

text: Whenever the principles of religion deteriorate and the
sanskrit:
principles of irreligion increase, the supreme controller, the
Personality of Godhead Çré Hari, appears by His own will.

text: O King, Mahäräja Parékñit, but for the Lord's personal
sanskrit:
desire, there is no cause for His appearance, disappearance or
activities. As the Supersoul, He knows everything. Consequently there is
no cause that affects Him, not even the results of fruitive activities.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead acts through His
sanskrit:
material energy in the creation, maintenance and annihilation of this
cosmic manifestation just to deliver the living entity by His compassion
and stop the living entity's birth, death and duration of materialistic
life. Thus He enables the living being to return home, back to Godhead.

text: Although the demons who take possession of the government
sanskrit:
are dressed like men of government, they do not know the duty of the
government. Consequently, by the arrangement of God, such demons, who
possess great military strength, fight with one another, and thus the
great burden of demons on the surface of the earth is reduced. The
demons increase their military power by the will of the Supreme, so that
their numbers will be diminished and the devotees will have a chance to
advance in Kåñëa consciousness.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, with the
sanskrit:
cooperation of Saìkarñaëa, Balaräma, performed activities beyond the
mental comprehension of even such personalities as Lord Brahmä and Lord
Çiva. [For instance, Kåñëa arranged the Battle of Kurukñetra to
kill many demons for the relief of the entire world.]

text: To show causeless mercy to the devotees who would take
sanskrit:
birth in the future in this age of Kali, the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, Kåñëa, acted in such a way that simply by remembering Him
one will be freed from all the lamentation and unhappiness of material
existence. [In other words, He acted so that all future devotees, by
accepting the instructions of Kåñëa consciousness stated in
Bhagavad-gétä, could be relieved from the pangs of material
existence.]

text: Simply by receiving the glories of the Lord through
sanskrit:
purified transcendental ears, the devotees of the Lord are immediately
freed from strong material desires and engagement in fruitive
activities.

text: Assisted by the descendants of Bhoja, Våñëi, Andhaka,
sanskrit:
Madhu, Çürasena, Daçärha, Kuru, Såïjaya and Päëòu, Lord
Kåñëa performed various activities. By His pleasing smiles, His
affectionate behavior, His instructions and His uncommon pastimes like
raising Govardhana Hill, the Lord, appearing in His transcendental body,
pleased all of human society.

text: Kåñëa's face is decorated with ornaments, such as
sanskrit:
earrings resembling sharks. His ears are beautiful, His cheeks
brilliant, and His smiling attractive to everyone. Whoever sees Lord
Kåñëa sees a festival. His face and body are fully satisfying for
everyone to see, but the devotees are angry at the creator for the
disturbance caused by the momentary blinking of their eyes.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Çré Kåñëa, known
sanskrit:
as lélä-puruñottama, appeared as the son of Vasudeva but immediately
left His father's home and went to Våndävana to expand His loving
relationship with His confidential devotees. In Våndävana the Lord
killed many demons, and afterwards He returned to Dvärakä, where
according to Vedic principles He married many wives who were the best of
women, begot through them hundreds of sons, and performed sacrifices for
His own worship to establish the principles of householder life.

text: Thereafter, Lord Çré Kåñëa created a misunderstanding
sanskrit:
between family members just to diminish the burden of the world. Simply
by His glance, He annihilated all the demoniac kings on the Battlefield
of Kurukñetra and declared victory for Arjuna. Finally, He instructed
Uddhava about transcendental life and devotion and then returned to His
abode in His original form.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: By the womb of the girl brought by
sanskrit:
his father, Vidarbha begot three sons, named Kuça, Kratha and
Romapäda. Romapäda was the favorite in the dynasty of Vidarbha.

text: The son of Romapäda was Babhru, from whom there came a son
sanskrit:
named Kåti. The son of Kåti was Uçika, and the son of Uçika was
Cedi. From Cedi was born the king known as Caidya and others.

text: The son of Kratha was Kunti; the son of Kunti, Våñëi;
sanskrit:
the son of Våñëi, Nirvåti; and the son of Nirvåti, Daçärha. From
Daçärha came Vyoma; from Vyoma came Jémüta; from Jémüta, Vikåti;
from Vikåti, Bhémaratha; from Bhémaratha, Navaratha; and from
Navaratha, Daçaratha.

text: From Daçaratha came a son named Çakuni and from Çakuni a
sanskrit:
son named Karambhi. The son of Karambhi was Devaräta, and his son was
Devakñatra. The son of Devakñatra was Madhu, and his son was
Kuruvaça, from whom there came a son named Anu.

text: The son of Anu was Puruhotra, the son of Puruhotra was
sanskrit:
Ayu, and the son of Ayu was Sätvata. O great Äryan King, Sätvata had
seven sons, named Bhajamäna, Bhaji, Divya, Våñëi, Devävådha,
Andhaka and Mahäbhoja. From Bhajamäna by one wife came three
sons-Nimloci, Kiìkaëa and Dhåñöi. And from his other wife came
three other sons-Çatäjit, Sahasräjit and Ayutäjit.

text: The son of Devävådha was Babhru. Concerning Devävådha
sanskrit:
and Babhru there are two famous songs of prayer, which were sung by our
predecessors and which we have heard from a distance. Even now I hear
the same prayers about their qualities [because that which was heard
before is still sung continuously].

text: "It has been decided that among human beings Babhru is
sanskrit:
the best and that Devävådha is equal to the demigods. Because of the
association of Babhru and Devävådha, all of their descendants,
numbering 14,065, achieved liberation." In the dynasty of King
Mahäbhoja, who was exceedingly religious, there appeared the Bhoja
kings.

text: O King, Mahäräja Parékñit, who can suppress your
sanskrit:
enemies, the sons of Våñëi were Sumitra and Yudhäjit. From Yudhäjit
came Çini and Anamitra, and from Anamitra came a son named Nighna.

text: The two sons of Nighna were Saträjita and Prasena. Another
sanskrit: son of Anamitra was another Çini, and his son was Satyaka.

text: The son of Satyaka was Yuyudhäna, whose son was Jaya. From
sanskrit:
Jaya came a son named Kuëi and from Kuëi a son named Yugandhara.
Another son of Anamitra was Våñëi.

text: From Våñëi came the sons named Çvaphalka and
sanskrit:
Citraratha. From Çvaphalka by his wife Gändiné came Akrüra. Akrüra
was the eldest, but there were twelve other sons, all of whom were most
celebrated.

text: The names of these twelve were Äsaìga, Särameya,
sanskrit:
Mådura, Måduvit, Giri, Dharmavåddha, Sukarmä, Kñetropekña,
Arimardana, Çatrughna, Gandhamäda and Pratibähu. These brothers also
had a sister named Sucärä. From Akrüra came two sons, named Devavän
and Upadeva. Citraratha had many sons, headed by Påthu and Vidüratha,
all of whom were known as belonging to the dynasty of Våñëi.

text: Kukura, Bhajamäna, Çuci and Kambalabarhiña were the four
sanskrit: sons of Andhaka. The son of Kukura was Vahni, and his son was Vilomä.

text: The son of Vilomä was Kapotaromä, and his son was Anu,
sanskrit:
whose friend was Tumburu. From Anu came Andhaka; from Andhaka, Dundubhi;
and from Dundubhi, Avidyota. From Avidyota came a son named Punarvasu.

text: Punarvasu had a son and a daughter, named Ähuka and
sanskrit:
Ähuké respectively, and Ähuka had two sons, named Devaka and
Ugrasena. Devaka had four sons, named Devavän, Upadeva, Sudeva and
Devavardhana, and he also had seven daughters, named Çäntidevä,
Upadevä, Çrédevä, Devarakñitä, Sahadevä, Devaké and Dhåtadevä.
Dhåtadevä was the eldest. Vasudeva, the father of Kåñëa, married
all these sisters.

text: Kaàsa, Sunämä, Nyagrodha, Kaìka, Çaìku, Suhü,
sanskrit: Räñörapäla, Dhåñöi and Tuñöimän were the sons of Ugrasena.

text: Kaàsä, Kaàsavaté, Kaìkä, Çürabhü and
sanskrit:
Räñörapälikä were the daughters of Ugrasena. They became the wives
of Vasudeva's younger brothers.

text: The son of Citraratha was Vidüratha, the son of Vidüratha
sanskrit:
was Çüra, and his son was Bhajamäna. The son of Bhajamäna was Çini,
the son of Çini was Bhoja, and the son of Bhoja was Hådika.

text: The three sons of Hådika were Devaméòha, Çatadhanu and
sanskrit:
Kåtavarmä. The son of Devaméòha was Çüra, whose wife was named
Märiñä.

text: Through Märiñä, King Çüra begot Vasudeva,
sanskrit:
Devabhäga, Devaçravä, Änaka, Såïjaya, Çyämaka, Kaìka, Çaméka,
Vatsaka and Våka. These ten sons were spotlessly pious personalities.
When Vasudeva was born, the demigods from the heavenly kingdom sounded
kettledrums. Therefore Vasudeva, who provided the proper place for the
appearance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, was also
known as Änakadundubhi. The five daughters of King Çüra, named
Påthä, Çrutadevä, Çrutakérti, Çrutaçravä and Räjädhidevé,
were Vasudeva's sisters. Çüra gave Påthä to his friend Kunti, who
had no issue, and therefore another name of Påthä was Kunté.

text: Once when Durväsä was a guest at the house of Påthä's
sanskrit:
father, Kunti, Påthä satisfied Durväsä by rendering service.
Therefore she received a mystic power by which she could call any
demigod. To examine the potency of this mystic power, the pious Kunté
immediately called for the sun-god.

text: As soon as Kunté called for the demigod of the sun, he
sanskrit:
immediately appeared before her, and she was very much surprised. She
told the sun-god, "I was simply examining the effectiveness of this
mystic power. I am sorry I have called you unnecessarily. Please return
and excuse me."

text: The sun-god said: O beautiful Påthä, your meeting with
sanskrit:
the demigods cannot be fruitless. Therefore, let me place my seed in
your womb so that you may bear a son. I shall arrange to keep your
virginity intact, since you are still an unmarried girl.

text: After saying this, the sun-god discharged his semen into
sanskrit:
the womb of Påthä and then returned to the celestial kingdom.
Immediately thereafter, from Kunté a child was born, who was like a
second sun-god.

text: Because Kunté feared people's criticisms, with great
sanskrit:
difficulty she had to give up her affection for her child. Unwillingly,
she packed the child in a basket and let it float down the waters of the
river. O Mahäräja Parékñit, your great-grandfather the pious and
chivalrous King Päëòu later married Kunté.

text: Våddhaçarmä, the King of Karüña, married Kunté's
sanskrit:
sister Çrutadevä, and from her womb Dantavakra was born. Having been
cursed by the sages headed by Sanaka, Dantavakra had formerly been born
as the son of Diti named Hiraëyäkña.

text: King Dhåñöaketu, the King of Kekaya, married
sanskrit:
Çrutakérti, another sister of Kunté's. Çrutakérti had five sons,
headed by Santardana.

text: Through the womb of Räjädhidevé, another sister of
sanskrit:
Kunté's, Jayasena begot two sons, named Vinda and Anuvinda. Similarly,
the king of the Cedi state married Çrutaçravä. This king's name was
Damaghoña.

text: The son of Çrutaçravä was Çiçupäla, whose birth has
sanskrit:
already been described [in the Seventh Canto of Çrémad-Bhägavatam].
Vasudeva's brother named Devabhäga had two sons born of his wife,
Kaàsä. These two sons were Citraketu and Båhadbala.

text: Vasudeva's brother named Devaçravä married Kaàsavaté,
sanskrit:
by whom he begot two sons, named Suvéra and Iñumän. Kaìka, by his
wife Kaìkä, begot three sons, named Baka, Satyajit and Purujit.

text: King Såïjaya, by his wife, Räñörapälikä, begot sons
sanskrit:
headed by Våña and Durmarñaëa. King Çyämaka, by his wife,
Çürabhümi, begot two sons, named Harikeça and Hiraëyäkña.

text: Thereafter, King Vatsaka, by the womb of his wife,
sanskrit:
Miçrakeçé, who was an Apsarä, begot sons headed by Våka. Våka, by
his wife, Durväkñé, begot Takña, Puñkara, Çäla and so on.

text: From Çaméka, by the womb of his wife, Sudämané, came
sanskrit:
Sumitra, Arjunapäla and other sons. King Änaka, by his wife,
Karëikä, begot two sons, namely Åtadhämä and Jaya.

text: Devaké, Pauravé, Rohiëé, Bhadrä, Madirä, Rocanä,
sanskrit:
Ilä and others were all wives of Änakadundubhi [Vasudeva]. Among them
all, Devaké was the chief.

text: Vasudeva, by the womb of his wife Rohiëé, begot sons such
sanskrit: as Bala, Gada, Säraëa, Durmada, Vipula, Dhruva, Kåta and others.

text: From the womb of Pauravé came twelve sons, including
sanskrit:
Bhüta, Subhadra, Bhadrabähu, Durmada and Bhadra. Nanda, Upananda,
Kåtaka, Çüra and others were born from the womb of Madirä. Bhadrä
[Kauçalyä] gave birth to only one son, named Keçé.

text: Vasudeva, by another of his wives, whose name was Rocanä,
sanskrit:
begot Hasta, Hemäìgada and other sons. And by his wife named Ilä he
begot sons headed by Uruvalka, all of whom were chief personalities in
the dynasty of Yadu.

text: From the womb of Dhåtadevä, one of the wives of
sanskrit:
Änakadundubhi [Vasudeva], came a son named Vipåñöha. The sons of
Çäntidevä, another wife of Vasudeva, were Praçama, Prasita and
others.

text: Vasudeva also had a wife named Upadevä, from whom came ten
sanskrit:
sons, headed by Räjanya, Kalpa and Varña. From Çrédevä, another
wife, came six sons, such as Vasu, Haàsa and Suvaàça.

text: By the semen of Vasudeva in the womb of Devarakñitä, nine
sanskrit:
sons were born, headed by Gadä. Vasudeva, who was religion personified,
also had a wife named Sahadevä, by whose womb he begot eight sons,
headed by Çruta and Pravara.

text: The eight sons born of Sahadevä such as Pravara and
sanskrit:
Çruta, were exact incarnations of the eight Vasus in the heavenly
planets. Vasudeva also begot eight highly qualified sons through the
womb of Devaké. These included Kértimän, Suñeëa, Bhadrasena, Åju,
Sammardana, Bhadra and Saìkarñaëa, the controller and serpent
incarnation. The eighth son was the Supreme Personality of Godhead
Himself-Kåñëa. The highly fortunate Subhadrä, the one daughter, was
your grandmother.

text: Whenever the principles of religion deteriorate and the
sanskrit:
principles of irreligion increase, the supreme controller, the
Personality of Godhead Çré Hari, appears by His own will.

text: O King, Mahäräja Parékñit, but for the Lord's personal
sanskrit:
desire, there is no cause for His appearance, disappearance or
activities. As the Supersoul, He knows everything. Consequently there is
no cause that affects Him, not even the results of fruitive activities.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead acts through His
sanskrit:
material energy in the creation, maintenance and annihilation of this
cosmic manifestation just to deliver the living entity by His compassion
and stop the living entity's birth, death and duration of materialistic
life. Thus He enables the living being to return home, back to Godhead.

text: Although the demons who take possession of the government
sanskrit:
are dressed like men of government, they do not know the duty of the
government. Consequently, by the arrangement of God, such demons, who
possess great military strength, fight with one another, and thus the
great burden of demons on the surface of the earth is reduced. The
demons increase their military power by the will of the Supreme, so that
their numbers will be diminished and the devotees will have a chance to
advance in Kåñëa consciousness.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, with the
sanskrit:
cooperation of Saìkarñaëa, Balaräma, performed activities beyond the
mental comprehension of even such personalities as Lord Brahmä and Lord
Çiva. [For instance, Kåñëa arranged the Battle of Kurukñetra to
kill many demons for the relief of the entire world.]

text: To show causeless mercy to the devotees who would take
sanskrit:
birth in the future in this age of Kali, the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, Kåñëa, acted in such a way that simply by remembering Him
one will be freed from all the lamentation and unhappiness of material
existence. [In other words, He acted so that all future devotees, by
accepting the instructions of Kåñëa consciousness stated in
Bhagavad-gétä, could be relieved from the pangs of material
existence.]

text: Simply by receiving the glories of the Lord through
sanskrit:
purified transcendental ears, the devotees of the Lord are immediately
freed from strong material desires and engagement in fruitive
activities.

text: Assisted by the descendants of Bhoja, Våñëi, Andhaka,
sanskrit:
Madhu, Çürasena, Daçärha, Kuru, Såïjaya and Päëòu, Lord
Kåñëa performed various activities. By His pleasing smiles, His
affectionate behavior, His instructions and His uncommon pastimes like
raising Govardhana Hill, the Lord, appearing in His transcendental body,
pleased all of human society.

text: Kåñëa's face is decorated with ornaments, such as
sanskrit:
earrings resembling sharks. His ears are beautiful, His cheeks
brilliant, and His smiling attractive to everyone. Whoever sees Lord
Kåñëa sees a festival. His face and body are fully satisfying for
everyone to see, but the devotees are angry at the creator for the
disturbance caused by the momentary blinking of their eyes.

text: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Çré Kåñëa, known
sanskrit:
as lélä-puruñottama, appeared as the son of Vasudeva but immediately
left His father's home and went to Våndävana to expand His loving
relationship with His confidential devotees. In Våndävana the Lord
killed many demons, and afterwards He returned to Dvärakä, where
according to Vedic principles He married many wives who were the best of
women, begot through them hundreds of sons, and performed sacrifices for
His own worship to establish the principles of householder life.

text: Thereafter, Lord Çré Kåñëa created a misunderstanding
sanskrit:
between family members just to diminish the burden of the world. Simply
by His glance, He annihilated all the demoniac kings on the Battlefield
of Kurukñetra and declared victory for Arjuna. Finally, He instructed
Uddhava about transcendental life and devotion and then returned to His
abode in His original form.

text: Çukadeva Gosvämé said: By the womb of the girl brought by
sanskrit:
his father, Vidarbha begot three sons, named Kuça, Kratha and
Romapäda. Romapäda was the favorite in the dynasty of Vidarbha.

text: The son of Romapäda was Babhru, from whom there came a son
sanskrit:
named Kåti. The son of Kåti was Uçika, and the son of Uçika was
Cedi. From Cedi was born the king known as Caidya and others.

text: The son of Kratha was Kunti; the son of Kunti, Våñëi;
sanskrit:
the son of Våñëi, Nirvåti; and the son of Nirvåti, Daçärha. From
Daçärha came Vyoma; from Vyoma came Jémüta; from Jémüta, Vikåti;
from Vikåti, Bhémaratha; from Bhémaratha, Navaratha; and from
Navaratha, Daçaratha.

text: From Daçaratha came a son named Çakuni and from Çakuni a
sanskrit:
son named Karambhi. The son of Karambhi was Devaräta, and his son was
Devakñatra. The son of Devakñatra was Madhu, and his son was
Kuruvaça, from whom there came a son named Anu.

text: The son of Anu was Puruhotra, the son of Puruhotra was
sanskrit:
Ayu, and the son of Ayu was Sätvata. O great Äryan King, Sätvata had
seven sons, named Bhajamäna, Bhaji, Divya, Våñëi, Devävådha,
Andhaka and Mahäbhoja. From Bhajamäna by one wife came three
sons-Nimloci, Kiìkaëa and Dhåñöi. And from his other wife came
three other sons-Çatäjit, Sahasräjit and Ayutäjit.

text: The son of Devävådha was Babhru. Concerning Devävådha
sanskrit:
and Babhru there are two famous songs of prayer, which were sung by our
predecessors and which we have heard from a distance. Even now I hear
the same prayers about their qualities [because that which was heard
before is still sung continuously].

text: "It has been decided that among human beings Babhru is
sanskrit:
the best and that Devävådha is equal to the demigods. Because of the
association of Babhru and Devävådha, all of their descendants,
numbering 14,065, achieved liberation." In the dynasty of King
Mahäbhoja, who was exceedingly religious, there appeared the Bhoja
kings.

text: O King, Mahäräja Parékñit, who can suppress your
sanskrit:
enemies, the sons of Våñëi were Sumitra and Yudhäjit. From Yudhäjit
came Çini and Anamitra, and from Anamitra came a son named Nighna.

text: The two sons of Nighna were Saträjita and Prasena. Another
sanskrit: son of Anamitra was another Çini, and his son was Satyaka.

text: The son of Satyaka was Yuyudhäna, whose son was Jaya. From
sanskrit:
Jaya came a son named Kuëi and from Kuëi a son named Yugandhara.
Another son of Anamitra was Våñëi.

text: From Våñëi came the sons named Çvaphalka and
sanskrit:
Citraratha. From Çvaphalka by his wife Gändiné came Akrüra. Akrüra
was the eldest, but there were twelve other sons, all of whom were most
celebrated.

text: The names of these twelve were Äsaìga, Särameya,
sanskrit:
Mådura, Måduvit, Giri, Dharmavåddha, Sukarmä, Kñetropekña,
Arimardana, Çatrughna, Gandhamäda and Pratibähu. These brothers also
had a sister named Sucärä. From Akrüra came two sons, named Devavän
and Upadeva. Citraratha had many sons, headed by Påthu and Vidüratha,
all of whom were known as belonging to the dynasty of Våñëi.

text: Kukura, Bhajamäna, Çuci and Kambalabarhiña were the four
sanskrit: sons of Andhaka. The son of Kukura was Vahni, and his son was Vilomä.

text: The son of Vilomä was Kapotaromä, and his son was Anu,
sanskrit:
whose friend was Tumburu. From Anu came Andhaka; from Andhaka, Dundubhi;
and from Dundubhi, Avidyota. From Avidyota came a son named Punarvasu.

text: Punarvasu had a son and a daughter, named Ähuka and
sanskrit:
Ähuké respectively, and Ähuka had two sons, named Devaka and
Ugrasena. Devaka had four sons, named Devavän, Upadeva, Sudeva and
Devavardhana, and he also had seven daughters, named Çäntidevä,
Upadevä, Çrédevä, Devarakñitä, Sahadevä, Devaké and Dhåtadevä.
Dhåtadevä was the eldest. Vasudeva, the father of Kåñëa, married
all these sisters.

text: Kaàsa, Sunämä, Nyagrodha, Kaìka, Çaìku, Suhü,
sanskrit: Räñörapäla, Dhåñöi and Tuñöimän were the sons of Ugrasena.

text: Kaàsä, Kaàsavaté, Kaìkä, Çürabhü and
sanskrit:
Räñörapälikä were the daughters of Ugrasena. They became the wives
of Vasudeva's younger brothers.

text: The son of Citraratha was Vidüratha, the son of Vidüratha
sanskrit:
was Çüra, and his son was Bhajamäna. The son of Bhajamäna was Çini,
the son of Çini was Bhoja, and the son of Bhoja was Hådika.

text: The three sons of Hådika were Devaméòha, Çatadhanu and
sanskrit:
Kåtavarmä. The son of Devaméòha was Çüra, whose wife was named
Märiñä.

text: Through Märiñä, King Çüra begot Vasudeva,
sanskrit:
Devabhäga, Devaçravä, Änaka, Såïjaya, Çyämaka, Kaìka, Çaméka,
Vatsaka and Våka. These ten sons were spotlessly pious personalities.
When Vasudeva was born, the demigods from the heavenly kingdom sounded
kettledrums. Therefore Vasudeva, who provided the proper place for the
appearance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kåñëa, was also
known as Änakadundubhi. The five daughters of King Çüra, named
Påthä, Çrutadevä, Çrutakérti, Çrutaçravä and Räjädhidevé,
were Vasudeva's sisters. Çüra gave Påthä to his friend Kunti, who
had no issue, and therefore another name of Påthä was Kunté.

text: Once when Durväsä was a guest at the house of Påthä's
sanskrit:
father, Kunti, Påthä satisfied Durväsä by rendering service.
Therefore she received a mystic power by which she could call any
demigod. To examine the potency of this mystic power, the pious Kunté
immediately called for the sun-god.

text: As soon as Kunté called for the demigod of the sun, he
sanskrit:
immediately appeared before her, and she was very much surprised. She
told the sun-god, "I was simply examining the effectiveness of this
mystic power. I am sorry I have called you unnecessarily. Please return
and excuse me."

text: The sun-god said: O beautiful Påthä, your meeting with
sanskrit:
the demigods cannot be fruitless. Therefore, let me place my seed in
your womb so that you may bear a son. I shall arrange to keep your
virginity intact, since you are still an unmarried girl.

text: After saying this, the sun-god discharged his semen into
sanskrit:
the womb of Påthä and then returned to the celestial kingdom.
Immediately thereafter, from Kunté a child was born, who was like a
second sun-god.

text: Because Kunté feared people's criticisms, with great
sanskrit:
difficulty she had to give up her affection for her child. Unwillingly,

chivalrous King Päëòu later married Kunté.

sanskrit:
sister Çrutadevä, and from her womb Dantavakra was born. Having been

sanskrit:
Çrutakérti, another sister of Kunté's. Çrutakérti had five sons,

sanskrit:

sanskrit:

sanskrit:
